# Theya — all components

> Generated by scripts/build-spec.mjs from the component sources — do not edit by hand. `@theya/shadcn` v0.1.0.

## Accordion

`import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/accordion';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-accordion--docs

**When to use**

- Several sections people scan by heading and open one or two of: FAQs, settings groups, long details.
- `type="single"` + `collapsible` for FAQs; `multiple` when comparing sections.

**When not to use**

- One show/hide toggle → use Collapsible
- Content everyone needs → use show it — don’t hide the main path
- Switching between parallel views → use Tabs

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: the section heading as a button, chevron on the right.
- Content: animates open; any content.

**Accordion props**

- `type`: `"single" | "multiple"`
- `collapsible?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, AccordionImplSingleProps, AccordionImplMultipleProps, AccordionImplProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, CollapsibleContentProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Questions people scan; they open the one they care about.

  ```tsx
  <Accordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
    {FAQ.map(([q, a]) => (
      <AccordionItem key={q} value={q}><AccordionTrigger>{q}</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>{a}</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    ))}
  </Accordion>
  ```

- Don’t: Required checkout steps hidden in an accordion: people miss the closed ones.

  ```tsx
  <Accordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
    <AccordionItem value="plan"><AccordionTrigger>Choose a plan</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Starter, Pro, Business…</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem value="pay"><AccordionTrigger>Payment details</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Card number, expiry…</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
  </Accordion>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Triggers are buttons inside headings, with aria-expanded; Enter/Space toggles, ↑/↓ move between triggers.
- Keep headings short — they are read as a list of questions.

## Alert

`import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, AlertActions } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/alert';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-alert--docs

**When to use**

- A message about this page or section that stays until it’s resolved.
- A warning before an action, or the summary of errors after submitting a form.

**When not to use**

- A confirmation that something just happened → use Toaster
- A problem with one field → use the field’s own error
- Site-wide news or maintenance → use AnnouncementBar
- A decision that blocks the page → use AlertDialog

**Anatomy**

- Container: `tone`, optional `indicator="stripe"`.
- Icon: the first child; matches the tone.
- Title: what happened.
- Description (optional): what to do about it.
- Actions (optional): `AlertActions`, or buttons under the text.
- Dismiss (optional): `dismissible` — only for messages that can safely go away.

**Alert props**

- `dismissible?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `dismissLabel?`: `string`, default `Dismiss (localized: alert.dismiss)`
- `indicator?`: `"none" | "stripe"`, default `none` — Full-tone accent bar on the left edge. See `AlertIndicator`. Default `'none'`.
- `live?`: `"assertive" | "polite"` — Announce as a live region when mounted dynamically. Omit for static banners.
- `onDismiss?`: `(() => void)`
- `shadow?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Adds `shadow-elevation-sm`. Off by default — an inline banner usually sits flush in
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: What happened, then what to do.

  ```tsx
  <Alert tone="danger" className="w-80">
    <WarningCircle />
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
      <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>Your card was declined. Update it to keep the site online after 12 November.</AlertDescription>
    </div>
  </Alert>
  ```

- Don’t: “Error” alone gives nothing to act on.

  ```tsx
  <Alert tone="danger" className="w-80">
    <WarningCircle />
    <AlertTitle>Error</AlertTitle>
  </Alert>
  ```

- Do: Tone matches how serious it is.

  ```tsx
  <Alert tone="warning" className="w-80">
    <WarningTriangle />
    <AlertTitle>Disk is 92% full</AlertTitle>
  </Alert>
  ```

- Don’t: Danger for news wears out the color for real problems.

  ```tsx
  <Alert tone="danger" className="w-80">
    <WarningCircle />
    <AlertTitle>New: dark theme is here</AlertTitle>
  </Alert>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Appearing after an action? Set `live` (`polite`, or `assertive` for errors) so it’s announced. Static alerts don’t need it.
- The tone is also in words (the title), not only in color and icon.
- For a form error summary, move focus to the alert after submit.

## AlertDialog

`import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogBody, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogPortal, AlertDialogOverlay } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-alertdialog--docs

**When to use**

- Confirming one deliberate, usually destructive or irreversible action before it happens.
- Interrupting is justified: losing data, money or access.

**When not to use**

- Reversible actions → use do it and offer Undo (UndoToast)
- Deletes people should type the name to confirm → use ConfirmDialog
- Forms or anything to read at length → use Dialog

**Anatomy**

- Title: the question with the object: “Delete shop.seashell.dev?”.
- Description: what will happen and what can’t be undone.
- Actions: `AlertDialogCancel` and `AlertDialogAction` labelled with the verb (“Delete site”), danger tone for destructive.

**AlertDialog props**

- `contentGap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `showFooterDivider?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `showHeaderDivider?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `titleSize?`: `"md" | "lg"`, default `md`

**AlertDialogHeader props**

- `gap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `showDivider?`: `boolean`

**AlertDialogFooter props**

- `gap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `showDivider?`: `boolean`

**AlertDialogTitle props**

- `size?`: `"md" | "lg"`

**AlertDialogBody props**

- `showDivider?`: `boolean` — Show the separator line between the body and the footer (dialogs with form/body content).

**AlertDialogAction props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `filled`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `danger`

**AlertDialogCancel props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `outlined`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `secondary`

Also accepts the props of: DialogProps, HTMLAttributes, DialogContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, DialogContentImplProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, DialogPortalProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Open it: the title names the object, the button names the action.

  ```tsx
  <AlertDialog>
    <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
      <Button appearance="outlined" tone="danger" size="md">Delete site</Button>
    </AlertDialogTrigger>
    <AlertDialogContent>
      <AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogTitle>Delete shop.seashell.dev?</AlertDialogTitle>
        <AlertDialogDescription>Its files, databases and 14 backups are removed. This can’t be undone.</AlertDialogDescription>
      </AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogFooter>
        <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
        <AlertDialogAction>Delete site</AlertDialogAction>
      </AlertDialogFooter>
    </AlertDialogContent>
  </AlertDialog>
  ```

- Don’t: “Are you sure? Yes / No” — sure about what, and what does Yes do?

  ```tsx
  <AlertDialog>
    <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
      <Button appearance="outlined" tone="danger" size="md">Delete site</Button>
    </AlertDialogTrigger>
    <AlertDialogContent>
      <AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogTitle>Are you sure?</AlertDialogTitle>
        <AlertDialogDescription>Please confirm.</AlertDialogDescription>
      </AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogFooter>
        <AlertDialogCancel>No</AlertDialogCancel>
        <AlertDialogAction>Yes</AlertDialogAction>
      </AlertDialogFooter>
    </AlertDialogContent>
  </AlertDialog>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s an `alertdialog`: focus starts on Cancel (the safe choice), Escape cancels, focus returns to the trigger.
- Title and description are read when it opens — put the consequence there, not in the button.

## AnimatedIcon

`import { AnimatedIcon } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/animated-icon';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-animatedicon--docs

**When to use**

- A small cue that answers an action: Copy turns into a tick, a menu button folds into ×, a refresh arrow turns.
- A hint on hover for a few key icon buttons (notifications, settings, delete).

**When not to use**

- Every icon on the screen — motion stops meaning anything → use static iconoir icons
- Long loading → use Spinner / Progress
- The only signal of a state change → use a label, toast or aria-live text as well

**Anatomy**

- Icon: iconoir 7.12.1 geometry, 24-unit grid, stroke 1.5, `currentColor`.
- trigger: `hover` (button / link ancestor hovered or focused), `active` (second state), `loop` (busy).

**AnimatedIcon props**

- `name`: `"Check" | "Copy" | "Bell" | "Settings" | "Refresh" | "Trash" | "Eye" | "ArrowRight" | "Download" | "Upload" | "Plus" | "Heart" | "Menu"` — Which icon: Check, Copy, Bell, Settings, Refresh, Trash, Eye, ArrowRight, Download, Upload, Plus, Heart, Menu.
- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**CheckAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**CopyAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**BellAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**SettingsAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**RefreshAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**TrashAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**EyeAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**ArrowRightAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**DownloadAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**UploadAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**PlusAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**HeartAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

**MenuAnimated props**

- `active?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Second state for icons that have one (Copy, Plus, Menu, Eye, Heart).
- `trigger?`: `"loop" | "active" | "hover"`, default `hover` — When the motion plays. Default `hover`.

Also accepts the props of: SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One animated icon on the button it belongs to; it plays on hover and keyboard focus.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="ghost" tone="neutral" iconOnly aria-label="Notifications" leftIcon={<BellAnimated />} />
  ```

- Don’t: Several icons moving on their own: nothing to look at first.

  ```tsx
  <span className="flex gap-2">
    <BellAnimated trigger="loop" />
    <SettingsAnimated trigger="loop" />
    <TrashAnimated trigger="loop" />
  </span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decorative: aria-hidden. Name the button, not the icon (aria-label="Copy").
- prefers-reduced-motion: no motion; active states still switch, instantly.
- Loops only while something is busy (WCAG 2.2.2 — nothing moves for more than 5 s unasked).

## AnnouncementBar

`import { AnnouncementBar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/announcement-bar';`

Status: beta · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-announcementbar--docs

**When to use**

- Something that concerns everyone on every page: planned maintenance, an ongoing incident, a policy change.
- A product announcement worth a strip above the header — rarely, one at a time.

**When not to use**

- A message about one page or section → use Alert
- Feedback on an action just taken → use Toaster
- Something that needs a decision before going on → use AlertDialog

**Anatomy**

- Bar: full width above the app header; `tone` × `appearance` (`filled` / `tonal`), optionally `sticky`.
- Icon (optional): matches the tone; decorative.
- Message: one sentence, one link at most.
- Dismiss (optional): remembered per browser with `dismissKey`; off for incidents.

**AnnouncementBar props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `filled`
- `aria-label?`: `string` — Landmark name. Default "Announcement".
- `dismissible?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `dismissKey?`: `string` — Remember the dismissal in this browser under this key. Change it when the message changes.
- `dismissLabel?`: `string`, default `Dismiss announcement (localized: announcementBar.dismiss)`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Leading 16px icon.
- `onDismiss?`: `(() => void)`
- `sticky?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Stick to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls.
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: What, when, and where to read more — in one line.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96">
    <AnnouncementBar tone="info" appearance="tonal" icon={<InfoCircle />} aria-label="Announcement, maintenance" dismissible={false}>
      Maintenance on Oct 12, 02:00–04:00 UTC. <a href="#">Details</a>
    </AnnouncementBar>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Danger for a promo — and nobody can close it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96">
    <AnnouncementBar tone="danger" icon={<WarningTriangle />} aria-label="Announcement, promo" dismissible={false}>
      New themes are here! Try them now!
    </AnnouncementBar>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: News can be dismissed; change dismissKey when the message changes.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96">
    <AnnouncementBar tone="primary" icon={<Sparks />} aria-label="Announcement, feature">
      Certificates now renew 30 days early. <a href="#">Learn more</a>
    </AnnouncementBar>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Stacked bars push the app down and none of them gets read.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-96 flex-col gap-1">
    <AnnouncementBar tone="primary" aria-label="Announcement 1">New dashboard is live.</AnnouncementBar>
    <AnnouncementBar tone="warning" aria-label="Announcement 2">Billing update on Nov 1.</AnnouncementBar>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A named region landmark, not a live region: it’s there on page load and isn’t announced over what the user is doing.
- Several bars on a page each need a unique `aria-label`.
- Links inside are underlined and inherit the bar’s color.
- After dismiss, focus moves to the next focusable element, not to the page body.

## AreaChart

`import { AreaChart } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/area-chart';`

Status: stable · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-areachart--docs

**When to use**

- One quantity over time where the volume matters: traffic, requests, storage used.
- A few stacked series that add up to a total (`series` + `stacked`).

**When not to use**

- Comparing several trends that don’t add up → use LineChart
- Categories with no order → use BarChart
- A trend inside a row or card → use Sparkline

**Anatomy**

- Area and line: soft gradient fill, 2px line; dots on the peak and latest point.
- Axes and grid: `yStep`, `unit`, `format`; `floatingAxis` for compact cards.
- Tooltip: crosshair with the exact value.
- States: `loading` skeleton; an empty frame for no data.

**AreaChart props**

- `data`: `AreaChartPoint[] | AreaChartMultiPoint[]`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `floatingAxis?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Float axis tick labels inside the plot area on a semi-transparent chip instead of an outside gutter.
- `format?`: `((v: number) => string)`
- `height?`: `number`, default `240`
- `labelPrefix?`: `string`, default ``
- `legend?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `series?`: `AreaChartSeries[]` — Render one area per series (stacked by default) instead of the single `value` field.
- `showXAxis?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `showYAxis?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `stacked?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Stack series on top of each other; false overlays them (only applies with `series`).
- `unit?`: `string`, default ``
- `yStep?`: `number`, default `1` — Gridline interval in data units.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Requests over a week — the shape of the volume is the point.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><AreaChart data={WEEK} unit="k" height={180} ariaLabel="Requests this week, peak 4.8k on Friday." /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Regions joined by a filled line imply a trend between them that doesn’t exist — use a bar chart.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><AreaChart data={REGIONS} unit="%" height={180} ariaLabel="Load by region." /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Always pass `ariaLabel` with the takeaway (“Requests this week, peak 4.8k on Friday”), not “Area chart”.
- Give the key number in text near the chart too; the tooltip is pointer-only.

## AspectRatio

`import { AspectRatio } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/aspect-ratio';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-aspectratio--docs

**When to use**

- Media whose box must keep its shape before it loads: previews, thumbnails, video, maps.
- Grids of cards where images must line up.

**When not to use**

- Text content → use normal layout — text needs to grow
- Images that must be shown whole at their own ratio → use a plain img with width only

**Anatomy**

- Box: `ratio` (16/9 default); clips overflow.
- Child: one fill element (absolute inset-0), usually object-cover, with alt.

**AspectRatio props**

- `ratio?`: `number`, default `16 / 9`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Every preview the same shape; the grid doesn’t jump while images load.

  ```tsx
  <div className="grid w-full grid-cols-2 gap-2">
    {[0, 1].map((i) => (
      <AspectRatio key={i} ratio={16 / 9} className="overflow-hidden rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-md)]">
        <img src={IMG} alt={`Site preview ${i + 1}`} className="absolute inset-0 size-full object-cover" />
      </AspectRatio>
    ))}
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Natural ratios side by side: ragged rows and layout shift on load.

  ```tsx
  <div className="grid w-full grid-cols-2 items-start gap-2">
    <img src={IMG} alt="Site preview 1" className="w-full rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-md)]" />
    <img src="/asset-examples/panda-avatar.png" alt="Site preview 2" className="w-full rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-md)]" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The child image still needs alt (or alt="" if decorative); the box itself adds nothing for screen readers.

## Attachment

`import { Attachment } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/attachment';`

Status: stable · Category: Files
Docs: ./?path=/docs/files-attachment--docs

**When to use**

- Showing a file that’s already attached: in a message, a ticket, a list of uploads.
- Staged files before sending, with `onRemove`; failed ones with `error`.

**When not to use**

- Picking or replacing a file → use File
- Uploading several files by drag and drop → use Dropzone

**Anatomy**

- Kind icon or preview: from `type` (MIME), or `previewUrl` for images.
- Name: truncated in the middle so the extension stays visible.
- Meta (optional): size and kind, or `metaText`; replaced by `error`.
- Remove / actions (optional): `onRemove`, `actions`.
- Variant: `pill` inline, `line` in text, `row` in lists, `card` in grids.

**Attachment props**

- `name`: `string`
- `actions?`: `ReactNode`
- `className?`: `string`
- `clickHint?`: `string` — What a click-only row does, e.g. "Replace file". Shown in place of the
- `error?`: `string`
- `href?`: `string` — Turns the name into a real link, its ::after stretched over the whole surface as the hit target.
- `metaText?`: `ReactNode` — Secondary metadata line, e.g. "Modified today". Overridden by `error` when set.
- `mimeLabels?`: `Record<string, string>`, default `{
  'image/png': 'PNG image',
  'image/jpeg': 'JPEG image',
  'application/pdf': 'PDF',
  'application/zip': 'ZIP archive',
  'text/plain': 'Text file',
  'video/mp4': 'MP4 video',
}`
- `onClick?`: `(() => void)`
- `onRemove?`: `(() => void)`
- `previewUrl?`: `string`
- `removeLabel?`: `string` — Accessible name for the remove button. Default "Remove {name}".
- `selected?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Marks the file as picked — a ring on top of the hover fill, plus `aria-current` on a link.
- `showKind?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `showMeta?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `size?`: `number`
- `type?`: `string`
- `variant?`: `"line" | "row" | "pill" | "card"`, default `pill`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Name, kind and size for each file; the failed one says why, in place.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
    <Attachment variant="row" name="quarterly-report.pdf" type="application/pdf" size={248000} onRemove={() => {}} />
    <Attachment variant="row" name="backup.tar.gz" size={5300000000} error="Exceeds the 2 GB upload limit" onRemove={() => {}} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A bare link and a generic error: which file, how big, and what went wrong?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2 font-body text-body-m">
    <Link href="#gl-att" underline>Download attachment</Link>
    <span className="text-[var(--color-text-text-danger)]">Upload failed</span>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The name is the accessible name; size and kind are read as its description.
- Remove buttons are named per file (“Remove quarterly-report.pdf”); localize with `removeLabel`.
- An error is part of the description, not only red text.

## Autocomplete

`import { Autocomplete } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/autocomplete';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-autocomplete--docs

**When to use**

- Free text where common values are worth suggesting: a hostname, a city, a recent search.
- Any typed value is valid — the suggestions only save typing.

**When not to use**

- The value must be one of the options → use Combobox or Select
- Several values → use Combobox (multiple) or TagInput
- No useful suggestions → use TextField

**Anatomy**

- Input: the value is whatever text is in it.
- Suggestions: filtered as you type; `note` adds a secondary line; `disableFilter` when the server filters.
- Empty / loading (optional): `emptyMessage`, `loading` — the typed text is kept either way.

**Autocomplete props**

- `options`: `AutocompleteOption[]`
- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `contentClassName?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `disableFilter?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Turn off local filtering when the parent supplies already-filtered options (async).
- `emptyMessage?`: `string`, default `No results. (localized: common.noResults)`
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md` — Matches TextField's own heightSize: 'md' (40px, body-m) or 'sm' (32px, body-s) — the dropdown's own text size follows it too.
- `id?`: `string`
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `loadingMessage?`: `string`, default `Loading… (localized: common.loading)`
- `name?`: `string`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `showClear?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Show the clear (x) button when there is text. Defaults to true.
- `value?`: `string`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Suggests common hosts, accepts any other.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-ac-host">SMTP host</Label>
    <Autocomplete id="gl-ac-host" options={HOSTS} placeholder="smtp.example.com" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A fixed set of values in a free-text field: a typo like “Prro” instead of “Pro” is saved as the plan.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-ac-plan">Plan</Label>
    <Autocomplete id="gl-ac-plan" options={[{ value: 'starter', label: 'Starter' }, { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }]} placeholder="Type a plan" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Arrows move through suggestions, Enter fills the input, Escape closes the list and keeps the text.
- Label it with `Label` + `id` or `aria-label`.
- The number of suggestions is announced as they change.

## Avatar

`import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback, AvatarBadge } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/avatar';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-avatar--docs

**When to use**

- Showing who: a person, a team or an account next to their name — in lists, comments, menus.
- Photo when there is one, initials otherwise (`type` image / text / icon).

**When not to use**

- Several people in a small space → use AvatarGroup
- Product or file images → use an image or Attachment

**Anatomy**

- Content: image with `alt`, initials, or an icon; falls back to initials if the image fails.
- Size and shape: `size` sm/md/lg (32/48/64), circle for people, square for teams and orgs.
- Outline (optional): `outline` solid/gradient for emphasis (current user, status).

**Avatar props**

- `alt?`: `string` — `type="image"`: required alt text — announced in place of the photo.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `tonal` — Fill for `AvatarFallback` when using the `type` shorthand (`text`/`icon`/an image's fallback). Independent of `outline`.
- `fallback?`: `ReactNode` — `type="image"`: shown while the image loads or if it fails to load. Falls back to `initials`, then `icon`.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — `type="icon"`: the icon element to show.
- `initials?`: `ReactNode` — `type="text"`: the initials/short text to show.
- `outline?`: `"none" | "solid" | "gradient"`, default `gradient` — Ring around the avatar, drawn as two nested rings per Figma: an outer
- `separator?`: `boolean`, default `true` — The background-color separator ring between the colored `outline` ring
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square"`, default `circle`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `sm`
- `src?`: `string` — `type="image"`: the image source.
- `type?`: `"image" | "text" | "icon"` — Shorthand for Figma's Type variant — renders the matching content

**AvatarFallback props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `tonal`

**AvatarBadge props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "outlined"`, default `filled`
- `children?`: `ReactNode` — Shorthand for `value` — lets `<AvatarBadge>3</AvatarBadge>` keep working.
- `dot?`: `boolean` — Renders a plain dot instead of `value`/`icon` — takes priority over both.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon content (sized by BadgeIndicator, colored via currentColor). Ignored when `dot` is set.
- `pulse?`: `boolean` — Draw attention to something new: two rings spread from the badge, three times, then
- `pulseKey?`: `string | number` — Replays the pulse whenever it changes.
- `separator?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Ring in the surface background color, separating the badge from the
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square"`, default `circle`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `sm`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, default `danger`
- `value?`: `ReactNode`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, AvatarImageProps, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes, AvatarFallbackProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Initials beside the full name — the name carries meaning, the avatar helps scanning.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
    <Avatar type="text" initials="DS" />
    <span className={NAME}>Dana Stoyanova</span>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Initials alone: DS, DM, DK — who is who?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Avatar type="text" initials="DS" />
    <Avatar type="text" initials="DM" />
    <Avatar type="text" initials="DK" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- An image avatar needs `alt` with the person’s name — unless the name is right next to it, then `alt=""`.
- Initials are read letter by letter; give the name in visible text nearby.

## AvatarGroup

`import { AvatarGroup } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/avatar-group';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-avatargroup--docs

**When to use**

- Showing that several people are involved — collaborators, assignees, viewers — when the exact list is secondary.

**When not to use**

- When people need to know exactly who → use a list with names
- One person → use Avatar

**Anatomy**

- Stack: overlapping avatars; `size` forced on every child.
- Overflow (optional): `max` collapses the rest into “+N”.

**AvatarGroup props**

- `max?`: `number` — Max avatars to show before collapsing the rest into a "+N" count.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `sm`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Four faces and “+3”: the size of the team at a glance.

  ```tsx
  <AvatarGroup max={4} aria-label="7 collaborators">{people(['DS', 'MK', 'IP', 'TR', 'AL', 'GB', 'NV'])}</AvatarGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: Every avatar, no max: the stack grows with the team and stops being scannable.

  ```tsx
  <AvatarGroup aria-label="7 collaborators">{people(['DS', 'MK', 'IP', 'TR', 'AL', 'GB', 'NV'])}</AvatarGroup>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name the group with `aria-label`, including the count (“7 collaborators”).
- The “+N” is a count, not a button — if people can see the rest, add a real button or a popover.

## Badge

`import { Badge } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/badge';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-badge--docs

**When to use**

- A short status or label attached to something: “Active”, “Beta”, “Expired”.
- A count next to a name: unread, pending, errors.

**When not to use**

- Something people click, select or remove → use Chip or Button
- A sentence or an explanation → use Alert or plain text
- A dot-only live status in a dense list → use StatusDot

**Anatomy**

- Container: `tone` × `appearance` (`tonal` by default, `filled` for the strongest) × `size`.
- Label: one or two words.

**Badge props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `tonal` — `tonal` (default) — tinted background. `filled` — full tone background, same colors as Chip's solid look.
- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `sm`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Tone follows meaning, and the word says it too.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
    <Badge tone="warning">Expiring</Badge>
    <Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Status colors as decoration teach people that red doesn’t mean anything.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Badge tone="info">Next.js</Badge>
    <Badge tone="danger">Astro</Badge>
    <Badge tone="success">Node.js</Badge>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: One word.

  ```tsx
  <Badge tone="neutral">Beta</Badge>
  ```

- Don’t: A sentence in a pill is hard to read and wraps badly.

  ```tsx
  <Badge tone="neutral">This feature is in beta and may change</Badge>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Never color alone: the label carries the meaning.
- For a bare count, add context for screen readers: `3` + sr-only “unread messages”.
- A badge isn’t focusable; if it does something, it’s a Chip or a Button.

## BadgeIndicator

`import { BadgeIndicator } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/badge-indicator';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-badgeindicator--docs

**When to use**

- A count or a “something new” dot on an icon, avatar or nav item: unread notifications, pending invites.
- A tiny status mark where a Badge with a word doesn’t fit.

**When not to use**

- A status that needs a word (“Active”, “Expired”) → use Badge
- Live status next to a text label in a list → use StatusDot
- A number people need to read precisely → use Stat or plain text

**Anatomy**

- Container: 16 / 20px (`size`), `circle` or `square`, `filled` or `outlined`, `tone`.
- Content: a short `value`, an `icon`, or nothing with `dot`.

**BadgeIndicator props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "outlined"`, default `filled`
- `dot?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Renders a plain dot instead of `value`/`icon` — takes priority over both.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon content (sized by BadgeIndicator, colored via currentColor). Ignored when `dot` is set.
- `pulse?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Draw attention to something new: two rings spread from the badge, three times, then
- `pulseKey?`: `string | number` — Replays the pulse whenever it changes.
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square"`, default `circle`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `sm`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, default `neutral`
- `value?`: `ReactNode` — Qty/text content, e.g. '5' or '99+'. Ignored when `dot` is set; if `icon` is also set, `icon` wins.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Cap long counts (“9+”, “99+”) — the exact number lives in the list.

  ```tsx
  <BellWith value="9+" label="Notifications, more than 9 unread" />
  ```

- Don’t: A four-digit count overflows the badge and says nothing more.

  ```tsx
  <BellWith value="1284" label="Notifications" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The indicator is visual: put its meaning into the name of what it sits on (“Notifications, 3 unread”).
- A `dot` is hidden from screen readers — the parent’s label must say “new” or “unread”.
- Not focusable and not clickable; the icon button under it is the target.
- `pulse` rings three times and stops — under 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2). Use it for something that just arrived, never as a permanent state; it is skipped with reduced motion.

## BarChart

`import { BarChart } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/bar-chart';`

Status: stable · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-barchart--docs

**When to use**

- Comparing a value across categories: load by region, deploys per day, tickets per team.
- `orientation="horizontal"` for a ranked breakdown with long labels.

**When not to use**

- Parts of a whole → use DonutChart (up to 7 parts)
- Continuous time with many points → use AreaChart or LineChart
- Several series per category → use LineChart, or separate charts

**Anatomy**

- Bars: one brand color, rounded caps.
- Value grid: `valueStep`, `unit`, `format`.
- Tooltip: exact value per bar.

**BarChart props**

- `data`: `BarChartPoint[]`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `format?`: `((v: number) => string)`
- `height?`: `number`, default `240`
- `labelPrefix?`: `string`, default ``
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `vertical`
- `unit?`: `string`, default ``
- `valueStep?`: `number`, default `1` — Gridline interval in data units.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Sorted largest first, horizontal so the region names fit.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><BarChart data={REGIONS} orientation="horizontal" unit="%" valueStep={10} height={180} ariaLabel="Load by region, led by eu-west-1 at 42%." /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Unsorted columns: people have to compare heights to find the leader.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><BarChart data={SHUFFLED} unit="%" valueStep={10} height={180} ariaLabel="Load by region." /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `ariaLabel` states the takeaway (“led by eu-west-1 at 42%”).
- One color for one series — color carries no meaning here, so it doesn’t need a legend.

## Breadcrumb

`import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbSeparator, BreadcrumbEllipsis } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/breadcrumb';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-breadcrumb--docs

**When to use**

- Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy of three or more levels, and letting people go up.
- Long trails: collapse the middle with `BreadcrumbEllipsis` (a menu of the hidden levels).

**When not to use**

- Steps of a process → use Stepper
- Flat sites with one or two levels → use the page title alone
- Browsing history (“back”) → use a Back link

**Anatomy**

- Links: `BreadcrumbLink` for each ancestor, in sentence case.
- Separator: hairline chevron.
- Current page: `BreadcrumbPage` — text, not a link.
- Ellipsis (optional): hidden middle levels in a menu.

**BreadcrumbLink props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`

**BreadcrumbPage props**

- `icon?`: `ReactNode`

**BreadcrumbEllipsis props**

- `items?`: `{ label: string; href: string; }[]` — The levels the ellipsis stands for, top first. With them, the ellipsis

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, OlHTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Ancestors are links; the current page is plain text at the end.

  ```tsx
  <Breadcrumb aria-label="Breadcrumb example">
    <BreadcrumbList>
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#gl-bc">Sites</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#gl-bc">shop.seashell.dev</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Backups</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
    </BreadcrumbList>
  </Breadcrumb>
  ```

- Don’t: Wizard steps as a breadcrumb: they’re a sequence, not a hierarchy — use Stepper.

  ```tsx
  <Breadcrumb aria-label="Wizard as breadcrumb">
    <BreadcrumbList>
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#gl-bc">Account</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#gl-bc">Plan</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Payment</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
    </BreadcrumbList>
  </Breadcrumb>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a `nav` named “Breadcrumb”; the current page has `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators are hidden from screen readers.
- The ellipsis is a button named “Show N more levels”.

## Button

`import { Button } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/button';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-button--docs

**When to use**

- To do something: save, submit, create, delete, start a flow, open a dialog.
- One `filled` primary action per area; secondary actions `outlined` or `ghost` next to it.
- Inside cards and toolbars at `md`; page-level actions at the default `xl`.

**When not to use**

- Going to another page or section → use a link, or Button asChild around an <a>
- Switching a setting on or off → use Switch
- Choosing one of a few options → use ToggleGroup or RadioGroup
- Several related actions that don’t fit side by side → use SplitButton or DropdownMenu

**Anatomy**

- Container: appearance (`filled`, `tonal`, `outlined`, `ghost`) × tone × size.
- Label: a verb, sentence case: “Save changes”, “Delete domain”.
- Left icon (optional): via `leftIcon`; replaced by the Spinner while `loading`, and by a tick that draws itself while `success`.
- Right icon (optional): via `rightIcon` — for direction (→) or a menu (⌄).
- Badge (optional): via `badge` — a count (`{5}`, `"9+"`) or `{ dot: true }` pinned to the top-right corner; danger by default.

**Button props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `filled`
- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`, default `false`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`, default `xl`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean`, default `false` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One primary action; the alternative is quieter.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Cancel</Button>
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Save changes</Button>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two filled buttons compete — people can’t tell which one moves them forward.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Cancel</Button>
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Save changes</Button>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: The label says what happens.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="filled" tone="danger" size="md" leftIcon={<Trash />}>Delete domain</Button>
  ```

- Don’t: “OK”, “Yes”, “Submit” make people re-read the question to know what they’re agreeing to.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="filled" tone="danger" size="md">OK</Button>
  ```

- Do: `softDisabled` with the reason next to it — still focusable, and it says what’s missing.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-1.5">
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md" softDisabled aria-describedby="gl-btn-why">Publish</Button>
    <span id="gl-btn-why" className="font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">Add a title to publish.</span>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A disabled button with no reason leaves people guessing, and keyboard users can’t reach it at all.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md" disabled>Publish</Button>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `iconOnly` buttons need `aria-label` — a dev warning fires without it.
- `loading` keeps the width and the label (the spinner replaces the icon), so nothing jumps and the name stays the same.
- Prefer `softDisabled` + `aria-describedby` over `disabled` when the reason matters.
- A `badge` is aria-hidden — pass `badgeLabel` (“5 unread”) so the count is read with the button name; a dev warning fires without it.
- The focus ring (4px) takes the button’s tone; never remove it.
- Don’t nest a button inside a link or another button.

## Calendar

`import { Calendar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/calendar';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-calendar--docs

**When to use**

- The calendar is the content: picking a booking day, showing availability, choosing several days.
- Inside your own popover or panel; `mode` single, multiple or range.

**When not to use**

- A date field in a form → use DatePicker
- A range field in a form → use DateRangePicker

**Anatomy**

- Caption and nav: month name with arrows, or month/year dropdowns (`captionLayout="dropdown"`).
- Grid: weekdays, then days; today is marked, outside days are dimmed.
- Day states: selected, range start/middle/end, `disabled` via matchers.

Also accepts the props of: PropsBase, PropsSingle, PropsSingleRequired, PropsMulti, PropsMultiRequired, PropsRange, PropsRangeRequired.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Choosing the day is the main task here, so the month stays open; weekends are off.

  ```tsx
  <Calendar mode="single" disabled={{ dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }} aria-label="Delivery day" labels={{ labelNav: () => 'Delivery day months' }} />
  ```

- Don’t: A full calendar for one form field takes the whole form — use a DatePicker.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
    <TextField label="Project name" defaultValue="Spring launch" widthSize="md" />
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <span id="gl-cal-due" className="font-body text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
        Due date
      </span>
      <Calendar mode="single" aria-labelledby="gl-cal-due" labels={{ labelNav: () => 'Due date months' }} />
    </div>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Arrows move by day, Page Up/Down by month, Home/End to week start/end; Enter selects.
- Give it a name (`aria-label`) when no heading says what the dates are for.
- Two calendars on one page: name each one’s month navigation (`labels={{ labelNav }}`) so the landmarks differ.
- Explain disabled days in text — a grayed-out day says nothing about why.

## Card

`import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardLink, CardContent, CardAction, CardFooter, CardMedia, CardAvatar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/card';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-card--docs

**When to use**

- A self-contained unit people scan and compare: an item in a grid, the summary of one object, a settings section.
- A whole-card link or filter via `action`.

**When not to use**

- Only to draw a border around a page section — use space and a heading
- A message about the page → use Alert
- Inside another card — use a divider or a list instead of nesting

**Anatomy**

- Container: `size` (padding) and `tone` (tinted border for a status).
- Header (optional): `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction` on the right.
- Content: the body.
- Footer (optional): actions — `md` buttons.

**Card props**

- `action?`: `CardPrimaryAction` — Primary action for the whole card. Providing one makes the card interactive automatically.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "outlined"`, default `outlined` — `outlined` (default) surface card, or `filled` brand card on the primary color.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Dims the card, blocks pointer events, and disables `action`/`selectable`.
- `effect?`: `"tilt" | "spotlight" | "lift"` — Pointer effect, mouse only (touch and keyboard see the plain card):
- `href?`: `string` — Convenience shorthand for `action={{ type: 'link', href }}`. `action` takes precedence when both are set.
- `interactive?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `onSelectedChange?`: `((selected: boolean) => void)`
- `selectable?`: `"checkbox" | "radio"` — Renders a Radio or Checkbox pinned to the card's top-left corner and
- `selected?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `selectLabel?`: `string` — Accessible name for the selection control. Required when `selectable` is set.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, default `neutral` — Status tone: tinted border/surface and matching hover/focus colors. Default `neutral` (untinted).

**CardHeader props**

- `divider?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`

**CardLink props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false`

**CardMedia props**

- `height?`: `string | number`, default `180` — Banner height. Defaults to 180px (on the 4px grid).

**CardAvatar props**

- `alt?`: `string` — `type="image"`: required alt text — announced in place of the photo.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"` — Fill for `AvatarFallback` when using the `type` shorthand (`text`/`icon`/an image's fallback). Independent of `outline`.
- `fallback?`: `ReactNode` — `type="image"`: shown while the image loads or if it fails to load. Falls back to `initials`, then `icon`.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — `type="icon"`: the icon element to show.
- `initials?`: `ReactNode` — `type="text"`: the initials/short text to show.
- `outline?`: `"none" | "solid" | "gradient"`, default `solid` — Ring around the avatar, drawn as two nested rings per Figma: an outer
- `separator?`: `boolean` — The background-color separator ring between the colored `outline` ring
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square"`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `lg`
- `src?`: `string` — `type="image"`: the image source.
- `type?`: `"image" | "text" | "icon"` — Shorthand for Figma's Type variant — renders the matching content

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The whole card is the link (`action`) — one target, the biggest one.

  ```tsx
  <Card action={{ type: 'link', href: '#seashell', ariaLabel: 'seashell.shop' }} className="w-64">
    <CardHeader divider={false}>
      <CardTitle>seashell.shop</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Active · 3 mailboxes</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
  </Card>
  ```

- Don’t: A “View” button as the only way in makes people aim for a small target inside a big one.

  ```tsx
  <Card className="w-64">
    <CardHeader divider={false}>
      <CardTitle>seashell.shop</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Active · 3 mailboxes</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
    <CardContent className="pt-0">
      <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">View</Button>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
  ```

- Do: Buttons inside cards are `md`.

  ```tsx
  <Card className="w-64">
    <CardHeader divider={false}>
      <CardTitle>Backups</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Last run 2 hours ago</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
    <CardContent className="flex gap-2 pt-0">
      <Button size="md">Run now</Button>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
  ```

- Don’t: Page-size buttons overpower the card they sit in.

  ```tsx
  <Card className="w-64">
    <CardHeader divider={false}>
      <CardTitle>Backups</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Last run 2 hours ago</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
    <CardContent className="flex gap-2 pt-0">
      <Button>Run now</Button>
      <Badge tone="success">OK</Badge>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- With `action`, give an `ariaLabel` that matches the card’s title — that’s the link’s name.
- Interactive children (checkbox, menu) sit above the stretched link and stay usable.
- A toned card (`tone` other than `neutral`) states its status in text too; the tint alone isn’t enough.
- `effect` (tilt, spotlight, lift) reacts to the mouse only and is decoration: touch and keyboard users get the plain card, and prefers-reduced-motion turns tilt and lift off. Use it on showcase cards, not in dense product lists.

## CardFan

`import { CardFan } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/card-fan';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-cardfan--docs

**When to use**

- A playful group of 3–5 cards in a hero or an about page: team members, plans, product shots.

**When not to use**

- More than five cards, or cards people compare → use Card grid
- Navigation or settings → use Tabs / List

**Anatomy**

- Stack: cards on top of each other, slightly rotated.
- Fan: on hover or focus the cards spread by `offset` px and `spread`°, one after another.
- Active card: the one under the pointer or focus lifts 16px and comes to the front.

**CardFan props**

- `offset?`: `number`, default `88` — Horizontal distance between neighbouring cards when open, px (default 88). Tightened automatically when the container is too narrow for it.
- `spread?`: `number`, default `8` — Rotation between neighbouring cards when open, degrees (default 8).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The fan reads as one group.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>3–5 cards of the same size</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: Cards cover each other even when open.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>10 cards of mixed size</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Every card stays in the tab order and the accessibility tree; the fan only changes the layout.
- Keyboard focus opens the fan and lifts the focused card, so focus is never hidden behind another card.
- On touch, a tap opens the fan. prefers-reduced-motion: the fan opens without animation.

## CardStack

`import { CardStack } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/card-stack';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-cardstack--docs

**When to use**

- A landing or empty-state showcase that cycles a few cards: testimonials, highlights, recent invoices.

**When not to use**

- Content the user has to read or act on → use Card grid / List
- Browsing many items by hand → use Carousel

**Anatomy**

- Deck: the front card plus `depth` cards behind it, each 12px higher and 5% smaller.
- Cycle: every `interval` ms the front card drops away and returns to the back.
- Controls: Pause / Play and Next, under the deck.

**CardStack props**

- `depth?`: `number`, default `2` — Cards visible behind the front one (default 2).
- `hideControls?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Hide the Pause / Next controls — only when the page has another way to stop it.
- `interval?`: `number`, default `4000` — Time each card stays in front, ms (default 4000).
- `layout?`: `"stack" | "fan"`, default `stack` — `stack`: cards behind sit higher and smaller. `fan`: they spread to the side like a hand of cards.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Few short cards; time to read each one.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>3–6 short cards, 4 s each</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: Interactive content that leaves while someone is using it.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>A form inside a cycling card</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Pauses on hover and while anything inside has focus; Pause / Play stops it for good (WCAG 2.2.2).
- Only the front card is in the accessibility tree; the rest are aria-hidden and inert.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no timer and no animation, the cards change only with Next.

## Carousel

`import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselIndicators, CarouselNext } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/carousel';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-carousel--docs

**When to use**

- Browsing a set of similar, optional items one or a few at a time: templates, screenshots, product photos.

**When not to use**

- Key messages or anything people must see → use show it on the page — later slides are rarely seen
- A few items that fit → use a grid

**Anatomy**

- Track: drag/swipe; `orientation`, `opts` (align, loop).
- Items: “2 of 6” as each slide’s name.
- Controls: `CarouselPrevious`/`CarouselNext`, optional indicators.

**Carousel props**

- `opts?`: `Partial<OptionsType>`
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `horizontal`
- `peek?`: `boolean`, default `false` — The current slide sits in the middle, its neighbours peek in from the
- `plugins?`: `CreatePluginType<LoosePluginType, {}>[]`
- `setApi?`: `((api: EmblaCarouselType) => void)`

**CarouselPrevious props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`

**CarouselIndicators props**

- `variant?`: `"default" | "on-dark"`, default `default` — `on-dark` uses white/translucent-white dots for an image or video background; `default` uses the standard surface tokens.

**CarouselNext props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Templates to browse — optional, alike, and many.

  ```tsx
  <Slides label="Site templates" items={['Blog', 'Shop', 'Portfolio', 'Docs', 'Landing', 'Wiki']} />
  ```

- Don’t: Important notices in slides: most people never see slide 2 or 3.

  ```tsx
  <Slides label="Announcements" items={['Price change on May 1', 'Planned downtime Sat', 'New region: Mumbai']} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A named region (`aria-label`) with role description “carousel”; each item says its position.
- Arrow keys move between slides; Previous/Next are named buttons. No autoplay — or a pause button if you must.

## ChartRangeSelection

`import { ChartRangeSelection } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/chart-range-selection';`

Status: beta · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-chartrangeselection--docs

**When to use**

- Selecting a span on an ordered x-axis to zoom in or filter: “show errors from Aug 3 to Aug 6”.

**When not to use**

- Unordered categories (regions, teams) → use Filter or a legend toggle
- Picking dates precisely → use DateRangePicker

**Anatomy**

- Wrapper: focusable; draws the selection band over the chart.
- Child chart: a categorical Recharts chart whose x-axis matches labels.
- Result: `onRangeChange` → show the selected span in text and offer to clear it.

**ChartRangeSelection props**

- `children`: `ReactElement<SelectableChartProps, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>` — A categorical Recharts chart (AreaChart, LineChart, BarChart, ComposedChart). Pass it without a ResponsiveContainer — this provides one.
- `labels`: `readonly (string | number)[]` — X-axis values in the same order as the wrapped chart's data.
- `aria-label?`: `string` — Accessible name of the selector. Default "Select a range".
- `className?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Disable drag selection while continuing to display selectedRange.
- `height?`: `number`, default `240`
- `onRangeChange?`: `((range: ChartSelectionRange | null) => void)`
- `selectedRange?`: `ChartSelectionRange | null` — Controlled selection. Omit to use internal state.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: An ordered time axis; the selected span is written out under the chart.

  ```tsx
  <TimeRange />
  ```

- Don’t: A “range” of regions means nothing — there’s no order between them.

  ```tsx
  <CategoryRange />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- ←/→ move a cursor over the x-axis, Shift+←/→ extend a selection, Home/End jump, Esc clears (WCAG 2.1.1).
- Cursor moves and selections are announced in a live region.

## Chat

`import { Chat, ChatMessages, ChatTyping } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/chat';`

Status: beta · Category: AI & Chat
Docs: ./?path=/docs/ai-chat-chat--docs

**When to use**

- A conversation surface: an AI assistant, support chat, comments thread in real time.
- Transcript that scrolls with the composer pinned below.

**When not to use**

- A one-off question and answer → use a form and a result
- Threaded comments on an object → use a comments list

**Anatomy**

- Chat: flex column; give it a height so only the transcript scrolls.
- ChatMessages: `role="log"`, newest last; Messages inside.
- Composer: usually a PromptArea, pinned at the bottom; HoldToTalk fits its trailing slot.
- ChatTyping (optional): three bouncing dots, last in the log while the other side writes.

**ChatTyping props**

- `avatar?`: `ReactNode`
- `label?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A fixed height: the transcript scrolls, the composer stays in reach.

  ```tsx
  <div className={BOX}>
    <Chat className="h-full">
      <ChatMessages aria-label="Conversation example">
        <Message author="Assistant">Your SSL certificate renews in 5 days.</Message>
        <Message variant="sent" author="You">Renew it now.</Message>
      </ChatMessages>
      <PromptArea aria-label="Message the assistant" placeholder="Ask anything…" />
    </Chat>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Composer on top, newest message first: it reads backwards and isn’t announced as a log.

  ```tsx
  <div className={BOX}>
    <div className="flex h-full flex-col gap-2 overflow-auto p-3">
      <PromptArea aria-label="Message, composer on top" placeholder="Ask anything…" />
      <Message variant="sent" author="You">Renew it now.</Message>
      <Message author="Assistant">Your SSL certificate renews in 5 days.</Message>
    </div>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Keep the newest message last in the DOM — `role="log"` announces additions at the end.
- Name the transcript (“Conversation with Assistant”) when there are several on a page.

## Checkbox

`import { Checkbox } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/checkbox';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-checkbox--docs

**When to use**

- Independent yes/no choices that apply when the form is saved.
- Choosing several items from a list, and selecting rows for bulk actions.

**When not to use**

- A setting that takes effect immediately → use Switch
- Exactly one of several options → use RadioGroup
- Many options people search through → use Combobox or TagInput

**Anatomy**

- Box: checked, unchecked or `indeterminate` (some children selected).
- Label: clickable, says what “on” means.
- Description (optional): a line under the label for consequences.
- Group legend (optional): for several related boxes — `CheckboxGroup` wraps them in a fieldset.

**Checkbox props**

- `checked?`: `boolean | "indeterminate"` — Controlled checked state. Accepts a plain boolean, or 'indeterminate' directly.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Small helper text below the label — only rendered when `label` is set.
- `error?`: `boolean | null`, default `false`
- `indeterminate?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Convenience for checked="indeterminate" — shows a dash instead of a checkmark.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` — Label shown next to the box. Omit for a bare checkbox with no text.
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm" | null`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, CheckboxProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Worded positively: checked means yes.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Checkbox id="gl-cb-news" />
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cb-news">Send me product news</Label>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A negative label turns “checked” into a double negative.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Checkbox id="gl-cb-news2" />
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cb-news2">Don’t send me product news</Label>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: Takes effect at once (no Save) — a switch.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Switch id="gl-cb-sw" defaultChecked />
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cb-sw">Email alerts</Label>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A checkbox that applies instantly surprises people who expect a Save.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Checkbox id="gl-cb-alerts" defaultChecked />
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cb-alerts">Email alerts</Label>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Every box needs a label — a `Label` with `htmlFor`, or `aria-label` in a table row (“Select seashell.shop”).
- Indeterminate is announced as “mixed”; use it only for a parent of partly selected children.
- Group related boxes in `CheckboxGroup` so the legend is read with each option.
- Space toggles; the whole label is a click target.

## CheckboxGroup

`import { CheckboxGroup, CheckboxGroupItem } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/checkbox-group';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-checkboxgroup--docs

**When to use**

- Several related yes/no choices that form one value (“Notify me by: Email, SMS”).
- Up to about 8 options people should see at once.

**When not to use**

- Exactly one option → use RadioGroup
- Long or searchable lists → use Combobox (multiple)
- Unrelated settings that only share a page → use separate Checkbox or Switch

**Anatomy**

- Legend: `label` — rendered as the fieldset legend.
- Items: `CheckboxGroupItem`; its `name` is what lands in the value array.
- Size: `size` sm/md flows to every item and sets the gap.

**CheckboxGroup props**

- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string[]` — Uncontrolled initial checked set.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` — Disables every child Checkbox at once.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` — Group label — rendered as a <legend> via the native fieldset.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string[]) => void)`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md` — Checkbox size for every item, unless an item overrides its own. Defaults to "md".
- `value?`: `string[]` — Controlled checked set (pair with onValueChange).

**CheckboxGroupItem props**

- `name`: `string`
- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Small helper text below the label — only rendered when `label` is set.
- `error?`: `boolean | null`
- `indeterminate?`: `boolean` — Convenience for checked="indeterminate" — shows a dash instead of a checkmark.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` — Label shown next to the box. Omit for a bare checkbox with no text.
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm" | null`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, CheckboxProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One legend, one value; the question is asked once.

  ```tsx
  <CheckboxGroup label="Notify me by" defaultValue={['email']}>
    <CheckboxGroupItem name="email" label="Email" />
    <CheckboxGroupItem name="sms" label="SMS" />
    <CheckboxGroupItem name="push" label="Push notifications" />
  </CheckboxGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: Loose boxes repeat the question in every label and lose the group name for screen readers.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Notify me by email" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox label="Notify me by SMS" />
    <Checkbox label="Notify me by push" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The legend is read with each option — keep it short and question-like.
- Each item is its own tab stop; Space toggles.
- An error for the whole group goes under the group and is linked with `aria-describedby`, not on one box.

## Chip

`import { Chip, ChipRemove } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/chip';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-chip--docs

**When to use**

- Selectable or removable values: quick filters (“Critical”, “Mine”), selected tags, suggestions.

**When not to use**

- A read-only status or count → use Badge
- Choosing one of several views → use ToggleGroup or Tabs
- Actions → use Button

**Anatomy**

- Pill: a real button stretched over it; `pressed` / `onPressedChange`.
- Icon (optional): leading.
- Remove (optional): `ChipRemove` — a sibling button, not nested.
- Look: `tone`, `appearance` tonal/filled, `size` sm/md/lg.

**Chip props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `tonal` — `'tonal'` (default) — tinted background, matches Badge's default look. `'filled'` — full tone background + on-dark text.
- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `bordered?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Adds a tone-colored border on top of `appearance`. Off by default — every tone (including neutral) is borderless at rest.
- `defaultPressed?`: `boolean`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Leading icon, before the label. Unstyled — sized automatically to the chip's size variant. Replaced by a checkmark when a `appearance="filled"` chip is selected (see `pressed`/`defaultPressed`).
- `interactive?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `onClick?`: `MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement>`
- `onKeyDown?`: `KeyboardEventHandler<HTMLElement>`
- `onPressedChange?`: `((pressed: boolean) => void)`
- `pressed?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `toggleable?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Interactive chips toggle (aria-pressed) by default. Pass false for a chip that performs an action instead, e.g. opens an editor — it is then a plain button with no pressed state.
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Quick filters people toggle on and off.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Chip defaultPressed>Critical</Chip>
    <Chip>Mine</Chip>
    <Chip>Unassigned</Chip>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A status that can’t be clicked styled as a chip — use a Badge.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2 font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
    shop.seashell.dev
    <Chip tone="success" interactive={false}>Running</Chip>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: Read-only state is a Badge.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2 font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
    shop.seashell.dev
    <Badge tone="success">Running</Badge>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Chips for an either-or view: both end up selected — use ToggleGroup.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Chip defaultPressed>List</Chip>
    <Chip defaultPressed>Grid</Chip>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Toggle chips are buttons with `aria-pressed`; Space/Enter toggles.
- Remove buttons are named per chip (“Remove Critical”).
- For selection that must read without color, use `appearance="filled"` — selected filled chips also show a check.

## CodeBlock

`import { CodeBlock } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/code-block';`

Status: stable · Category: Code
Docs: ./?path=/docs/code-codeblock--docs

**When to use**

- A command, snippet or config the user reads and copies: install steps, a DNS record, an API example.
- Generated output shown as-is, where exact characters matter.

**When not to use**

- The user edits the code → use CodeEditor
- A streaming log or console output → use Terminal
- Showing what changed between two versions → use DiffViewer
- One short token inside a sentence (a path, a flag) → use inline <code> or Kbd for keys
- A single secret or value to copy, like an API key → use TextField read-only with CopyButton

**Anatomy**

- Header (optional): filename or language label; appears only with `filename` / `language`.
- Code: mono, keeps whitespace, scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping.
- Copy button (optional): copies the exact `code` string; in the header, or floating top-right without one.

**CodeBlock props**

- `code`: `string`
- `copy?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `copyLabel?`: `string`, default `Copy code (localized: codeBlock.copy)`
- `filename?`: `string` — Filename shown mono in the header (takes visual priority over `language`).
- `language?`: `string` — Language hint shown as a muted label in the header (no highlighting applied).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Only the command — Copy gives exactly what to paste.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><CodeBlock language="bash" code="npm run cache:clear" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A prompt sign and sample output get copied along and break the paste.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><CodeBlock language="bash" code={'$ npm run cache:clear\nCache cleared.'} /></div>
  ```

- Do: Multi-line config in a block with its filename.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><CodeBlock filename="nginx.conf" code={'location /static/ {\n  expires 30d;\n}'} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Code squeezed into a text field loses line breaks and indentation.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="nginx.conf" defaultValue="location /static/ { expires 30d; }" widthSize="lg" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The code area is a tab stop, so long lines can be scrolled with the keyboard.
- The copy button is named (`copyLabel`) and confirms with a tooltip; name it after the content when there are several blocks (“Copy install command”).
- Introduce the block with text — what it is and where to run it; the code itself is not a description.

## CodeEditor

`import { CodeEditor } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/code-editor';`

Status: beta · Category: Code
Docs: ./?path=/docs/code-codeeditor--docs

**When to use**

- Editing config, templates, rules or scripts in the product: JSON, HTML, CSS, JS/TS, shell.
- Long code shown read-only where line numbers and selection help (`readOnly`).

**When not to use**

- A short snippet to read and copy → use CodeBlock
- Prose with formatting → use RichTextEditor
- Plain multi-line text → use TextArea
- Comparing versions → use DiffViewer

**Anatomy**

- Header (optional): filename / language, with Copy and Clear on the right (`copy`, `clearable`).
- Gutter: line numbers.
- Editing area: syntax color from `language`; grows between `minHeight` and `maxHeight`, then scrolls.

**CodeEditor props**

- `clearable?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `clearLabel?`: `string`, default `Clear (localized: common.clear)`
- `copy?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `copyLabel?`: `string`, default `Copy code (localized: codeBlock.copy)`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `extensions?`: `Extension[]`, default `[]` — Extra CodeMirror extensions, added alongside whatever `language` auto-resolves (if anything).
- `filename?`: `string`
- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Forces the code area (not the header) onto a fixed dark surface (Luna Pro Midnight) regardless of the page's own theme.
- `language?`: `string` — Also auto-selects syntax coloring when it matches a known grammar: json, html, css, javascript/js/jsx, typescript/ts/tsx, bash/shell/sh. Unrecognized values still just show as a header label.
- `maxHeight?`: `string`
- `minHeight?`: `string`, default `8rem`
- `onChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `value?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Language set — brackets, indentation and color help avoid syntax errors.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><CodeEditor aria-label="Redirect rules" filename="redirects.json" language="json" defaultValue={'{\n  "/old": "/new"\n}'} minHeight="5rem" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A plain textarea for JSON: no line numbers, Tab leaves the field.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><TextArea aria-label="Redirect rules" defaultValue={'{\n  "/old": "/new"\n}'} rows={3} /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**
