- Always give an `aria-label` (or a visible label referenced by it) — it names the editing area.
- Tab indents inside the editor. To leave with the keyboard press Esc, then Tab — say so near editors in forms.
- Validate on save and point to the line in the error message; color alone doesn’t mark a syntax error.
- Copy and Clear buttons are named (`copyLabel`, `clearLabel`).

## Collapsible

`import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/collapsible';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-collapsible--docs

**When to use**

- One optional region people expand on demand: “Advanced settings”, “Show 12 more”, technical details.

**When not to use**

- Several related sections → use Accordion
- Required fields → use show them

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: a button whose label says what opens (“Advanced settings”); chevron turns.
- Content: `CollapsibleContent`, animated height.

Also accepts the props of: CollapsibleProps, HTMLAttributes, CollapsibleContentProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Optional, rarely used settings, one click away.

  ```tsx
  <Collapsible className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-3">
    <CollapsibleTrigger asChild>
      <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md" rightIcon={<NavArrowDown />} className="self-start">Advanced settings</Button>
    </CollapsibleTrigger>
    <CollapsibleContent>
      <TextField label="Custom build flags" optional widthSize="full" />
    </CollapsibleContent>
  </Collapsible>
  ```

- Don’t: “More” hiding a required field: vague label, and the form fails on a field nobody saw.

  ```tsx
  <Collapsible className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-3">
    <CollapsibleTrigger asChild>
      <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md" rightIcon={<NavArrowDown />} className="self-start">More</Button>
    </CollapsibleTrigger>
    <CollapsibleContent>
      <TextField label="Admin email" required widthSize="full" />
    </CollapsibleContent>
  </Collapsible>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Its label names the content, not just “More”/“Show”.

## ColorPicker

`import { ColorPicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/color-picker';`

Status: beta · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-colorpicker--docs

**When to use**

- Any color, including custom: brand and theme colors, chart series, white-label setup.
- `ColorField` in forms — a text field with a swatch that opens the picker.

**When not to use**

- A fixed set of colors → use SwatchPicker
- Product variants → use SwatchPicker

**Anatomy**

- Tabs: Palette, From photo, Custom — choose with `views`.
- Area and sliders: saturation/brightness, hue, and opacity with `alpha`.
- Input row: format (HEX/RGB/HSL via `formats`) and channel fields.
- No color (optional): `clearable`.

**ColorPicker props**

- `alpha?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Adds the alpha slider and a % field; the value becomes #rrggbbaa when not opaque.
- `clearable?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Adds a "No color" swatch to the palette; picking it sets the value to ''.
- `defaultFormat?`: `"hex" | "rgb" | "hsl"`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`, default `#3b6fd6`
- `defaultView?`: `"palette" | "photo" | "custom"`
- `eyeDropper?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Shows the EyeDropper button where the browser supports it.
- `formats?`: `ColorFormat[]`, default `['hex', 'rgb', 'hsl']` — Formats offered in the input row.
- `onValueChange?`: `((hex: string) => void)` — Fires continuously while dragging and on every input commit.
- `onValueCommit?`: `((hex: string) => void)` — Fires when a drag ends, a key is released or an input commits — for saving/undo history.
- `photo?`: `string` — Initial image for the From photo view (the user can upload another).
- `swatches?`: `string[]` — Preset colors for the Palette view.
- `value?`: `string` — Hex color (#rrggbb or #rrggbbaa). An empty string means "no color" (see `clearable`).
- `viewLabels?`: `Partial<Record<ColorPickerView, string>>` — Tab names.
- `views?`: `ColorPickerView[]` — Which sources to offer. More than one renders tabs (Palette / From photo / Custom).

**ColorField props**

- `alpha?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Adds the alpha slider and a % field; the value becomes #rrggbbaa when not opaque.
- `className?`: `string`
- `clearable?`: `boolean` — Adds a "No color" swatch to the palette; picking it sets the value to ''.
- `defaultFormat?`: `"hex" | "rgb" | "hsl"`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`, default `#3b6fd6`
- `defaultView?`: `"palette" | "photo" | "custom"`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `eyeDropper?`: `boolean` — Shows the EyeDropper button where the browser supports it.
- `formats?`: `ColorFormat[]` — Formats offered in the input row.
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `name?`: `string`
- `onValueChange?`: `((hex: string) => void)` — Fires continuously while dragging and on every input commit.
- `onValueCommit?`: `((hex: string) => void)` — Fires when a drag ends, a key is released or an input commits — for saving/undo history.
- `photo?`: `string` — Initial image for the From photo view (the user can upload another).
- `swatches?`: `string[]` — Preset colors for the Palette view.
- `value?`: `string` — Hex color (#rrggbb or #rrggbbaa). An empty string means "no color" (see `clearable`).
- `viewLabels?`: `Partial<Record<ColorPickerView, string>>` — Tab names.
- `views?`: `ColorPickerView[]` — Which sources to offer. More than one renders tabs (Palette / From photo / Custom).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: In a form: a field that shows and accepts the hex, the picker on demand.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-64"><ColorField label="Brand color" defaultValue="#4f46e5" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two presets for a brand color — the customer’s own color isn’t there.

  ```tsx
  <SwatchPicker
    aria-label="Brand color"
    shape="square"
    options={[{ value: 'a', label: 'Indigo', color: '#4f46e5' }, { value: 'b', label: 'Teal', color: '#0d9488' }]}
    defaultValue="a"
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The area and each slider are keyboard-operable (arrows, Home/End) and announce the value.
- Always keep the text input — it’s the precise, accessible way to set a color.
- Check the chosen color’s contrast where it’s used; the picker doesn’t know the context.

## Combobox

`import { Combobox } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/combobox';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-combobox--docs

**When to use**

- Picking from a long list people search rather than scroll: regions, users, domains.
- `multiple`: several values shown as chips — tags, recipients, labels.
- `allowCreate`: a list people can add to (new tag).

**When not to use**

- Up to 15 known options → use Select (6–15) or RadioGroup (up to 5)
- Free text where suggestions only help → use Autocomplete
- Searching content, not choosing a value → use SearchBox (Patterns: Search)

**Anatomy**

- Input: typing filters the list (label and keywords).
- Chips (optional): in `multiple` mode; Backspace removes the last.
- Clear / chevron buttons (optional): `showClear`, `showChevron`.
- List: options, an empty message, a loading state, and the “Create …” row with `allowCreate`.

**Combobox props**

- `options`: `ComboboxOption[]`
- `allowCreate?`: `boolean` — Allow the current input to be committed even if it matches no option.
- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `chevronLabel?`: `string`, default `Open options (localized: combobox.open)` — Accessible label for the chevron button that opens the list.
- `className?`: `string`
- `clearLabel?`: `string`, default `Clear selection (localized: combobox.clear)`
- `contentClassName?`: `string`
- `createOnDelimiter?`: `boolean` — In multiple mode, commit the current input as a chip when space or comma is typed.
- `createOptionIcon?`: `ReactNode`
- `createOptionLabel?`: `((query: string) => ReactNode)`, default `localized: combobox.create` — Label for the create-option row in multiple mode. Defaults to `Create "{query}"`.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | string[]`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `No results. (localized: common.noResults)`
- `filter?`: `((option: ComboboxOption, query: string) => boolean)`
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"` — Matches TextField's own heightSize: 'md' (40px, body-m) or 'sm' (32px, body-s) — the dropdown's own text size follows it too.
- `id?`: `string`
- `loading?`: `boolean`
- `loadingMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `Loading… (localized: common.loading)`
- `multiple?`: `boolean`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void) | ((value: string[]) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Select… (localized: combobox.placeholder)`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean` — Presentation-only: muted fill, no hover, no chevron/clear/chip-remove. Chips always wrap.
- `renderChip?`: `((option: ComboboxOption) => ReactNode)`
- `renderOption?`: `((option: ComboboxOption) => ReactNode)`
- `showChevron?`: `boolean` — Shows the chevron button that opens the list. Hidden when `readOnly`. Default `true`.
- `showClear?`: `boolean`
- `value?`: `string | string[]`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Many options with long names — people type “frank” instead of scanning.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cbx-region">Region</Label>
    <Combobox id="gl-cbx-region" options={REGIONS} placeholder="Search regions" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two options behind a search field — a Select or segmented control is faster.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-cbx-sort">Sort by</Label>
    <Combobox id="gl-cbx-sort" options={[{ value: 'new', label: 'Newest' }, { value: 'old', label: 'Oldest' }]} placeholder="Search" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Input is a `combobox`; arrows move through options, Enter picks, Escape closes.
- Label it with `Label` + `id` or `aria-label` — the placeholder isn’t a label.
- Chips are announced with their remove buttons (“Remove EU (Ireland)”).

## Command

`import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandEmpty, CommandLoading, CommandGroup, CommandSeparator, CommandItem, CommandShortcut, CommandFooter } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/command';`

Status: stable · Category: Search & Filter
Docs: ./?path=/docs/search-filter-command--docs

**When to use**

- A ⌘K palette (`CommandDialog`): jump to any page or run any action by typing.
- A searchable list of actions or destinations inside a popover.

**When not to use**

- Choosing a value for a form field → use Combobox or Select
- A handful of actions → use Buttons or DropdownMenu
- Searching content and showing results on a page → use SearchBox (Patterns: Search)

**Anatomy**

- Input: filters items by label and keywords as you type.
- Groups (optional): `CommandGroup heading`; a group with no matches hides.
- Item: icon, label, optional `description`/`breadcrumb`, `CommandShortcut`.
- Empty / loading: `CommandEmpty`, `CommandLoading`.

**Command props**

- `label?`: `string`
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `shouldFilter?`: `boolean`, default `true`

**CommandDialog props**

- `className?`: `string`
- `description?`: `string`, default `Search for pages and actions, or run a command. (localized: command.description)`
- `title?`: `string`, default `Command palette (localized: command.title)`

**CommandInput props**

- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `value?`: `string`

**CommandGroup props**

- `heading?`: `ReactNode`

**CommandItem props**

- `breadcrumb?`: `ReactNode` — Path/context line ABOVE the label, smaller and subtler — e.g. "Settings > Review".
- `description?`: `ReactNode`, default `Search for pages and actions, or run a command. (localized: command.description)` — Second line under the label, smaller and subtler. When set (or `breadcrumb` is set), `children` is treated as the label only — don't also embed a leading icon or trailing CommandShortcut in children; use the `icon`/`toneIcon` props instead.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon before the label — 16px, decorative. Mutually exclusive with `toneIcon` (same slot). You can still embed an icon directly in `children` instead (existing pattern) if you don't need `description`.
- `keywords?`: `string[]`
- `onSelect?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `toneIcon?`: `{ tone: StatusTone; icon?: ReactNode; shape?: "circle" | "square"; }` — Tone-tinted glyph before the label instead of `icon` — same slot.
- `value?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, DialogProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Many destinations and actions, grouped, reached by typing.

  ```tsx
  <div className={BOX}>
    <Command label="Go to or run">
      <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search…" />
      <CommandList>
        <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
        <CommandGroup heading="Go to">
          <CommandItem value="dashboard"><HomeSimple /> Dashboard</CommandItem>
          <CommandItem value="sites"><Globe /> Sites</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
        <CommandSeparator />
        <CommandGroup heading="Settings">
          <CommandItem value="settings"><Settings /> General settings<CommandShortcut>⌘,</CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
          <CommandItem value="tools"><Wrench /> Tools</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </CommandList>
    </Command>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Don’t hide two actions like these behind a palette — show them as buttons.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Cancel</Button>
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Save</Button>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The input is a `combobox`; the highlighted item is its `aria-activedescendant`. Arrows move, Enter runs, Escape clears.
- Name it with `label` (“Command menu”); the dialog version also needs `title`.
- Shortcuts shown in items are hints only — the real shortcut must work outside the palette too.

## ConfirmDialog

`import { ConfirmDialog } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/confirm-dialog';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-confirmdialog--docs

**When to use**

- High-stakes, irreversible deletes where a click isn’t enough: `confirmValue` makes people type the name.
- Deleting a domain, a database, an organisation.

**When not to use**

- Ordinary confirmations → use AlertDialog
- Reversible actions → use UndoToast

**Anatomy**

- Title and description: the object and what’s lost.
- Type-to-confirm (optional): `confirmValue`; the action enables only on an exact match.
- Actions: `confirmLabel` with the verb; `tone="danger"`.

**ConfirmDialog props**

- `title`: `ReactNode`
- `cancelLabel?`: `string`, default `Cancel (localized: common.cancel)`
- `confirmIcon?`: `ReactNode`
- `confirmLabel?`: `string`, default `Delete (localized: confirmDialog.confirm)`
- `confirmValue?`: `string` — Require the user to type this string exactly to enable the action.
- `confirmValueMono?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Monospace the typed value (a domain, slug, id, etc). Set false for a non-identifier value like an email. Defaults to true.
- `contentGap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `onConfirm?`: `(() => void)`
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `open?`: `boolean`
- `showFooterDivider?`: `boolean`
- `showHeaderDivider?`: `boolean`
- `titleSize?`: `"md" | "lg"`, default `md`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "danger"`, default `danger`
- `trigger?`: `ReactNode`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Typing the domain makes deleting the wrong one unlikely.

  ```tsx
  <ConfirmDialog
    title="Delete seashell.dev?"
    description="All DNS records, mailboxes and certificates for this domain are removed."
    confirmValue="seashell.dev"
    confirmLabel="Delete domain"
    tone="danger"
    trigger={<Button appearance="outlined" tone="danger" size="md">Delete domain</Button>}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: Typing a title to archive a draft that can be restored: friction with no protection.

  ```tsx
  <ConfirmDialog
    title="Archive this draft?"
    confirmValue="Q3 newsletter draft"
    confirmValueMono={false}
    confirmLabel="Archive"
    tone="neutral"
    trigger={<Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Archive draft</Button>}
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The field says exactly what to type; the action stays disabled until it matches.
- If the deleted row held the trigger, focus moves to its nearest surviving ancestor instead of falling to the page.

## ContextMenu

`import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuTrailing, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuTrigger, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuSub } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/context-menu';`

Status: stable · Category: Menus
Docs: ./?path=/docs/menus-contextmenu--docs

**When to use**

- A right-click shortcut in tool-like surfaces: a file grid, a canvas, a code editor, a kanban card.
- Only as a second path to actions that are also reachable some other way.

**When not to use**

- The only way to reach an action → use a visible Button or DropdownMenu
- Content pages and forms (people expect the browser menu) → use DropdownMenu

**Anatomy**

- Trigger area: `ContextMenuTrigger` around the target.
- Content: opens at the pointer; same items as DropdownMenu — shortcuts, checkbox/radio, submenus.

**ContextMenuItem props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "danger"`, default `neutral`

**ContextMenuLabel props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

**ContextMenuSubTrigger props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: ContextMenuProps, HTMLAttributes, MenuContentProps, MenuContentImplProps, PopperContentProps, MenuItemProps, MenuItemImplProps, MenuCheckboxItemProps, MenuRadioItemProps, MenuSubContentProps, ContextMenuTriggerProps, MenuRadioGroupProps, ContextMenuSubProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Right-click is a shortcut; the same actions are behind the visible kebab.

  ```tsx
  <ContextMenu>
    <ContextMenuTrigger asChild>
      <div className={TILE}>
        <span>report.pdf</span>
        <DropdownMenu>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
            <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="sm" iconOnly leftIcon={<KebabIconVertical />} aria-label="More actions for report.pdf" />
          </DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
            <DropdownMenuItem>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      </div>
    </ContextMenuTrigger>
    <ContextMenuContent>
      <ContextMenuItem>Rename</ContextMenuItem>
      <ContextMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</ContextMenuItem>
    </ContextMenuContent>
  </ContextMenu>
  ```

- Don’t: Actions only on right-click: invisible, and out of reach on touch and for many keyboard users.

  ```tsx
  <ContextMenu>
    <ContextMenuTrigger asChild>
      <div className={TILE}>
        <span>report.pdf</span>
      </div>
    </ContextMenuTrigger>
    <ContextMenuContent>
      <ContextMenuItem>Rename</ContextMenuItem>
      <ContextMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</ContextMenuItem>
    </ContextMenuContent>
  </ContextMenu>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Keyboard users open it with Shift+F10 or the Menu key — few know that, so never make it the only path.
- Inside, it works like DropdownMenu: arrows, typeahead, Escape.
- On touch it opens on long-press; keep the same actions in a visible menu.

## CopyButton

`import { CopyButton } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/copy-button';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-copybutton--docs

**When to use**

- Next to a value people paste somewhere else: an API key, a DNS record, a command, a link.
- When selecting the text by hand would be fiddly (long, monospaced, partly hidden).

**When not to use**

- A secret that should stay masked until asked → use SecretField (copy built in)
- A block of code → use CodeBlock (copy built in)
- Sharing a page → use a Share action or the URL itself

**Anatomy**

- Button: a Button; icon-only with `label={null}` (then `aria-label`).
- Icon: copy → check for the confirmation.
- Label (optional): “Copy” → “Copied” for `resetDelay` ms.

**CopyButton props**

- `value`: `string` — Text written to the clipboard.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `tonal`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `copiedLabel?`: `ReactNode`, default `Copied (localized: copyButton.copied)` — Label shown for `resetDelay`ms after a successful copy. Default "Copied".
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `label?`: `ReactNode`, default `Copy (localized: copyButton.copy)` — Visible label beside the icon. Pass null for icon-only (then set aria-label). Default "Copy".
- `onCopied?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `onCopyError?`: `((error: unknown) => void)`
- `resetDelay?`: `number`, default `1500` — ms before the button reverts from the copied state. Default 1500.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`, default `md`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Right next to the value it copies, and the name says which value.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <code className="rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-md)] bg-[var(--color-bg-neutral-bg-neutral-subtle)] px-2 py-1 font-mono text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text)]">ns1.theya.dev</code>
    <CopyButton value="ns1.theya.dev" label={null} aria-label="Copy ns1.theya.dev" appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="sm" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: One “Copy” for two values — which one did it take?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2">
    <code className="font-mono text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text)]">ns1.theya.dev</code>
    <code className="font-mono text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text)]">ns2.theya.dev</code>
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Copy</Button>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The confirmation is announced (“Copied”), not only shown by the icon swap.
- Icon-only needs an `aria-label` naming the value: “Copy API key”, not just “Copy”.
- If copying fails, say so — wire `onCopyError` to a toast.

## CountUp

`import { CountUp } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/count-up';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-countup--docs

**When to use**

- A headline figure on a landing page: “12,400 sites”, “99.98% uptime”, “3× faster”.

**When not to use**

- A live value in product UI (it must read correctly the moment it’s seen) → use Stat
- Numbers people compare in a table → use Table / DataTable
- Time left until something → use Countdown

**Anatomy**

- Number: tabular digits, formatted with `format` (Intl) in the provider’s locale.
- Prefix / suffix (optional): text in the same line: `$`, `+`, `%`.

**CountUp props**

- `to`: `number` — The value to land on.
- `duration?`: `number`, default `1400` — Run time, ms.
- `format?`: `NumberFormatOptions` — Number format (locale from TheyaLocaleProvider): `{ maximumFractionDigits: 1 }`, `{ style: 'percent' }`, `{ notation: 'compact' }`…
- `from?`: `number`, default `0` — Where to start.
- `prefix?`: `string`, default `` — Text before / after the number, inside the same line: "$", "+".
- `suffix?`: `string`, default ``

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One figure, counted once when it comes into view.

  ```tsx
  <span className="text-heading-m"><CountUp to={12400} /> sites</span>
  ```

- Don’t: Counting a live product value: for a second it shows a wrong number.

  ```tsx
  <span className="text-body-m">Disk: <CountUp to={78} suffix="%" /></span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Screen readers get only the final value; the running digits are hidden from them.
- prefers-reduced-motion: the final value shows at once.
- Tabular digits keep the width steady while it counts, so nothing around it shifts.

## Countdown

`import { Countdown } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/countdown';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-countdown--docs

**When to use**

- Time left until a deadline that matters to the user: a trial ending, a maintenance window starting, “resend code in 0:42”.
- A promo end on a landing (`appearance="blocks"`).

**When not to use**

- The deadline is far away (weeks) → use the date: “Trial ends Nov 12”
- Elapsed time or duration → use plain text or Timeline
- Fake urgency → use nothing — don’t

**Anatomy**

- Digits: inline `clock` (2d 04:12:09) or `compact` (2d 4h 12m), tiles in `blocks`, or a draining `ring` with the largest unit inside (give `from` so it knows the full span).
- Unit labels (optional): under each tile in blocks.
- Completed (optional): what shows at zero (`completed`).

**Countdown props**

- `to`: `string | number | Date` — Deadline: a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp in ms.
- `appearance?`: `"inline" | "blocks" | "ring"`, default `inline` — `inline` text, `blocks` tiles, or `ring`: a ring that drains as time runs out, with
- `completed?`: `ReactNode` — Shown instead of the zeros once the deadline has passed.
- `format?`: `"clock" | "compact"`, default `clock` — Inline format: `clock` → 2d 04:12:09, `compact` → 2d 4h 12m.
- `from?`: `string | number | Date` — Ring only: when the countdown started, for the share left. Defaults to when it mounted.
- `labels?`: `Partial<Record<CountdownUnit, [string, string]>>` — Unit names (singular, plural) — used for block labels and the spoken text.
- `onComplete?`: `(() => void)` — Fires once when the countdown reaches zero while mounted.
- `paused?`: `boolean` — Freezes the countdown at its current value.
- `precision?`: `"minutes" | "seconds"`, default `seconds` — Smallest unit that ticks. `minutes` re-renders once a minute.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`
- `srText?`: `((remaining: string) => string)` — Prefix/suffix for the spoken text, e.g. (t) => `Sale ends in ${t}`.
- `trimLeading?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Hides leading units that are zero (days, then hours).
- `urgentBelow?`: `number` — Below this many seconds the numbers turn danger.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Inline, minutes are enough for a two-day deadline.

  ```tsx
  <p className="text-body-m">Trial ends in <Countdown to={inTwoDays()} format="compact" /></p>
  ```

- Don’t: Ticking seconds for a trial: noise that reads like pressure.

  ```tsx
  <Countdown to={inTwoDays()} appearance="blocks" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `role="timer"`; the spoken text is a sentence that changes once a minute — screen readers aren’t flooded every second.
- Give the deadline as a date too, near the countdown, for people who read it later.
- Don’t trigger anything irreversible at zero without telling people first.

## DataTable

`import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/data-table';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-datatable--docs

**When to use**

- Lists of records people scan, sort, filter, select and act on: sites, domains, invoices, users.
- Rows that open a detail page (whole-row link) or carry per-row actions.

**When not to use**

- A handful of static rows → use Table
- Details of one object → use DescriptionList
- Cards with images or rich content → use a card grid
- Hierarchy → use Tree

**Anatomy**

- Toolbar (optional): filter / search, then bulk actions when rows are selected (`toolbar` + DataTableToolbar).
- Header: sortable column headers (`DataTableColumnHeader`), optional select-all.
- Rows: one or two lines (`lines`); cells are DataTableCell kinds; `meta.primary` makes the row a link.
- Row menu (optional): per-row actions pinned right (`rowMenu`), also on right-click with `contextual`.
- Footer (optional): pagination, or infinite scroll with `onLoadMore`.
- Loading / empty: skeleton rows while `loading`; `emptyState` for none or no matches.
- Phone layout: below 640px rows stack into items (`mobileLayout="stack"`, default; labels from `meta.label`). `paged` keeps the primary column and pages the rest; `scroll` keeps the table, with `meta.pin` columns frozen.

**DataTable props**

- `columns`: `ColumnDef<TData, unknown>[]`
- `data`: `TData[]`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `columnFilters?`: `ColumnFiltersState`
- `columnsPerPage?`: `number`, default `2` — `mobileLayout="paged"`: how many columns besides the primary one show at a time on a phone.
- `embedded?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Drop the container's own border/background chrome, round only its top corners, for nesting inside another bordered surface.
- `embeddedBottomRounded?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `No results. (localized: common.noResults)`
- `emptyState?`: `((table: Table<TData>) => ReactNode)` — Rich empty state, rendered with the live table instance so it can branch on filter activity. Takes precedence over `emptyMessage`.
- `enableSelection?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Prepend a select-all/select-row checkbox column. Auto-drops below md.
- `estimateRowHeight?`: `number`, default `48`
- `fillViewport?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Stretch the scroll body to the remaining viewport height. Overridden by explicit `maxHeight`.
- `getRowHref?`: `((row: TData) => string)`
- `getRowId?`: `((row: TData) => string)` — Stable identity for a row, used as its selection key. Supply whenever selection is enabled and `data` can change under the user.
- `getRowLabel?`: `((row: TData) => string)`
- `hasMore?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `hideFooter?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Omit the footer and disable client-side pagination — every row renders.
- `hideHeader?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Omit the header row entirely. Mutually exclusive with sorting and header select-all.
- `lines?`: `"1" | "2"`, default `1` — Lines of text a row is sized for. Set 2 when ANY column stacks a value over a second line.
- `linkComponent?`: `ElementType` — Element for the whole-row link. Defaults to a plain `<a>`; pass your router's link for client-side navigation.
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `loadingMore?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `manualFiltering?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `manualPagination?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `manualSorting?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `maxHeight?`: `string | number`
- `mobileLayout?`: `"stack" | "paged" | "scroll"`, default `stack` — Below 640px: `stack` (default) turns each row into a stacked item with label/value pairs; `paged` shows the primary column plus a few others at a time; `scroll` keeps the table and scrolls it sideways.
- `onColumnFiltersChange?`: `OnChangeFn<ColumnFiltersState>`
- `onLoadMore?`: `(() => void)` — Switch to infinite scroll: a sentinel row calls this when it nears view. Replaces the pager.
- `onPaginationChange?`: `OnChangeFn<PaginationState>`
- `onRowClick?`: `((row: TData) => void)`
- `onRowSelectionChange?`: `OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>`
- `onSortingChange?`: `OnChangeFn<SortingState>`
- `overscan?`: `number`, default `8`
- `pageCount?`: `number`
- `pageSize?`: `number`, default `10`
- `pagination?`: `PaginationState`
- `pinSelection?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `rowCount?`: `number`
- `rowMenu?`: `DataTableRowMenu<TData>` — Per-row actions, appended as the final column, pinned right at every width. `contextual` also exposes them on right-click.
- `rowSelection?`: `RowSelectionState`
- `selectAll?`: `"header" | "none" | "toolbar"`, default `header` — Where the select-all control lives: "header" (default), "toolbar" (pair with DataTableToolbar), or "none".
- `selectAllTooltip?`: `ReactNode`, default `Select All (localized: dataTable.selectAllTooltip)`
- `skeletonRows?`: `number`
- `sorting?`: `SortingState`
- `stickyHeader?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `toolbar?`: `((table: Table<TData>) => ReactNode)`
- `virtualized?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Render only rows in view (plus overscan) via

**DataTableColumnHeader props**

- `column`: `Column<TData, TValue>`
- `title`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Each column uses its kind: mono for domains, status with a dot, numbers on the right.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-[26rem]"><DataTable columns={good} data={SITES} hideFooter ariaLabel="Sites" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Everything as plain text: raw status values, numbers that don’t line up.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-[26rem]"><DataTable columns={bad} data={SITES} hideFooter ariaLabel="Sites, plain" /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name the table with `ariaLabel`; give rows a `getRowLabel` so links, checkboxes and menus say which row they act on.
- The whole-row link is a real link on the primary cell; controls in cells stay separately focusable.
- Sort state is announced on the column header; selection count is announced in the toolbar.
- Set `getRowId` whenever selection is on and the data can change.

## DataTableCell

`import { DataTableCell, DataTableCellMenuTrigger } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/data-table-cell';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-datatablecell--docs

**When to use**

- Every cell of a DataTable: pick the kind by content — text, mono, primary, status, badge, usage, sparkline.
- Editable cells (input, number, select, combobox, switch…) for inline edits in a table.

**When not to use**

- Outside a table → use the matching component: Badge, StatusDot, TextField…
- Editing many fields of one row → use a Drawer or a detail page

**Anatomy**

- Box: one row height for the whole table (`lines` 1 or 2); `loading` draws the kind’s own placeholder.
- Value: by `kind`.
- Second line (optional): `secondary` under the value, `secondaryMono` for identifiers.

**DataTableCell props**

- `ariaLabel`: `string`
- `checked`: `boolean | "indeterminate"`
- `data`: `number[]`
- `total`: `number | null` — null for an unlimited/indeterminate quota: no bar, no misleading 0%.
- `value`: `ReactNode | string[] | DateRange` — ONE value: a cell has no room for a two-thumb range — that belongs in `custom`.
- `area?`: `boolean`
- `badges?`: `BadgeCellBadge[]` — Several badges, worst severity first. Collapse from the tail as the column narrows.
- `below?`: `ReactNode` — Extra lines under `secondary` — sized as a minimum since they appear only at some widths.
- `calendarProps?`: `Omit<DayPickerProps, "onSelect" | "mode" | "selected" | "numberOfMonths">`
- `collapsedLabel?`: `string` — Noun used once every badge collapses into one ("4 alerts"). Defaults to "badges".
- `describedBy?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`
- `errorMessage?`: `string`
- `formatValue?`: `((value: number) => string)` — Doubles as the visible readout and the thumb's aria-valuetext. Defaults to the bare number.
- `grow?`: `boolean` — Keep the row height as a minimum rather than fixed, for content whose line count varies by row.
- `header?`: `string`
- `height?`: `number`
- `id?`: `string`
- `invalid?`: `boolean`
- `kind?`: `"number" | "input" | "select" | "menu" | "textarea" | "switch" | "text" | "combobox" | "slider" | "status" | "primary" | "badge" | "custom" | "mono" | "usage" | "sparkline" | "autocomplete" | "tags" | "date-range" | "selector"`
- `label?`: `ReactNode` — Required: status is never color alone.
- `labelledBy?`: `string`
- `leading?`: `ReactNode` — Sits before the text: an Avatar, an icon, a favicon. Keep it ≤32px.
- `lines?`: `"1" | "2"` — Lines the cell is sized for. You rarely pass it — inherits the table's `lines` unless this cell has a second line of its own.
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Render the first-load placeholder for this kind instead of the value.
- `max?`: `number`
- `min?`: `number`
- `mono?`: `boolean`
- `muted?`: `boolean`
- `numberOfMonths?`: `number`
- `onBlur?`: `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> | FocusEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement>`
- `onCheckedChange?`: `((checked: boolean) => void) | ((checked: boolean) => void)`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void) | ((value: string) => void) | ((value: number | null) => void) | ((value: string) => void) | ((value: string) => void) | ((value: string) => void) | ((value: string[]) => void) | ((value: DateRange) => void) | ((value: number) => void)`
- `options?`: `string[] | AutocompleteOption[] | ComboboxOption[] | { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; }[]`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean` — Value stays selectable and normal-ink; gives up border/hover wash/affordances.
- `revealOnHover?`: `boolean` — Keep the control invisible until hovered/focused/open. Needs `group/row` on the row.
- `rows?`: `number`
- `secondary?`: `ReactNode`
- `secondaryMono?`: `boolean` — Render the second line in monospace (right for an identifier, wrong for a sentence).
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"` — Applies to every badge in the group, including the collapsed "N more" pill.
- `step?`: `number`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "muted" | "primary" | "brand"`
- `type?`: `"number" | "text" | "tel" | "url" | "email"`
- `width?`: `number`

**DataTableCellMenuTrigger props**

- `label`: `string`
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`
- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Render onto the child element instead of a <button> (shadcn/Radix Slot convention).
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Renders as a square icon-only button (no label). Provide the icon via leftIcon.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The main value on top, details on the second line.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-64"><DataTableCell kind="text" value="shop.seashell.dev" mono secondary="eu-west-1 · Pro" lines={2} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Four facts in one line truncate, and none of them can be sorted.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-64"><DataTableCell value="shop.seashell.dev · eu-west-1 · Pro · 12.4 GB" /></div>
  ```

- Do: Status: a dot plus a word.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-40"><DataTableCell kind="status" tone="danger" label="Error" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: An internal code people have to look up.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-40"><DataTableCell value="ERR_5" /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Editable kinds need a `label` — usually “column, row” (“Plan, shop.seashell.dev”); it isn’t visible in the cell.
- Invalid edits show a real message linked to the field, not only a red border.
- Status and badge kinds always carry a word; color is never the only signal.

## DataTableToolbar

`import { DataTableToolbar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/data-table-toolbar';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-datatabletoolbar--docs

**When to use**

- Above a selectable DataTable: filter / search when idle, bulk actions when rows are selected — in the same strip.

**When not to use**

- Page-level actions (Create, Import) → use PageHeader actions
- A table without selection or filters → use nothing — skip the strip
- Actions on one row → use the row menu

**Anatomy**

- Select all: checkbox on the left, never moves between states.
- Idle content: `idleLeft` (a count) and `children` (FilterField) on the right.
- Selection count: replaces the select-all label once rows are picked.
- Bulk actions: verbs with icons; overflow to “More” when out of room; `tone="danger"` + `confirm` for deletes.
- Clear: drops the selection.

**DataTableToolbar props**

- `table`: `Table<TData>`
- `actions?`: `DataTableBulkAction<TData>[]`, default `[]`
- `allRowsCount?`: `number` — Total rows matching the table's current server-side filters.
- `children?`: `ReactNode` — Right-hand side of the idle state — usually a FilterField.
- `clearLabel?`: `string`, default `Clear selection (localized: dataTable.clearSelection)`
- `embedded?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Flush treatment for a toolbar embedded at the bottom of a card.
- `idleLeft?`: `ReactNode` — Extra idle-state left-hand content (e.g. a result count).
- `maxVisible?`: `number` — Hard ceiling on inline actions, even when the bar has room for more. Unset: no ceiling.
- `minTrailingWidth?`: `number`, default `160` — Floor, in px, the idle bar's trailing slot needs before select-all label gives way to a bare checkbox.
- `onSelectAllScopeChange?`: `((scope: { excludeIds: string[]; } | null) => void)`
- `resolveAllRowIds?`: `((filters: ColumnFiltersState) => Promise<string[]>)` — Resolve IDs for every server-side row matching the table's current
- `selectAllLabel?`: `ReactNode`, default `Select all (localized: dataTable.selectAll)`
- `selectAllScope?`: `{ excludeIds: string[]; } | null` — Selection strategy: "every filtered row except these ids", kept by
- `selectAllTooltip?`: `ReactNode`, default `Select All (localized: dataTable.selectAllTooltip)`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Actions appear with the selection, say how many rows, and Delete asks first.

  ```tsx
  <Demo />
  ```

- Don’t: Always-there disabled buttons: no count, no context, easy to miss when they wake up.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-[26rem] gap-2">
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" disabled>Archive selected</Button>
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="danger" disabled>Delete selected</Button>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The selection count is a polite live region.
- Bulk actions are one Toolbar: a single tab stop, arrows between actions.
- Clear returns focus to the select-all checkbox.
- Disabled actions explain why (`disabledReason`) in a tooltip.

## DatePicker

`import { DatePicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/date-picker';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-datepicker--docs

**When to use**

- One date near today that people pick by looking at a month: a start date, a due date, a delivery day.
- Dates with rules — past days, weekends — disabled through `calendarProps`.

**When not to use**

- A date people know by heart, far from today (birth date, card expiry) → use MaskedInput
- A start and end → use DateRangePicker
- A date with a time → use DateTimePicker

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: looks like a Select: calendar icon, the date or a placeholder, chevron.
- Clear (optional): `showClear` for optional dates.
- Calendar popover: opens on the selected month; rules via `calendarProps` (`disabled`, `startMonth`…).

**DatePicker props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `calendarProps?`: `Omit<DayPickerProps, "onSelect" | "mode" | "selected">`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `Date`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `id?`: `string`
- `onChange?`: `((date: Date) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Pick a date (localized: datePicker.placeholder)`
- `showClear?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show an inline clear button when a date is selected. Default false.
- `value?`: `Date`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A date close to today; days in the past can’t be picked.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-dp-start">Start date</Label>
    <DatePicker id="gl-dp-start" placeholder="Pick a date" calendarProps={{ disabled: { before: new Date() } }} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A birth date in a calendar: 30 years of “previous month” clicks for something people can type.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-dp-birth">Date of birth</Label>
    <DatePicker id="gl-dp-birth" placeholder="Pick a date" />
  </div>
  ```

- Do: A known date far from today: typed, with the format in the label.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-dp-birth2">Date of birth (DD.MM.YYYY)</Label>
    <MaskedInput id="gl-dp-birth2" mask="__.__.____" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A due date that allows the past — and opens years away from today.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-dp-due">Due date</Label>
    <DatePicker id="gl-dp-due" defaultValue={new Date(2020, 0, 1)} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The trigger is named by its label (`Label` + `id` or `aria-label`); the chosen date is its description.
- In the calendar: arrows move by day, Page Up/Down by month, Enter picks, Escape closes and returns focus.
- Say the rule in text too (“From today”) — a disabled day isn’t explained by itself.

## DateRangePicker

`import { DateRangePicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/date-range-picker';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-daterangepicker--docs

**When to use**

- A start and end date picked together: a report period, a booking, a filter.
- People need to see the length of the span while choosing.

**When not to use**

- Fixed periods (Last 7 days, This month) → use Select or ToggleGroup — add a Custom option that opens this
- A single date → use DatePicker
- A time span within a day → use TimeRangePicker

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: same field as DatePicker; shows “Jun 3 – Jun 17, 2026”.
- Calendar: `numberOfMonths` (2 by default, stacked below md); stays open until both ends are picked.
- Clear (optional): `showClear`.

**DateRangePicker props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `calendarProps?`: `Omit<DayPickerProps, "onSelect" | "mode" | "selected" | "numberOfMonths">`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `DateRange`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `id?`: `string`
- `numberOfMonths?`: `number`, default `2`
- `onChange?`: `((range: DateRange) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Pick a date range (localized: dateRangePicker.placeholder)`
- `showClear?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show an inline clear button when a range is selected. Default false.
- `value?`: `DateRange`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One field, one calendar: the span is drawn as you pick it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-drp-period">Report period</Label>
    <DateRangePicker id="gl-drp-period" placeholder="Pick a period" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two separate pickers: two popovers, and “To” can end up before “From”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-3">
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="gl-drp-from">From</Label>
      <DatePicker id="gl-drp-from" placeholder="Pick a date" />
    </div>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="gl-drp-to">To</Label>
      <DatePicker id="gl-drp-to" placeholder="Pick a date" />
    </div>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The trigger is named by the label; the chosen range is its description.
- Keyboard works as in DatePicker; the first Enter sets the start, the second the end.
- After clearing, focus returns to the trigger.

## DateTimePicker

`import { DateTimePicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/date-time-picker';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-datetimepicker--docs

**When to use**

- A moment that needs both date and time: a scheduled send, a maintenance window, a reminder.

**When not to use**

- Only the date matters → use DatePicker
- A time every day (opening hours) → use TimeField or TimeRangePicker

**Anatomy**

- Date: a DatePicker.
- Time: a TimeField; `step` in minutes, `hourCycle` 12/24. Stays empty until a time is actually picked.
- Value: one `Date`; `onChange`’s second argument says whether the time was set.

**DateTimePicker props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `calendarProps?`: `Omit<DayPickerProps, "onSelect" | "mode" | "selected">`
- `className?`: `string`
- `dateClassName?`: `string`
- `datePlaceholder?`: `string`, default `Pick a date (localized: datePicker.placeholder)`
- `defaultValue?`: `Date`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `hourCycle?`: `"12" | "24"`, default `12`
- `id?`: `string`
- `onChange?`: `((value: Date, meta: { timeSet: boolean; }) => void)` — `timeSet` is false while only the date was picked — the Date then carries a placeholder 00:00.
- `showClear?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show the inline clear button in the date field. Default false.
- `step?`: `number`, default `30`
- `timeClassName?`: `string`
- `timePlaceholder?`: `string`, default `Select time (localized: timeField.placeholder)`
- `value?`: `Date`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Date and time picked separately, in 15-minute steps; no silent midnight.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-96 max-w-full flex-col gap-2">
    <span aria-hidden="true" className="font-body text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
      Send at
    </span>
    <DateTimePicker aria-label="Send at" step={15} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: One text field for both: format errors, and no idea whether 3:00 is AM or PM.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Send at" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" widthSize="lg" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name it with `aria-label`: the date part gets that name, the time part gets it plus “time” (“Send at time”).
- If the time is required, say so when it’s missing — don’t store 00:00.
- Say the time zone in the description when people in several zones use it.

## DensityToggle

`import { DensityToggle } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/density-toggle';`

Status: beta · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-densitytoggle--docs

**When to use**

- Products with data-heavy screens (tables, admin forms), where some people want more rows on screen and others want larger targets.
- A single dense region on a regular page: control it with `value` / `onValueChange` and put `data-density` on that region.

**When not to use**

- Marketing and landing pages → use the default density, no toggle
- Touch-first screens → use default or comfortable; compact controls drop to 24–36px

**Anatomy**

- Group: outlined single ToggleGroup, one option always on; uncontrolled it sets `data-density` on the document.
- Options: Compact · Default · Comfortable — text labels, localized.

**DensityToggle props**

- `onValueChange?`: `((density: Density) => void)`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `sm` — Toggle size. sm (32px) fits a toolbar, md (40px) a settings form.
- `value?`: `"default" | "compact" | "comfortable"` — Controlled value. When set, the toggle only reports changes through

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Next to the table it affects, or in the view / display settings.

  ```tsx
  <DensityToggle />
  ```

- Don’t: One switch per screen or region; repeated switches fight each other.

  ```tsx
  <span className="font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">Density toggle inside every card</span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A radio-style group named “Density”; arrow keys move between options, the current one is announced as checked.
- Compact shrinks controls one step (40 → 36px for a default field) but never under 24px, the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum; DataTable keeps a 44px floor for controls below the md breakpoint.

## DescriptionList

`import { DescriptionList } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/description-list';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-descriptionlist--docs

**When to use**

- Properties of one object: site details, an invoice header, a certificate.
- A read-only summary before confirming (review step).

**When not to use**

- Several objects with the same fields → use Table or DataTable
- Editable properties → use a form, or InlineEdit / PropertyGrid
- Two or three big numbers → use Stat or Metric

**Anatomy**

- List: stacks on mobile, two columns from sm.
- Item: one pair.
- Term: the label.
- Details: the value; mono for identifiers. Long values wrap.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Label and value, read top to bottom.

  ```tsx
  <DescriptionList className="w-80">
    {PAIRS.map(([t, d]) => (
      <DescriptionItem key={t}><DescriptionTerm>{t}</DescriptionTerm><DescriptionDetails className={t === 'Plan' ? undefined : 'font-code'}>{d}</DescriptionDetails></DescriptionItem>
    ))}
  </DescriptionList>
  ```

- Don’t: A “Field / Value” table for one object adds headers that say nothing.

  ```tsx
  <Table className="w-80">
    <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Field</TableHead><TableHead>Value</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
    <TableBody>{PAIRS.map(([t, d]) => <TableRow key={t}><TableCell>{t}</TableCell><TableCell>{d}</TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Real dl / dt / dd: screen readers pair each term with its value.
- Empty values say so (“Not set”), not a blank or a dash alone.

## Dialog

`import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogBody, DialogFooter, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogTrigger, DialogClose, DialogPortal, DialogOverlay } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/dialog';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-dialog--docs

**When to use**

- A short, focused task that needs an answer before going on: rename, invite, a form of a few fields.
- When leaving the page for it would lose context.

**When not to use**

- Confirming something destructive → use ConfirmDialog / AlertDialog
- Long forms, or content people compare with the page → use Drawer or a page
- A message that needs no answer → use Toaster or Alert
- Extra detail next to a control → use Popover

**Anatomy**

- Overlay: dims and blocks the page.
- Header: `DialogTitle` (required) and `DialogDescription`.
- Body: the content or form.
- Footer: actions, primary last (right).
- Close button: top right; `showCloseButton` to hide it when the footer has Cancel.

**DialogContent props**

- `gap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"`, default `md` — Spacing between the header, body, and footer sections: `md` (default), `sm`, or `none`.
- `showCloseButton?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `size?`: `"md" | "full" | null`

**DialogHeader props**

- `showDivider?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Show the separator line between the header and dialog content.

**DialogBody props**

- `showDivider?`: `boolean`

**DialogFooter props**

- `showDivider?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Show the separator line between dialog content and the footer.

**DialogTitle props**

- `size?`: `"md" | "lg"`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: DialogProps, DialogContentProps, HTMLAttributes, DismissableLayerProps, DialogContentImplProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, DialogPortalProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Title names the task; the primary button repeats the verb.

  ```tsx
  <DialogMock title="Invite people" actions={<><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Cancel</Button><Button size="md">Send invites</Button></>} />
  ```

- Don’t: “Are you sure?” + Yes/No says nothing about what will happen.

  ```tsx
  <DialogMock title="Are you sure?" actions={<><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">No</Button><Button size="md">Yes</Button></>} />
  ```

- Do: Small and finishable in one go.

  ```tsx
  <DialogMock title="Rename database" actions={<><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Cancel</Button><Button size="md">Rename</Button></>}>One field, one decision.</DialogMock>
  ```

- Don’t: A wizard in a dialog: no room, no URL, easy to lose with one Escape.

  ```tsx
  <DialogMock title="Edit site settings" actions={<Button size="md">Next</Button>}>Step 1 of 6 — General, Domains, Environment, Build, SSL, Backups…</DialogMock>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Focus moves into the dialog on open, stays inside while it’s open, and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape closes. `DialogTitle` is required — it’s the dialog’s accessible name.
- Don’t open a dialog from another dialog.
- The first focus goes to the first field, or to the least destructive action when there’s no field.

## DiffViewer

`import { DiffViewer } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/diff-viewer';`

Status: beta · Category: Code
Docs: ./?path=/docs/code-diffviewer--docs

**When to use**

- Reviewing a change before applying it: config, a template, a policy, a file restored from backup.
- Showing what an automated change did (an update, a migration) so people can trust it.

**When not to use**

- Only one version matters → use CodeBlock
- Comparing structured records field by field → use DescriptionList or a table with old / new columns
- Editing the result → use CodeEditor next to the diff

**Anatomy**

- Header (optional): filename (old → new when renamed), +/− stats, view switch and `actions`.
- Lines: added / removed / unchanged with line numbers; changed words get a stronger highlight (`wordDiff`).
- Expander: a row standing in for hidden unchanged lines; `context` sets how many stay visible around each change.
- Empty message (optional): shown when both texts are identical.

**DiffViewer props**

- `newValue`: `string` — Changed text.
- `oldValue`: `string` — Original text.
- `actions?`: `ReactNode` — Extra header content (e.g. a copy or "apply" button), placed at the end.
- `context?`: `number`, default `3` — Unchanged lines kept around each change; longer runs collapse. `Infinity` never collapses.
- `defaultView?`: `"split" | "unified"`, default `unified` — Initial view when uncontrolled.
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `No changes (localized: diffViewer.empty)` — Shown when both texts are identical.
- `expandLabel?`: `((hiddenCount: number) => string)`, default `localized: diffViewer.expand` — Text of the expander row.
- `filename?`: `string` — New file name, shown mono in the header.
- `label?`: `string` — Accessible name of the scrollable diff region. Defaults to the filename.
- `language?`: `string` — Language hint shown as a tag in the header (no highlighting applied).
- `lineNumbers?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `oldFilename?`: `string` — Previous file name — when it differs from `filename` the header shows a rename (old → new).
- `onViewChange?`: `((view: DiffView) => void)`
- `stats?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Shows the +added −removed counter in the header.
- `view?`: `"split" | "unified"` — Controlled view.
- `viewToggle?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Renders a Unified/Split switch in the header.
- `wordDiff?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Highlights changed words inside paired lines.
- `wrap?`: `boolean` — Wraps long lines instead of scrolling horizontally. Defaults to true in split view.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The change is visible at a glance, with the exact word highlighted.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><DiffViewer oldValue={OLD} newValue={NEW} filename="config.yml" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two blocks side by side make people hunt for the difference.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
    <CodeBlock filename="before" code={OLD} copy={false} />
    <CodeBlock filename="after" code={NEW} copy={false} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Added and removed lines carry “Added:” / “Removed:” for screen readers; + and − signs back up the color.
- The diff is a named, focusable region — set `label` when there are several on a page.
- Expanders are buttons that say how many lines they reveal.
- The view switch is a named toggle group. Unified is the default: split needs width and reads poorly on narrow screens.

## DonutChart

`import { DonutChart } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/donut-chart';`

Status: stable · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-donutchart--docs

**When to use**

- Parts of one whole, up to 7: storage by environment, plan mix, traffic by source.
- When the total matters too — it sits in the center.

**When not to use**

- Comparing values that aren’t parts of a whole → use BarChart
- More than 7 parts, or many tiny slices → use BarChart, or group into “Other”
- Change over time → use AreaChart or LineChart

**Anatomy**

- Ring: slices in palette order; `thickness` default/thin.
- Center: total by default; `centerLabel`/`centerValue`.
- Legend: name and value per slice; `layout` vertical/horizontal.

**DonutChart props**

- `data`: `DonutChartSlice[]`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `centerLabel?`: `string`, default `Total (localized: chart.total)`
- `centerValue?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `format?`: `((v: number) => string)`
- `height?`: `number`, default `200`
- `layout?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `vertical`
- `legend?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `showCenter?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `thickness?`: `"default" | "thin"`, default `default` — Ring band width: "default" (thicker) or "thin" (a slim indicator ring).
- `unit?`: `string`, default ``

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Three parts of one total, named in the legend.

  ```tsx
  <DonutChart
    data={[{ label: 'Production', value: 62 }, { label: 'Staging', value: 24 }, { label: 'Dev', value: 14 }]}
    unit=" GB"
    layout="horizontal"
    height={160}
    ariaLabel="Storage by environment: production 62 GB of 100 GB."
  />
  ```

- Don’t: Seven similar slices: angles this close can’t be compared — a sorted bar chart can.

  ```tsx
  <DonutChart
    data={[
      { label: 'eu-west-1', value: 22 }, { label: 'eu-central-1', value: 18 }, { label: 'us-east-1', value: 16 },
      { label: 'us-west-2', value: 14 }, { label: 'ap-south-1', value: 11 }, { label: 'ap-southeast-1', value: 10 }, { label: 'sa-east-1', value: 9 },
    ]}
    unit="%"
    layout="horizontal"
    height={160}
    ariaLabel="Traffic by region."
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `ariaLabel` states the takeaway; the legend repeats every name and value as text.
- Slice colors aren’t the only cue — the legend order matches the ring.

## DotSeparator

`import { DotSeparator } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/dot-separator';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-dotseparator--docs

**When to use**

- Separating short inline facts on one line: “eu-west-1 · Created Mar 2026 · v2.4.0”.

**When not to use**

- Between sentences or long items → use separate lines
- Between sections → use Separator

**Anatomy**

- Dot: decorative, hidden from screen readers.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Three short facts on one line.

  ```tsx
  <p className={META}>eu-west-1<DotSeparator />Created Mar 2026<DotSeparator />v2.4.0</p>
  ```

- Don’t: Sentences joined by dots: they wrap and the dots land at line starts.

  ```tsx
  <p className={`${META} w-72 flex-wrap`}>
    Backups run nightly and are kept for 14 days<DotSeparator />Restores take up to an hour<DotSeparator />Contact support for older copies
  </p>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The dot is aria-hidden; screen readers hear the facts run together, so keep each one self-explanatory.

## Drawer

`import { Drawer, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerBody, DrawerFooter, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription, DrawerTrigger, DrawerPortal, DrawerClose, DrawerOverlay } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/drawer';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs

**When to use**

- Short, touch-first tasks from the bottom of a phone screen: sort, filters, share, a few actions.
- Content people dismiss with a swipe.

**When not to use**

- Long or multi-step forms → use a page or Dialog
- Side panels on desktop → use PushSheet
- Confirming a destructive action → use AlertDialog

**Anatomy**

- Handle: drag to dismiss; the backdrop fades with it.
- Header: `DrawerTitle` (required) and description.
- Body and footer: short content; the main action in the footer.

**Drawer props**

- `direction?`: `"end" | "start" | "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"`, default `bottom`

**DrawerContent props**

- `width?`: `"fixed" | "full"`, default `full` — Bottom/top drawers only: 'full' spans edge-to-edge (default, current behavior). 'fixed' caps the sheet at a centered max width on larger screens (sm:max-w-xl).

Also accepts the props of: WithFadeFromProps, WithoutFadeFromProps, HTMLAttributes, DialogContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, DialogContentImplProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, DialogPortalProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A few big tap targets; one tap and it’s gone.

  ```tsx
  <Drawer>
    <DrawerTrigger asChild><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Sort</Button></DrawerTrigger>
    <DrawerContent>
      <DrawerHeader>
        <DrawerTitle>Sort sites</DrawerTitle>
        <DrawerDescription>Choose an order for the list.</DrawerDescription>
      </DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerBody>
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
          {['Newest first', 'Name A–Z', 'Most traffic'].map((o) => (
            <DrawerClose key={o} asChild>
              <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="lg" className="justify-start">{o}</Button>
            </DrawerClose>
          ))}
        </div>
      </DrawerBody>
    </DrawerContent>
  </Drawer>
  ```

- Don’t: A four-step wizard in a sheet one swipe can throw away.

  ```tsx
  <Drawer>
    <DrawerTrigger asChild><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Create site</Button></DrawerTrigger>
    <DrawerContent>
      <DrawerHeader>
        <DrawerTitle>Create site — step 1 of 4</DrawerTitle>
        <DrawerDescription>Domain, plan, region, database, admin account…</DrawerDescription>
      </DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerFooter>
        <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="lg">Next</Button>
      </DrawerFooter>
    </DrawerContent>
  </Drawer>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a modal dialog: focus is trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.
- `DrawerTitle` names it; the swipe always has a button alternative (Close or an action).

## DropdownMenu

`import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuTrailing } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/dropdown-menu';`

Status: stable · Category: Menus
Docs: ./?path=/docs/menus-dropdownmenu--docs

**When to use**

- Secondary actions behind a trigger: “more actions” for a row or card, a user menu, a split button’s options.
- Settings that toggle in place: `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`.

**When not to use**

- Choosing a value for a form field → use Select
- The one or two actions people use most → use Buttons
- Navigation between pages → use NavigationMenu or links

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: a Button (often `iconOnly` with a kebab) via `asChild`.
- Content: `size` matches the trigger; `align` to the trigger’s edge.
- Items: icon, label, `DropdownMenuShortcut`; `tone="danger"` for destructive ones, last and separated.
- Groups (optional): labels, separators, submenus.

**DropdownMenuContent props**

- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xs"`, default `md`

**DropdownMenuItem props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "danger"`, default `neutral`

**DropdownMenuLabel props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

**DropdownMenuSubTrigger props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: DropdownMenuProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, MenuContentProps, MenuContentImplProps, PopperContentProps, MenuItemProps, MenuItemImplProps, MenuCheckboxItemProps, MenuRadioItemProps, MenuRadioGroupProps, MenuSubContentProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The main action stays visible; the rest sit behind a named kebab.

  ```tsx
  <div className={ROW}>
    <span>shop.seashell.dev</span>
    <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
      <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="sm">Open</Button>
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
          <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="sm" iconOnly leftIcon={<KebabIconVertical />} aria-label="More actions for shop.seashell.dev" />
        </DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
          <DropdownMenuItem>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Everything, including the most common “Open”, hidden behind “Actions”.

  ```tsx
  <div className={ROW}>
    <span>shop.seashell.dev</span>
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
        <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="sm" rightIcon={<NavArrowDown />}>Actions</Button>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
        <DropdownMenuItem>Open</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`; name icon triggers after their object (“More actions for …”).
- Enter/Space/↓ opens, arrows move, typing jumps to an item, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- Destructive items still need a confirmation or undo — a menu click is easy to mis-hit.

## Dropzone

`import { Dropzone } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/dropzone';`

Status: stable · Category: Files
Docs: ./?path=/docs/files-dropzone--docs

**When to use**

- Uploading one or several files where dragging from the desktop is common: documents, media, imports.
- Showing what’s staged (`files`), uploading (`loading`) and done (`successFile`) in one place.

**When not to use**

- A single file in a form → use File
- Showing already attached files → use Attachment

**Anatomy**

- Drop area: also a button — click or Enter opens the picker.
- Hint: `hint` — accepted formats and size limit.
- Staged list (optional): `files` with `onRemove`; per-file errors.
- States: `error`, `loading`, `successFile`, `disabled`.

**Dropzone props**

- `onFiles`: `(files: File[]) => void`
- `accept?`: `string` — Accepted types, same syntax as <input accept> (".pdf,image/*"). Applied to dropped files too, not only the picker.
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `error?`: `string`
- `files?`: `StagedFile[]`
- `hint?`: `string`
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Zone shows a spinner + "Uploading…" and becomes non-interactive. Takes priority over error/successFile while true.
- `multiple?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `onReject?`: `((files: File[]) => void)` — Called with dropped files that don't match `accept` (they are not passed to onFiles). Use it to show an error.
- `onRemove?`: `((index: number) => void)`
- `successFile?`: `{ name: string; uploadedAt: string; }` — Replaces the drag/or/Browse content with a single-file success confirmation (checkmark, name, upload date) — for single-file flows like a resume upload. Ignored while `error` is set.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Formats and size limit up front; the accept filter matches the hint.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <Dropzone aria-label="Upload documents" hint="PDF or DOCX, up to 25 MB each" accept=".pdf,.docx" onFiles={() => {}} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: No limits shown — people find them out from a failed upload.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <Dropzone aria-label="Upload documents" onFiles={() => {}} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name it with `aria-label` (“Upload documents”); it’s a button, so keyboard users never need to drag.
- Errors are announced and stay visible next to the area; per-file errors sit on the file.
- Rejected files go to `onReject` — tell people which ones and why.

## EmptyState

`import { EmptyState, EmptyStateIcon, EmptyStateTitle, EmptyStateDescription, EmptyStateActions } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/empty-state';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-emptystate--docs

**When to use**

- A list, table or section with nothing in it yet — explain what will appear and how to start.
- No results for a search or filter (`filtered`) — say so and offer to clear.

**When not to use**

- Data is still loading → use Skeleton or TableSkeleton
- Loading failed → use Alert with a retry
- A whole-page onboarding flow → use a dedicated page or Stepper

**Anatomy**

- Icon (optional): decorative, hints at the object type.
- Title: what’s empty: “No sites yet”. Use `titleAs="h2"` when it’s the main content of the region.
- Description (optional): why it matters or what will show up here.
- Action (optional): the one next step: create, import, clear filters.

**EmptyState props**

- `title`: `ReactNode`
- `action?`: `ReactNode`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `filtered?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Switch to the alternate content used when an active filter has no results.
- `filteredAction?`: `ReactNode`
- `filteredDescription?`: `ReactNode`
- `filteredIcon?`: `ReactNode`
- `filteredTitle?`: `ReactNode`
- `height?`: `Height<string | number>` — Fill the parent's height or use an explicit CSS height. Omit for content height.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`
- `titleAs?`: `ElementType`

**EmptyStateTitle props**

- `as?`: `ElementType`
- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Says what will be here and gives the first step.

  ```tsx
  <EmptyState
    className="w-80"
    icon={<Globe />}
    title="No sites yet"
    description="Create a site to get a domain, SSL and backups."
    action={<Button>Create site</Button>}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: “No data” — is it broken, loading, or just empty?

  ```tsx
  <EmptyState className="w-80" title="No data" />
  ```

- Do: For a search, show the query and a way out.

  ```tsx
  <EmptyState
    className="w-80"
    icon={<Search />}
    title="No results for “shp”"
    description="Check the spelling or clear the filters."
    action={<Button appearance="tonal" tone="secondary">Clear filters</Button>}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: The “first time” state shown for a filter with no matches.

  ```tsx
  <EmptyState className="w-80" icon={<Globe />} title="No sites yet" action={<Button>Create site</Button>} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The icon is decorative; the title carries the meaning.
- When results drop to zero after typing or filtering, announce the count in a live region — the empty state itself isn’t one.
- One primary action at most; a second option goes in as a link or tonal button.

## Fab

`import { Fab, FabSpeedDial } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/fab';`

Status: beta · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-fab--docs

**When to use**

- The one main action of a screen that must stay reachable while scrolling, mostly on mobile: “New message”, “Add site”.
- Extended (with `label`) when the icon alone isn’t obvious.

**When not to use**

- Secondary or destructive actions
- Screens with more than one equally important action → use Button in the page header or StickyActionBar
- Desktop pages where the action fits in the header → use Button
- Two to five related create actions behind one button → use FabSpeedDial

**Anatomy**

- Container: pill (extended) or circle; `size` sm/md/lg, `tone`, `appearance`.
- Icon: always shown.
- Label (optional): makes it extended; with `collapseOnScroll` it folds while scrolling down.

**Fab props**

- `icon`: `ReactNode` — The action's icon. Always shown.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `filled`
- `collapsed?`: `boolean` — Force the folded state (controlled), e.g. collapse while a sheet is open.
- `collapseOnScroll?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Fold the extended FAB to the round one while scrolling down, unfold on scroll up.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` — Text for the extended FAB. Without it the FAB is round and icon-only (pass `aria-label`).
- `position?`: `"none" | "bottom-end" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-center"`, default `bottom-end` — Where it's pinned. `none` renders it in normal flow.
- `scrollContainer?`: `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` — Scroll container to watch for `collapseOnScroll`. Defaults to the window.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — sm 40px, md 56px (default), lg 64px.
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "primary" | "secondary"`, default `primary`

**FabSpeedDial props**

- `actions`: `FabSpeedDialAction[]` — Two to five related actions. More than three stack in a column.
- `className?`: `string`
- `closeLabel?`: `string`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — The closed FAB's icon; it turns 45° into a close. Default: a plus.
- `openLabel?`: `string` — Accessible names of the trigger. Default "Open actions" / "Close actions".
- `position?`: `"none" | "bottom-end" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-center"`, default `bottom-end`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "primary" | "secondary"`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One FAB, the screen’s main action, with a label.

  ```tsx
  <Fab position="none" icon={<Plus />} label="New site" />
  ```

- Don’t: Two FABs compete, and two plus icons say nothing.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-3">
    <Fab position="none" icon={<Plus />} aria-label="Add" />
    <Fab position="none" icon={<Plus />} aria-label="Import" tone="secondary" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Icon-only needs `aria-label`. When it collapses on scroll the label stays in the DOM, so the name doesn’t change.
- It floats over content: keep the bottom of the page reachable (pad the content by the FAB’s height).
- Tab order follows the DOM, not the position on screen — place it where it makes sense to reach it.

## FeedbackWidget

`import { FeedbackWidget } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/feedback-widget';`

Status: beta · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-feedbackwidget--docs

**When to use**

- “Was this helpful?” at the end of a help article, a docs page or an AI answer.
- A compact version under a chat answer (`size="sm"`).

**When not to use**

- Rating a product, order or support case → use Rating or a survey
- Collecting bug reports → use a form or a support channel
- Mid-task, while people are busy → use ask after the task is done

**Anatomy**

- Question: about this exact content.
