- Yes / No: toggle buttons; the vote is sent right away (`onVote`).
- Follow-up (optional): reason chips + comment after “No” (or “Yes” with `askOnPositive`); optional, sent with `onSubmit`.
- Thank-you: replaces the widget when done.

**FeedbackWidget props**

- `askOnPositive?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Also ask a follow-up after "Yes". Default false: a yes is just thanked.
- `className?`: `string`
- `noLabel?`: `string`, default `No (localized: feedbackWidget.no)`
- `onSubmit?`: `((details: FeedbackDetails) => void)` — Fires when the follow-up is sent.
- `onVote?`: `((vote: FeedbackVote) => void)` — Fires as soon as Yes or No is clicked.
- `positiveReasons?`: `string[]`, default `['Accurate', 'Easy to follow', 'Solved my problem']` — Reason chips after "Yes" — only when `askOnPositive`.
- `question?`: `string`, default `Was this page helpful? (localized: feedbackWidget.question)`
- `reasons?`: `string[]`, default `['Inaccurate', 'Hard to understand', 'Missing information', 'Didn’t solve my problem']` — Reason chips offered after "No". Empty array = comment only.
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `thankYou?`: `string`, default `Thanks for your feedback. (localized: feedbackWidget.thanks)`
- `yesLabel?`: `string`, default `Yes (localized: feedbackWidget.yes)`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One question about this page, answered in one click.

  ```tsx
  <FeedbackWidget question="Did this article solve your problem?" />
  ```

- Don’t: A product-wide question under one article gives answers nobody can act on.

  ```tsx
  <FeedbackWidget question="How satisfied are you with our hosting overall?" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Yes / No have visible labels and report their state (aria-pressed).
- When the follow-up opens, focus moves into it; after finishing, focus returns to the chosen vote.
- The thank-you is a polite live region.

## Field

`import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/field';`

Status: stable · Category: Form Structure
Docs: ./?path=/docs/form-structure-field--docs

**When to use**

- Stacking a Label, a control, a description and an error for controls that don’t draw them themselves (Select, Combobox, DatePicker, custom).

**When not to use**

- TextField / TextArea — label, description and error are built in → use their own props
- react-hook-form forms → use Form (FormItem wires ids for you)

**Anatomy**

- Field: vertical stack, 8px gap; `invalid`, `required`, `disabled` as data attributes.
- Label: the shared Label, with `htmlFor`.
- Control: gets `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` from you.
- FieldDescription / FieldError (optional): help text, then the error (announced).

**Field props**

- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `invalid?`: `boolean`
- `required?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The error is text under the control and linked to it.

  ```tsx
  <Field invalid className="w-64">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-fd-plan" required>Plan</Label>
    <Select>
      <SelectTrigger id="gl-fd-plan" error widthSize="full" aria-describedby="gl-fd-plan-err" aria-invalid>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a plan" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {PLANS.map((p) => (
          <SelectItem key={p} value={p.toLowerCase()}>{p}</SelectItem>
        ))}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
    <FieldError id="gl-fd-plan-err">Choose a plan to continue.</FieldError>
  </Field>
  ```

- Don’t: Only a red border: nothing says what’s wrong, and screen readers hear nothing.

  ```tsx
  <Field className="w-64">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-fd-plan2" required>Plan</Label>
    <Select>
      <SelectTrigger id="gl-fd-plan2" error widthSize="full" aria-invalid>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a plan" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {PLANS.map((p) => (
          <SelectItem key={p} value={p.toLowerCase()}>{p}</SelectItem>
        ))}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
    <FieldDescription>You can change it later.</FieldDescription>
  </Field>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Field doesn’t wire ids — pass `id`, `aria-describedby` (description + error ids) and `aria-invalid` to the control yourself.
- `FieldError` is `role="alert"`: render it only when there is an error.

## Fieldset

`import { Fieldset } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/fieldset';`

Status: stable · Category: Form Structure
Docs: ./?path=/docs/form-structure-fieldset--docs

**When to use**

- Grouping related controls under one name: an address, notification settings, a section of a long form.
- `disabled` on the fieldset to switch off a whole group at once.

**When not to use**

- A single field → use Label or the field’s own label
- Visual grouping only, nothing to name → use spacing or Separator
- A group of checkboxes as one value → use CheckboxGroup

**Anatomy**

- Legend: `legend` — section title style (body-l, semibold).
- Description (optional): one line under the legend.
- Content: controls stacked with a 16px gap.

**Fieldset props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Supporting line below the legend.
- `legend?`: `ReactNode` — Group caption, rendered as the <legend>.

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One legend for related settings — read with each switch.

  ```tsx
  <Fieldset legend="Email notifications" description="Sent to dana@seashell.dev." className="w-72">
    <Switch label="Weekly report" defaultChecked />
    <Switch label="Billing alerts" defaultChecked />
    <Switch label="Product news" />
  </Fieldset>
  ```

- Don’t: A fieldset around one field: the name is said twice.

  ```tsx
  <Fieldset legend="Email" className="w-72">
    <TextField label="Email" widthSize="full" />
  </Fieldset>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Screen readers announce the legend when focus enters the group.
- Native `disabled` cascades to every control inside.
- Don’t nest fieldsets more than one level — legends pile up in announcements.

## File

`import { File } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/file';`

Status: stable · Category: Files
Docs: ./?path=/docs/files-file--docs

**When to use**

- One file in a form: a logo, a certificate, a document to attach.
- Showing the current file and letting people replace it.

**When not to use**

- Several files at once, or drag and drop is the main way in → use Dropzone
- Just displaying an attached file → use Attachment
- An image that needs framing → use File + ImageCropper

**Anatomy**

- Empty tile: dashed, with `pickLabel` and `pickHint` (formats, size).
- Filled slot: the file as an Attachment; clicking replaces it (`replaceLabel` on hover/focus).
- Native input: the file lives in a real input, so a plain form submits it (`inputProps.name`).

**File props**

- `accept?`: `string`
- `actions?`: `ReactNode`
- `className?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `empty?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Starts the slot without file metadata (the dashed "add" tile).
- `error?`: `string`
- `href?`: `string` — Turns the name into a real link, its ::after stretched over the whole surface as the hit target.
- `inputProps?`: `InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>`
- `meta?`: `ReactNode` — Secondary metadata, e.g. "Modified today".
- `mimeLabels?`: `Record<string, string>`
- `name?`: `string` — Initial file name inherited from Attachment.
- `onFileChange?`: `((file: File | null) => void)`
- `pickHint?`: `ReactNode` — Optional secondary line under pickLabel in the empty tile, e.g. "PNG or JPG, up to 25 MB".
- `pickLabel?`: `string`, default `Add file (localized: file.pick)` — Label shown in the empty (dashed) tile. Default "Add file".
- `previewUrl?`: `string`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Presentation-only: the input remains mounted but cannot be activated.
- `replaceLabel?`: `string`, default `Replace file (localized: file.replace)` — Shown on hover/keyboard focus of a filled, clickable slot, and read as its description — says that a click picks a new file in place of this one. Default "Replace file".
- `selected?`: `boolean` — Marks the file as picked — a ring on top of the hover fill, plus `aria-current` on a link.
- `showKind?`: `boolean`
- `showMeta?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `number` — Initial byte size inherited from Attachment.
- `type?`: `string`
- `variant?`: `"line" | "row" | "pill" | "card"`, default `card`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One file, one compact slot that says what it accepts.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-56">
    <File empty pickLabel="Add logo" pickHint="SVG or PNG, up to 2 MB" inputProps={{ name: 'gl-logo', accept: 'image/svg+xml,image/png' }} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A full dropzone for a single logo takes the space of the whole form.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <Dropzone aria-label="Upload logo" multiple={false} hint="SVG or PNG, up to 2 MB" onFiles={() => {}} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The empty tile is a button named by pickLabel + pickHint; the filled slot is named by the file name.
- After picking, focus moves to the file; after removing, back to the tile.
- Always say the limits in `pickHint` — the native picker won’t.

## Filter

`import { Filter } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/filter';`

Status: stable · Category: Search & Filter
Docs: ./?path=/docs/search-filter-filter--docs

**When to use**

- Narrowing a list or table by a few facets: status, region, owner.
- Several values per facet, with counts per option.

**When not to use**

- Many attributes plus keyword search → use FilterField
- Arbitrary conditions (greater than, between, any/all) → use QueryBuilder
- A value in a form → use Select, CheckboxGroup or Combobox

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: facet name; with a selection shows the count (“Status, 2”); `heightSize` sm/md/lg.
- Popover: checkbox options with counts; `searchable` for long lists.
- Clear: back to “no filter”.

**Filter props**

- `label`: `string` — The facet name shown on the trigger, e.g. "Status".
- `options`: `FilterOption[]`
- `align?`: `"center" | "end" | "start"`, default `start`
- `defaultValue?`: `string[]`
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — Trigger height (and search-field height, when `searchable`) — matches TextField/Select/Toggle/Button's shared scale. sm 32px, body-s | md (default) 40px, body-m | lg 48px, body-m.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string[]) => void)`
- `searchable?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show a search box above the list (for facets with many options).
- `value?`: `string[]`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One trigger per facet; several values each; counts say how many match.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
    <Filter label="Status" options={STATUS} defaultValue={['active']} />
    <Filter label="Region" options={REGION} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A select as a filter: one status at a time and a fake “All” option.

  ```tsx
  <Select defaultValue="all">
    <SelectTrigger widthSize="md" aria-label="Status">
      <SelectValue />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem value="all">All statuses</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="active">Active</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="suspended">Suspended</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="pending">Pending</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The trigger is a button whose name includes the selection count (“Status, 1 selected”).
- Options are a named checkbox group; Space toggles.
- Announce the new result count on the page when filters change.

## FilterField

`import { FilterField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/filter-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Search & Filter
Docs: ./?path=/docs/search-filter-filterfield--docs

**When to use**

- Keyword search and filtering by many attributes in one field: servers, logs, users.
- Applied filters should stay visible and editable as chips.

**When not to use**

- Two or three facets → use Filter
- Nested any/all logic → use QueryBuilder

**Anatomy**

- Input: free text searches; focusing it lists the attributes.
- Step two: the chosen attribute’s editor: options, text with operator, date or number range.
- Chips: one per applied filter; click to edit, × to remove.

**FilterField props**

- `attributes`: `FilterAttribute[]`
- `addLabel?`: `string`, default `Add filter (localized: filterField.add)`
- `align?`: `"center" | "end" | "start"`, default `start`
- `applyLabel?`: `string`, default `Apply (localized: filterField.apply)`
- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `attributeLabel?`: `string`, default `Filter by… (localized: filterField.attribute)`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultQuery?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `AppliedFilter[]`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `emptyMessage?`: `string`, default `No attributes. (localized: filterField.noAttributes)`
- `id?`: `string`
- `inputClassName?`: `string`
- `onQueryChange?`: `((query: string) => void)`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: AppliedFilter[]) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Filter or search… (localized: filterField.placeholder)`
- `query?`: `string`
- `searchLabel?`: `string`, default `Search for (localized: filterField.searchFor)` — Lead-in for the free-text search row in the dropdown ("Search for" "query"). Defaults to the locale's `filterField.searchFor`.
- `value?`: `AppliedFilter[]`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Five attributes and search in one field; what’s applied is visible as chips.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96 max-w-full">
    <FilterField attributes={ATTRS} defaultValue={[{ key: 'status', value: 'active' }]} aria-label="Filter servers" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A trigger per attribute: the bar wraps, and names and dates get squeezed into checkboxes.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-96 max-w-full flex-wrap gap-2">
    <Filter label="Name" options={opts(['web-01', 'web-02'])} />
    <Filter label="Status" options={opts(['Active', 'Suspended'])} />
    <Filter label="Region" options={opts(['Europe', 'Americas'])} />
    <Filter label="Created" options={opts(['Today', 'This week'])} />
    <Filter label="CPU cores" options={opts(['2', '4'])} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The input is a `combobox` named with `aria-label`; attributes are a listbox.
- Each chip is a button named “Status: Active” with a separate remove button.
- Focus moves into step two when it opens and back to the input when a filter is applied.

## Form

`import { Form, FormItem, FormLabel, FormControl, FormDescription, FormMessage, FormField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/form';`

Status: stable · Category: Form Structure
Docs: ./?path=/docs/form-structure-form--docs

**When to use**

- Forms with validation on react-hook-form: FormField per control, FormItem with FormLabel, FormDescription and FormMessage.
- Any form where errors must be tied to fields automatically.

**When not to use**

- One or two fields with no validation logic → use TextField / Field directly
- Editing an object’s properties in a side panel → use PropertyGrid

**Anatomy**

- Form: RHF’s FormProvider around a native form.
- FormField: a typed Controller for one value.
- FormItem: gives `FormLabel`, `FormControl`, `FormDescription`, `FormMessage` shared ids.
- FormMessage: the field’s error, linked and announced.

**FormLabel props**

- `data-error?`: `boolean`
- `optional?`: `boolean`
- `required?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, LabelHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The error sits under the field it’s about and says how to fix it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-4">
    <TextField label="Domain" defaultValue="seashell" error="Add the ending, like .dev or .com." widthSize="full" />
    <TextField label="Admin email" defaultValue="dana@seashell.dev" widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Only a banner on top: which field, and what’s wrong with it?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-4">
    <Alert tone="danger">
      <WarningCircle />
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
        <AlertTitle>Form has errors</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>Please check the fields below.</AlertDescription>
      </div>
    </Alert>
    <TextField label="Domain" defaultValue="seashell" widthSize="full" />
    <TextField label="Admin email" defaultValue="dana@seashell.dev" widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `FormControl` sets `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` on the control for you.
- Switch, Checkbox and Radio render buttons — `FormLabel`’s htmlFor may not name them; add `aria-label`.
- On submit with errors, move focus to the first invalid field.

## HelpIcon

`import { HelpIcon } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/help-icon';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-helpicon--docs

**When to use**

- One line of optional background next to a label, a column header or a stat: what a term means, why a setting exists.

**When not to use**

- Instructions needed to fill a field → use the field’s description
- Long explanations or links → use a description, Popover or docs link

**Anatomy**

- Button: a “?” glyph; `size` sm (inline, one line tall) or md (30px standalone); `label` names it.
- Tooltip: children — one short line.

**HelpIcon props**

- `align?`: `"center" | "end" | "start"`
- `contentClassName?`: `string`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`, default `<HelpCircle />`
- `label?`: `string`
- `side?`: `"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"`, default `top`
- `sideOffset?`: `number`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm" | null`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Background people may want, not need.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-hi-renew">
      Auto-renew window
      <HelpIcon label="About the renew window">Renewal runs this many days before expiry.</HelpIcon>
    </Label>
    <TextField id="gl-hi-renew" defaultValue="30" widthSize="sm" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Rules people must follow, hidden behind “?” — they belong under the field.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-hi-pass">
      Password
      <HelpIcon label="Password rules">At least 12 characters, one number, one symbol, not one of your last 5.</HelpIcon>
    </Label>
    <TextField id="gl-hi-pass" type="password" widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a button named by label; the hint opens on focus too and is linked as its description.
- Doesn’t open on touch — never the only place for required information.

## HoldToTalk

`import { HoldToTalk } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/hold-to-talk';`

Status: beta · Category: AI & Chat
Docs: ./?path=/docs/ai-chat-holdtotalk--docs

**When to use**

- Voice input in a prompt or chat composer, where speaking replaces typing for one message.

**When not to use**

- Long dictation or a recorder with pause and review → use a toggle Button (Record / Stop)
- Anything that isn’t voice → use Button

**Anatomy**

- Button: a round microphone button.
- Waveform: appears while held; the button grows into a pill.

**HoldToTalk props**

- `label?`: `string` — Accessible name. Default "Hold to talk".
- `onCancel?`: `(() => void)` — Escape, or the pointer slid off the button before release: discard.
- `onHoldEnd?`: `(() => void)` — Released normally: send what was recorded.
- `onHoldStart?`: `(() => void)`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: In the composer’s trailing slot, next to Send.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-solid border-[var(--color-border-border)] px-3 py-1.5 font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-subtler)]">
    <span className="flex-1">Ask anything…</span>
    <HoldToTalk />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A name that hides how it works — say “Hold to talk”, so the press-and-hold is announced.

  ```tsx
  <HoldToTalk label="Record" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Space or Enter held down works like a held pointer; Escape cancels.
- aria-pressed while held, and “Release to send” is announced once.
- Recording is yours: start it in onHoldStart, send in onHoldEnd, discard in onCancel.

## HoverCard

`import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/hover-card';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-hovercard--docs

**When to use**

- A quick preview of what a link points to — a user, a site, a ticket — that people could also get by clicking.

**When not to use**

- Anything people must reach on touch → use Popover
- A short label for an icon → use Tooltip
- Actions or forms → use Popover or DropdownMenu

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: a real link or button whose own action works without the card.
- Content: a small read-only card, shown after a delay on hover or focus.

Also accepts the props of: HoverCardProps, HoverCardContentProps, HoverCardContentImplProps, HTMLAttributes, PopperContentProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Hover or focus the link for a preview; clicking still opens the site.

  ```tsx
  <HoverCard>
    <HoverCardTrigger asChild><Link href="#gl-hc" size="md" className="font-mono">shop.seashell.dev</Link></HoverCardTrigger>
    <HoverCardContent>
      <p className="font-mono text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">shop.seashell.dev</p>
      <p className="mt-1 font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtler)]">Running · eu-west-1 · 184,320 requests today</p>
    </HoverCardContent>
  </HoverCard>
  ```

- Don’t: Actions that appear only on hover: unreachable on touch, and gone as the pointer moves.

  ```tsx
  <HoverCard>
    <HoverCardTrigger asChild><Link href="#gl-hc" size="md" className="font-mono">api.seashell.dev</Link></HoverCardTrigger>
    <HoverCardContent>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="sm">Restart</Button>
        <Button appearance="outlined" tone="danger" size="sm">Stop</Button>
      </div>
    </HoverCardContent>
  </HoverCard>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Opens on keyboard focus too, but screen readers don’t announce it — nothing in it may be missing elsewhere.
- Keep it read-only: no buttons, inputs or links inside.

## ImageCropper

`import { ImageCropper } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/image-cropper';`

Status: beta · Category: Files
Docs: ./?path=/docs/files-imagecropper--docs

**When to use**

- Framing an uploaded image before saving: avatar, logo, cover, product photo.
- The output has a fixed shape (`aspect`, `shape="circle"`).

**When not to use**

- Images shown at their own proportions → use upload as is (File)
- Editing: filters, drawing, annotations → use a dedicated editor

**Anatomy**

- Frame: fixed and centered; the image moves under it and always covers it.
- Grid (optional): `grid`: always, while interacting, or never.
- Controls (optional): zoom slider and rotate (`controls`, `rotatable`).
- Output: `onCropChange` + `getCroppedImage()` → a Blob to upload.

**ImageCropper props**

- `src`: `string`
- `aspect?`: `number`, default `1` — Width / height of the crop frame. 1 for avatars, 16 / 9 for covers.
- `controls?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Shows the zoom slider and rotate button under the image.
- `defaultZoom?`: `number`, default `1`
- `grid?`: `"always" | "interaction" | "never"`, default `interaction` — Rule-of-thirds lines inside the frame: always, only while moving, or never.
- `label?`: `string`, default `Crop area (localized: imageCropper.label)` — Accessible name of the crop area.
- `maxZoom?`: `number`, default `4`
- `minZoom?`: `number`, default `1` — Zoom range, relative to "image just covers the frame".
- `onCropChange?`: `((crop: CropState) => void)` — Fires on every change (drag, zoom, rotate, resize).
- `rotatable?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Shows the rotate button.
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "rect"`, default `rect` — `circle` masks the frame round (the output is still the square).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A square photo for a 16:9 cover: people choose which part goes in the frame.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <ImageCropper src="/asset-examples/panda-avatar.png" aspect={16 / 9} label="Crop cover image" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Saved as uploaded and stretched to the cover’s shape.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <img
      src="/asset-examples/panda-avatar.png"
      alt="Cover image, a square photo stretched to 16:9"
      className="aspect-video w-full rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-lg)] object-fill"
    />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name it with `label`; the frame is focusable — arrows pan, + / − zoom.
- The zoom slider and rotate button are real controls with names, for people who can’t drag or pinch.
- Give the result a meaningful alt where it’s shown.

## InlineEdit

`import { InlineEdit } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/inline-edit';`

Status: beta · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-inlineedit--docs

**When to use**

- Renaming one value where it’s shown: a site name, a page title, a note.
- Values people change now and then, not every time they visit.

**When not to use**

- Several related fields saved together → use a form with Save
- Values that need confirmation or have consequences (a domain, an email) → use a dialog or a form
- Something people edit all the time → use an always-visible TextField

**Anatomy**

- Display: the value as text, in the exact place and size the field will take.
- Field: TextField (or TextArea with `multiline`) while editing.
- Save / Cancel: small buttons next to the field.
- Error (optional): from `validate` or a rejected `onSave`; the field stays open.

**InlineEdit props**

- `label`: `string` — Accessible name of the value, e.g. "Site name". Used for the field and the "Edit …" hint.
- `autoComplete?`: `string` — Passed to the input while editing (e.g. "off", "email").
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`, default `` — Uncontrolled starting value.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `inheritFont?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Take the surrounding typography (e.g. inside an <h1>) instead of the field's own type step. Single-line only.
- `multiline?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Multi-line text: TextArea while editing, line breaks kept on display. Enter adds a line, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter saves.
- `onSave?`: `((value: string) => void | Promise<void>)` — Called with the new value. Return a promise to show a saving state;
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Add a value (localized: inlineEdit.placeholder)` — Shown in place of an empty value.
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Not editable: plain text, no hover, no edit hint.
- `saveOnBlur?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Save when focus leaves the field. Default true.
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md` — Text step for the default and multiline treatments. Ignored with `inheritFont`.
- `validate?`: `((value: string) => string)` — Return an error message to block saving, or undefined when the value is fine.
- `value?`: `string` — Controlled value. Update it from `onSave`.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One value, edited where it’s read.

  ```tsx
  <InlineEdit label="Site name" defaultValue="Seashell shop" />
  ```

- Don’t: A set of fields each saving on its own is a form in disguise — people won’t know what’s saved.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <TextField label="Site name" defaultValue="Seashell shop" widthSize="full" />
    <TextField label="Domain" defaultValue="seashell.shop" widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The display is a button named “Edit {label}”; `label` is required.
- Enter saves (⌘/Ctrl+Enter in multiline), Escape cancels; focus returns to the text afterwards.
- A failed save keeps what was typed and shows why.

## InputGroup

`import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/input-group';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-inputgroup--docs

**When to use**

- A fixed prefix or suffix that is part of the value’s format: https://, .theya.app, /mo, GB.
- A button that belongs to the field, inside its border.

**When not to use**

- Just an icon → use TextField leftIcon / rightIcon
- A unit people can change → use TextField + Select next to it
- Search with suggestions → use Autocomplete

**Anatomy**

- Container: one border and one focus ring for the whole group.
- Addon: `position` start/end, optional `divider`.
- Input: borderless; the container draws the border.

**InputGroupAddon props**

- `divider?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `position?`: `"end" | "start"`, default `start`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The fixed part is shown, not typed.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-ig-sub">Subdomain</Label>
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupInput id="gl-ig-sub" defaultValue="shop" />
      <InputGroupAddon position="end">.theya.app</InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Asking people to type the fixed part invites typos.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Subdomain" defaultValue="shop.theya.app" widthSize="md" description="Must end with .theya.app" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Label the input itself (htmlFor its id). The addon is visible text, not part of the name — repeat it in the description if it matters.
- Errors go on the input (aria-invalid + described message) — the group shows them together.

## InputOTP

`import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSlot, InputOTPSeparator } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/input-otp';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-inputotp--docs

**When to use**

- A one-time code of known length from an SMS, email or authenticator app.

**When not to use**

- Codes of varying length, or recovery codes with dashes → use TextField
- Anything that isn’t a code (PINs people set themselves) → use Password

**Anatomy**

- Input: one real input under the slots; `maxLength`, `pattern`, `inputMode`.
- Slots: one per character, grouped like the code is shown (3 + 3).
- Help / error text: linked with aria-describedby.

**InputOTP props**

- `containerClassName?`: `string`

**InputOTPSlot props**

- `index`: `number`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One field under the hood: paste and autofill fill every slot.

  ```tsx
  <InputOTP maxLength={6} inputMode="numeric" aria-label="Verification code">
    <InputOTPGroup>
      {[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((i) => (
        <InputOTPSlot key={i} index={i} />
      ))}
    </InputOTPGroup>
  </InputOTP>
  ```

- Don’t: Separate fields break paste, autofill and Backspace.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((i) => (
      <TextField key={i} aria-label={`Digit ${i + 1}`} widthSize="sm" />
    ))}
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Set `autoComplete="one-time-code"` and `inputMode="numeric"` for digits.
- Put `aria-invalid` on InputOTP itself and describe the error in text — the red border alone isn’t enough.

## Kanban

`import { Kanban, KanbanCard } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/kanban';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-kanban--docs

**When to use**

- Work moving through stages: tickets, a deploy pipeline, content review.
- Watching load per stage with WIP limits (`limit`).

**When not to use**

- An on / off state → use Switch in a list
- Ordering one list → use a sortable list
- Many fields per item to compare → use DataTable grouped by status
- Work planned in time → use Scheduler

**Anatomy**

- Column: title, status dot (`tone`), count, optional WIP limit and actions.
- Card: `KanbanCard` — eyebrow, title, description, footer — or your own.
- Drop placeholder: where the card will land.
- Column footer (optional): “Add card” and similar.

**Kanban props**

- `columns`: `KanbanColumn[]`
- `items`: `T[]`
- `renderItem`: `(item: T, state: { overlay: boolean; }) => ReactNode`
- `columnWidth?`: `string | number`, default `288` — Column width.
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `No items (localized: kanban.empty)` — Shown in an empty column.
- `getItemLabel?`: `((item: T) => string)`, default `(item) => item.id` — Text used for screen-reader announcements ("Picked up <label>").
- `label?`: `string`, default `Board (localized: kanban.label)` — Accessible name of the board.
- `onItemsChange?`: `((items: T[], move: KanbanMove) => void)` — Called on drop with the reordered array and what moved.
- `renderColumnActions?`: `((column: KanbanColumn) => ReactNode)` — Extra content in a column header, after the counter (e.g. an add button).
- `renderColumnFooter?`: `((column: KanbanColumn) => ReactNode)` — Content at the bottom of a column (e.g. "Add card").

**KanbanCard props**

- `title`: `ReactNode`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `eyebrow?`: `ReactNode` — Small row above the title (e.g. an ID or a tag).
- `footer?`: `ReactNode` — Bottom row (assignee, due date, counters).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Stages of real work, with a limit where it piles up.

  ```tsx
  <Board columns={FLOW} items={TASKS} />
  ```

- Don’t: Two columns for on / off — dragging to toggle is slower than a switch.

  ```tsx
  <Board columns={TOGGLE} items={FEATURES} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Keyboard: Tab to a card, Space to pick up, arrows to move (←/→ between columns), Space to drop, Esc to cancel.
- Each move is announced with the card and column names — set `getItemLabel`.
- Offer a non-drag way too (a “Move to…” menu on the card) for people who can’t drag.
- Over the limit, the count turns danger and says so in text.

## Kbd

`import { Kbd } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/kbd';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-kbd--docs

**When to use**

- Showing a keyboard key or shortcut in text, menus, tooltips and help: ⌘ K, Esc, ?.

**When not to use**

- Code or command-line text → use inline code
- A list of all shortcuts → use KeyboardShortcuts

**Anatomy**

- Key: one Kbd per key; combinations are several Kbd side by side.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One cap per key, inside a sentence that says what it does.

  ```tsx
  <p className={TEXT}>Press <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> <Kbd>K</Kbd> to search.</p>
  ```

- Don’t: A whole phrase in one cap — the key styling stops meaning “a key”.

  ```tsx
  <p className={TEXT}>Press <Kbd>Command + K on Mac or Control + K on Windows</Kbd> to search.</p>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Kbd only shows the shortcut; the shortcut must actually work and be described in text.
- Symbols like ⌘ are read inconsistently — add the word in surrounding text for important shortcuts.

## KebabIcon

`import { KebabIconVertical, KebabIconHorizontal } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/kebab-icon';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-kebabicon--docs

**When to use**

- The trigger of an overflow menu: “more actions” for a row, a card or a toolbar.
- Vertical in rows and cards, horizontal in toolbars and headers — keep one per context.

**When not to use**

- Hiding the one or two actions people use most — show them as buttons
- A truncated path or pagination gap → use BreadcrumbEllipsis / PaginationEllipsis

**Anatomy**

- Glyph: `KebabIconVertical` or `KebabIconHorizontal`, `size` sm/md/lg; inherits the text color.
- Button: always inside an icon-only Button that opens the menu.

**KebabIconVertical props**

- `className?`: `string`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — Icon size: sm (12px) / md (16px, default — matches the previous fixed 16×16) / lg (20px).

**KebabIconHorizontal props**

- `className?`: `string`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — Icon size: sm (12px) / md (16px, default — matches the previous fixed 16×16) / lg (20px).

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Inside a real button, named for what it’s about.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md" iconOnly leftIcon={<KebabIconVertical />} aria-label="More actions for seashell.shop" />
  ```

- Don’t: A bare icon isn’t a control — no focus, no name, no keyboard.

  ```tsx
  <span className="text-[var(--color-icon-icon-subtle)]"><KebabIconHorizontal /></span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The icon is decorative; the button carries the name: “More actions for seashell.shop”.
- The menu it opens is a DropdownMenu, so arrow keys and Escape work.

## KeyboardShortcuts

`import { KeyboardShortcuts } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/keyboard-shortcuts';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-keyboardshortcuts--docs

**When to use**

- A help dialog listing an app’s shortcuts, opened from a menu or with “?”.

**When not to use**

- One shortcut next to its action → use Kbd in the menu item or tooltip

**Anatomy**

- Groups: `groups`, each with a `heading`: Navigation, Actions…
- Row: description and `keys` (“then” for sequences).
- Hotkey (optional): `hotkey` (e.g. “?”); `scopeRef` limits it to a work area (WCAG 2.1.4).

**KeyboardShortcuts props**

- `groups`: `ShortcutGroup[]`
- `defaultOpen?`: `boolean`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `gap?`: `"none" | "md" | "sm"` — Spacing between the header, body, and footer sections: `md` (default), `sm`, or `none`.
- `hotkey?`: `string`
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `open?`: `boolean`
- `scopeRef?`: `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
- `showCloseButton?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"md" | "full" | null`
- `title?`: `ReactNode`, default `Keyboard shortcuts (localized: keyboardShortcuts.title)`
- `trigger?`: `ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, DialogContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, DialogContentImplProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Grouped by task, so people scan to the part they need.

  ```tsx
  <KeyboardShortcuts
    trigger={<Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Grouped shortcuts</Button>}
    groups={[
      { heading: 'Navigation', shortcuts: [{ keys: ['G', 'then', 'S'], description: 'Go to Sites' }, { keys: ['/'], description: 'Search' }] },
      { heading: 'Actions', shortcuts: [{ keys: ['N'], description: 'New site' }, { keys: ['?'], description: 'Show shortcuts' }] },
    ]}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: One ungrouped list in no order — fine for 3 shortcuts, not for 30.

  ```tsx
  <KeyboardShortcuts
    trigger={<Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">One long list</Button>}
    groups={[
      {
        shortcuts: [
          { keys: ['N'], description: 'New site' },
          { keys: ['/'], description: 'Search' },
          { keys: ['G', 'then', 'S'], description: 'Go to Sites' },
          { keys: ['E'], description: 'Edit' },
          { keys: ['?'], description: 'Show shortcuts' },
          { keys: ['G', 'then', 'B'], description: 'Go to Billing' },
        ],
      },
    ]}
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A single-character hotkey must be scoped or switchable (WCAG 2.1.4) — pass scopeRef.
- The hotkey is ignored while typing in a field.
- Keys are read as text, in order (“G then S”).

## Label

`import { Label } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/label';`

Status: stable · Category: Form Structure
Docs: ./?path=/docs/form-structure-label--docs

**When to use**

- Naming any form control that doesn’t draw its own label — Select, Combobox, DatePicker, NumberField, custom controls.
- Marking required (`required`, red *) and optional (`optional`, “(optional)”) fields.

**When not to use**

- TextField and TextArea — they take a label prop → use TextField label
- A group of controls → use Fieldset legend
- Plain text that names nothing → use a heading or text

**Anatomy**

- Text: short, a noun (“Domain”), not an instruction (“Enter your domain”).
- Required mark (optional): red *, hidden from screen readers — the control carries required itself.
- Optional mark (optional): “(optional)” in subtler text.

**Label props**

- `data-error?`: `boolean`
- `optional?`: `boolean`
- `required?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, LabelHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Both kinds marked: required with *, optional with “(optional)”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-4">
    <TextField label="Email" required widthSize="full" />
    <TextField label="Company" optional widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: No marks in a long form: people find out what’s required from the errors.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-4">
    <TextField label="Email" widthSize="full" />
    <TextField label="Company" widthSize="full" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Connect it: `htmlFor` on the label, the same `id` on the control. Clicking the label focuses the control.
- Radix controls that render a button (Switch, Checkbox) may also need `aria-label` — check the name in the a11y panel.
- Short all-required forms (sign-in) can skip both marks.

## Lightbox

`import { Lightbox } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/lightbox';`

Status: beta · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-lightbox--docs

**When to use**

- Looking closely at images — screenshots, product photos, attachments — and moving through a set.

**When not to use**

- Small images that are already readable → use show them inline
- Non-image content → use Dialog

**Anatomy**

- Image: fit to screen; click or +/− to zoom, drag to pan.
- Controls: previous/next, counter, close; caption under the image.
- Thumbnails (optional): `thumbnails` strip for a set.

**Lightbox props**

- `images`: `LightboxImage[]`
- `onOpenChange`: `(open: boolean) => void`
- `open`: `boolean`
- `defaultIndex?`: `number`, default `0` — Uncontrolled starting image.
- `index?`: `number` — Controlled current image.
- `onIndexChange?`: `((index: number) => void)`
- `thumbnails?`: `boolean` — Thumbnail strip under the image. Default: shown when there's more than one image.
- `title?`: `string`, default `Image viewer (localized: lightbox.title)` — Name of the dialog, e.g. "Seashell Sites screenshots".

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Screenshots worth a closer look, browsed as a set.

  ```tsx
  <Gallery />
  ```

- Don’t: A full-screen viewer for a 32px avatar with nothing more to see.

  ```tsx
  <Avatar />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Built on Dialog: focus is trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the thumbnail that opened it.
- Every image needs real `alt`; the counter (“2 of 3”) is announced as you move.
- ←/→ move, +/− zoom, 0 resets.

## LineChart

`import { LineChart } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/line-chart';`

Status: stable · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-linechart--docs

**When to use**

- Comparing a few trends over the same time: CPU vs memory, this week vs last.
- Up to 5 series; each gets a palette color and a legend entry with its name.

**When not to use**

- One series where volume matters → use AreaChart
- More than 5 series → use small multiples, or let people pick series
- Categories with no order → use BarChart

**Anatomy**

- Lines: one per `series` (key + name).
- Legend: repeats each name beside its swatch.
- Tooltip: all series at the hovered point, with names.

**LineChart props**

- `data`: `LineChartPoint[]`
- `series`: `LineChartSeries[]`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `format?`: `((v: number) => string)`
- `height?`: `number`, default `260`
- `labelPrefix?`: `string`, default ``
- `legend?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `showXAxis?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `showYAxis?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `unit?`: `string`, default ``
- `yStep?`: `number`, default `1` — Gridline interval in data units.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Two trends that are easy to tell apart and compare.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><LineChart data={two} series={[{ key: 'cpu', name: 'CPU' }, { key: 'mem', name: 'Memory' }]} unit="%" height={200} ariaLabel="CPU and memory this week, both peaking on Friday." /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Five crossing lines: a tangle where no single server can be followed.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full">
    <LineChart
      data={many}
      series={['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'].map((k) => ({ key: k, name: `web-0${'abcde'.indexOf(k) + 1}` }))}
      unit="%"
      height={200}
      ariaLabel="CPU per server this week."
    />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `ariaLabel` says what to take away, not “Line chart”.
- Series are named in the legend and tooltip, so color isn’t the only way to tell them apart.

## Link

`import { Link } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/link';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-link--docs

**When to use**

- Going somewhere: another page, a section, a document, an external site.
- Inside a sentence (no `size`, so it takes the text’s size) or as a standalone line with `size`.

**When not to use**

- Doing something: save, delete, open a dialog → use Button (ghost for a quiet one)
- A navigation item in a menu or sidebar → use SidebarItem, DropdownMenuItem, Tabs
- A whole card that leads somewhere → use CardLink

**Anatomy**

- Label: says where it goes: “Billing settings”, not “click here”. `size` xs–lg, or inherited.
- Underline: on hover by default; always with `underline`, thicker on hover.

**Link props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Render onto the child element (a router link) instead of an <a>.
- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Colors and focus ring for a dark or primary surface.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xs"` — Type step for a standalone link. Omit inside text to inherit the surrounding size.
- `underline?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Always underlined (links in running text). Off: underline on hover only.

Also accepts the props of: AnchorHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: In running text the link is underlined, so it doesn’t rely on color alone.

  ```tsx
  <p className={TEXT}>
    Read the <Link href="#gl-link" underline>refund policy</Link> before you cancel.
  </p>
  ```

- Don’t: Without the underline the link is just a blue word to anyone who can’t tell the colors apart.

  ```tsx
  <p className={TEXT}>
    Read the <Link href="#gl-link">refund policy</Link> before you cancel.
  </p>
  ```

- Do: An action is a Button, even a quiet one.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="ghost" tone="danger" size="md">Delete project</Button>
  ```

- Don’t: A link that deletes: screen readers announce “link”, and people expect it to navigate.

  ```tsx
  <Link href="#gl-link" size="md">Delete project</Link>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The text says where the link goes; “here”, “more” and “link” don’t make sense read out of context in a links list.
- Use `underline` inside running text (WCAG 1.4.1).
- On a dark or primary surface use `inverse`: the default link color and focus ring don’t have the contrast there.
- A link that opens a new tab says so in its text, e.g. “Pricing (opens in a new tab)”.

## ListItem

`import { ListItem } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/list-item';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-listitem--docs

**When to use**

- Lists lighter than a table: settings sections, notifications, a resource picker.
- A whole row that navigates (`href`) or toggles selection (`interactive`).

**When not to use**

- Several comparable columns → use DataTable
- Menu commands → use DropdownMenu
- Picking one of a few options → use OptionCard or RadioGroup

**Anatomy**

- Leading (optional): icon, avatar or thumbnail.
- Title: the item.
- Description (optional): one line of detail.
- Trailing (optional): value, badge, switch or chevron — outside the clickable area.

**ListItem props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `href?`: `string` — Renders the row's text region as a link.
- `interactive?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Renders the text region as a selectable, whole-row-clickable region.
- `leading?`: `ReactNode` — Leading visual: an icon, Avatar, or a tone-colored status glyph.
- `onClick?`: `MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement>`
- `onKeyDown?`: `KeyboardEventHandler<HTMLElement>`
- `selected?`: `boolean`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `title?`: `ReactNode`
- `trailing?`: `ReactNode` — Trailing content — meta text, a Badge, a kebab menu. Stays outside the link/button region.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Short title, one line of detail, the whole row is the link.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col">
    <ListItem href="#" leading={<Lock />} title="Security" description="Password, 2FA, sessions" trailing={<NavArrowRight />} />
    <ListItem href="#" leading={<Bell />} title="Notifications" description="Email and in-app" trailing={<NavArrowRight />} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A paragraph as description: the list stops being scannable.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col">
    <ListItem href="#" title="Security settings" description="Here you can manage your password, two-factor authentication, active sessions, API tokens and recovery codes for your account." />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The row is one real link or button; the description is attached as its description.
- Selected state is announced (`aria-pressed` / `aria-current`).
- A control in trailing is its own tab stop and needs its own label.

## Marquee

`import { Marquee } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/marquee';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-marquee--docs

**When to use**

- A strip of customer logos, short quotes or partner names on a landing page — “trusted by”.

**When not to use**

- Content people need to read or act on → use a static row or Carousel
- News, alerts, anything time-critical → use Alert or AnnouncementBar
- Product UI → use a static list

**Anatomy**

- Track: the items twice, moving by half its width; `duration` seconds per loop.
- Edge fade (optional): soft fade at both ends (`fade`).
- Pause button: stops and resumes the strip (`pauseButton`, on by default).

**Marquee props**

- `duration?`: `number`, default `30` — Seconds for one full loop; longer is calmer.
- `fade?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Fade the strip out at both edges.
- `gap?`: `string`, default `2.5rem` — Space between items (a CSS length, e.g. "2.5rem").
- `pauseButton?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Show the pause / play button (default). Turn off only for a purely decorative strip.
- `reverse?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Run against the reading direction.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Short, uniform items; calm speed; pause button kept.

  ```tsx
  <Marquee duration={20} className="w-72 text-body-m"><span>Northwind</span><span>Kestrel</span><span>Quartz</span><span>Lumen</span></Marquee>
  ```

- Don’t: Long sentences racing past with no way to stop them.

  ```tsx
  <Marquee duration={4} pauseButton={false} className="w-72 text-body-m"><span>Read our full terms before the offer ends tonight</span></Marquee>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- WCAG 2.2.2: the strip pauses on hover and keyboard focus, and the pause button stops it for good.
- The second copy of the items is aria-hidden and inert: screen readers and Tab meet each item once.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no movement — the items wrap into rows.

## MarqueeColumns

`import { MarqueeColumns } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/marquee-columns';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-marqueecolumns--docs

**When to use**

- A decorative wall of cards behind or beside a hero: testimonials, templates, integrations.

**When not to use**

- A single row of logos or short items → use Marquee
- Cards people need to read or click in order → use Card grid

**Anatomy**

- Columns: one per array in `columns`; neighbours drift in opposite directions at slightly different speeds.
- Fade: the top and bottom edges fade out.
- Pause: a Pause / Play button (`pauseButton`).

**MarqueeColumns props**

- `columns`: `ReactNode[][]` — One array of cards per column.
- `duration?`: `number`, default `40` — Seconds for one full loop of the first column (default 40); the others run a little faster or slower.
- `gap?`: `string`, default `1rem` — Space between cards and between columns (CSS length, default 1rem).
- `pauseButton?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Show the Pause / Play button (default true).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Enough cards to loop without visible repeats.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>3 columns, 4–6 short cards each</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: Moving controls are hard to hit.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>A wall of buttons and forms</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Pauses on hover and while anything inside has focus; Pause stops it for good (WCAG 2.2.2).
- Each column renders its items twice; the copy is aria-hidden and inert, so each card is met once.
- prefers-reduced-motion: the columns stand still.

## MaskedInput

`import { MaskedInput } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/masked-input';`

Status: beta · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-maskedinput--docs

**When to use**

- A value with one fixed format people type character by character: a card number, an IPv4 address, a date in a fixed form.

**When not to use**

- Phone numbers (formats differ by country) → use PhoneField
- Dates people may pick → use DatePicker
- Free text, names, emails → use TextField

**Anatomy**

- Field: TextField’s input and chrome; label it with a Label (htmlFor) or aria-label.
- Mask: `mask` template with placeholder chars; `showMask` shows it while empty.

**MaskedInput props**

- `mask`: `string` — Mask template, e.g. "+1 (___) ___-____" or "__/__/____".
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `error?`: `ReactNode` — Same error prop as TextField — turns the field danger-styled and can carry a message.
- `modify?`: `MaskedInputModify` — Conditionally tweak mask/replacement/showMask before masking.
- `onChange?`: `((e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void)`
- `onUnmaskedChange?`: `((raw: string) => void)` — Called with the raw value (mask literals stripped) on every change.
- `replacement?`: `string | Record<string, RegExp>` — Placeholder-char to allowed-pattern map. Default { _: /\d/ }. Pass a string like "#" as shorthand for { "#": /./ }.
- `showMask?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show the full mask template while empty.
- `track?`: `MaskedInputTrack` — Conditionally transform the entered value before masking.
- `value?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Groups appear as you type; separators aren’t typed.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-mi-card">Card number</Label>
    <MaskedInput id="gl-mi-card" mask="____ ____ ____ ____" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Making people strip spaces themselves.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Card number" placeholder="Enter 16 digits without spaces" widthSize="md" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The format goes in the description too (“16 digits”) — the mask alone isn’t read out.
- Known limitation: editing in the middle can move the caret to the end.
- Read the raw value with `onUnmaskedChange`, not by stripping on your side.

## Menubar

`import { Menubar, MenubarTrigger, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarLabel, MenubarSeparator, MenubarShortcut, MenubarSubTrigger, MenubarSubContent, MenubarMenu, MenubarGroup, MenubarRadioGroup, MenubarPortal, MenubarSub } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/menubar';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-menubar--docs

**When to use**

- An application-style menu bar for editors and tools: File, Edit, View, each with many commands.

**When not to use**

- Site or product navigation → use NavigationMenu or Sidebar
- One menu of actions → use DropdownMenu
- A few frequent actions → use a toolbar of Buttons

**Anatomy**

- Bar: one tab stop; `bordered` for a floating toolbar look.
- Trigger: opens its menu; arrows move between menus.
- Content: items, checkbox/radio items, submenus, shortcuts — same as DropdownMenu.

**Menubar props**

- `bordered?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Border + shadow, like a floating toolbar. Set false for a bare bar that blends into a surrounding app toolbar (no card chrome). Default true.

**MenubarItem props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "danger"`, default `neutral`

**MenubarLabel props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

**MenubarSubTrigger props**

- `inset?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: MenubarProps, HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, MenuContentProps, MenuContentImplProps, PopperContentProps, MenuItemProps, MenuItemImplProps, MenuCheckboxItemProps, MenuRadioItemProps, MenuSubContentProps, MenuRadioGroupProps, MenuPortalProps, MenubarSubProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Command menus of an editor, like a desktop app.

  ```tsx
  <Menubar aria-label="Editor menu">
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>New file</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Edit</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Undo</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>View</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Zoom in</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
  </Menubar>
  ```

- Don’t: Site navigation as a menubar: links become menu commands — use NavigationMenu.

  ```tsx
  <Menubar aria-label="Site menu">
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Products</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Hosting</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Pricing</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Plans</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Docs</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Guides</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
  </Menubar>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Role `menubar` with roving focus: Tab lands on the bar once, ←/→ move between menus, ↓ opens.
- Name the bar with `aria-label`.
- Items that navigate belong in navigation, not here — screen readers announce menu items, not links.

## Message

`import { Message } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/message';`

Status: beta · Category: AI & Chat
Docs: ./?path=/docs/ai-chat-message--docs

**When to use**

- One turn in a conversation, inside ChatMessages.
- `variant` received (left) / sent (right); author and time when they help.

**When not to use**

- System notices in a transcript (“Agent joined”) → use a centered small text line
- Notifications outside a chat → use Alert or Toaster

**Anatomy**

- Bubble: received: muted, left; sent: primary, right. `appearance` filled/tonal.
- Avatar and author (optional): who said it.
- Timestamp (optional): when it matters (support, async threads).

**Message props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal"`, default `filled`
- `author?`: `ReactNode`
- `avatar?`: `ReactNode` — Leading Avatar (usually shown on received messages).
- `timestamp?`: `ReactNode`
- `variant?`: `"received" | "sent"`, default `received`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Side and color say who; the author line says it in words too.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-2">
    <Message author="Assistant" timestamp="09:41">Backup finished — 2.4 GB, 14 files.</Message>
    <Message variant="sent" author="You" timestamp="09:42">Thanks!</Message>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Both sides styled as “sent” and unnamed: whose message is whose?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-2">
    <Message variant="sent">Backup finished — 2.4 GB, 14 files.</Message>
    <Message variant="sent">Thanks!</Message>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Side and color aren’t read out — keep author text (visually or sr-only) so screen readers know who spoke.
- Long code or tables inside a message should scroll inside the bubble, not stretch the transcript.

## MessagePopup

`import { MessagePopup, MessagePopupTrigger, MessagePopupContent } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/message-popup';`

Status: beta · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-messagepopup--docs

**When to use**

- A help or AI assistant that lives in a corner while the page stays usable beside it.

**When not to use**

- Forms people must complete → use Dialog or a page
- Notifications → use Toaster

**Anatomy**

- Launcher: a round icon button with a name.
- Panel: fixed width; `title`, `description`, close; holds a Chat transcript and a PromptArea.

**MessagePopup props**

- `sheet?`: `boolean` — Below 640px, open as a bottom sheet (Drawer) instead of a floating

**MessagePopupContent props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `sheetClassName?`: `string` — Sheet mode: classes for the scrolling body that holds the content (default padding px-6 pt-2 pb-5).
- `sheetTitle?`: `ReactNode` — Sheet mode: visible title at the top of the sheet. Falls back to `aria-label` (screen readers only).
- `showClose?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `title?`: `ReactNode`

Also accepts the props of: PopoverProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, PopoverContentProps, PopperContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, PopoverContentImplProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A conversation on the side; the page stays usable.

  ```tsx
  <MessagePopup>
    <MessagePopupTrigger>
      <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="lg" iconOnly leftIcon={<ChatBubble />} aria-label="Open assistant" />
    </MessagePopupTrigger>
    <MessagePopupContent title="Assistant" description="Ask about your sites and billing.">
      <p className="font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">Hi! How can I help?</p>
    </MessagePopupContent>
  </MessagePopup>
  ```

- Don’t: A form in a chat bubble — lost with one click outside.

  ```tsx
  <MessagePopup>
    <MessagePopupTrigger>
      <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="lg" iconOnly leftIcon={<ChatBubble />} aria-label="Open support form" />
    </MessagePopupTrigger>
    <MessagePopupContent title="New support ticket">
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <TextField label="Subject" widthSize="full" />
        <TextField label="Site" widthSize="full" />
        <TextField label="Contact email" widthSize="full" />
      </div>
    </MessagePopupContent>
  </MessagePopup>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The launcher is a named button with aria-expanded; focus moves into the panel and back on close.
- Put new messages in a live region so they’re announced.

## Meter

`import { Meter } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/meter';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-meter--docs

**When to use**

- How full something is within a known range: disk, memory, a quota, seats used.
- A score or level, also as segments (`segments`).

**When not to use**

- How far along a running task is → use Progress
- A total split into parts → use UsageBar
- A value people set → use Slider

**Anatomy**

- Label: what is measured.
- Value (optional): formatted with `format` (percent, GB…); hide with `showValue={false}` only if the label says it.
- Bar: fill by `value` between `min` and `max`; `tone` from how critical the level is.

**Meter props**

- `value`: `number`
- `format?`: `NumberFormatOptions`
- `getValueLabel?`: `((formattedValue: string, value: number) => string)` — Custom accessible value text (aria-valuetext), e.g. (f, v) => v >= 90 ? "Nearly full" : f.
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `max?`: `number`, default `100`
- `min?`: `number`, default `0`
- `segments?`: `number` — Render as `segments` discrete lit-or-not cells instead of a smooth
- `showValue?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `tone?`: `"info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Tone follows the level, and the number says it too.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-3">
    <Meter value={0.38} min={0} max={1} label="CPU" tone="success" format={{ style: 'percent' }} />
    <Meter value={0.96} min={0} max={1} label="Disk" tone="danger" format={{ style: 'percent' }} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Progress for a fill level reads as “almost done”, not “almost full”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-1">
    <span className="text-body-s">Disk</span>
    <Progress value={96} aria-label="Disk" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Native `role="meter"` with min / max / now. Use `getValueLabel` for words where they help (“Nearly full”).
- Without a visible `label`, pass `aria-label`.
- The tone isn’t the only signal — the value or label must say the level.
- For percent pass a fraction with `max={1}`; the component warns about 0.38 of 100.

## Metric

`import { Metric } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/metric';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-metric--docs

**When to use**

- Quick-glance counts repeated as rows inside a card: mailboxes used, aliases, records pending.

**When not to use**

- A headline KPI that stands alone → use Stat
- Usage against a limit that needs a bar → use Meter
- Properties of one object → use DescriptionList

**Anatomy**

- Icon (optional): muted and decorative.
- Value: the number, read first.
- Label: follows the value in the same line (“121`/150 mailboxes`”).
- Actions (optional): a link or small button on the right.

**Metric props**

- `label`: `string`
- `value`: `ReactNode` — The metric value — a string/number is the common case (tabular-nums).
- `actions?`: `ReactNode` — Optional trailing controls. Omit to render none.
- `description?`: `string` — Optional muted explainer line below the value/label.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Optional leading icon (decorative — the visible value/label carry the meaning).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Rows of counts in a card, scanned top to bottom.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Metric icon={<Mail />} value={121} label="/150 mailboxes" />
    <Metric icon={<WarningCircle />} value={2} label=" DNS records not propagated" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: KPI tiles stacked as a list: heavy, and every row competes for attention.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Stat label="Mailboxes" value="121/150" />
    <Stat label="DNS records not propagated" value={2} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Each row is a named group (label, plus description), so it reads as one statement.
- The icon is hidden from screen readers — the label must carry any severity.

## NavigationMenu

`import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuItem } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/navigation-menu';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-navigationmenu--docs

**When to use**

- A horizontal site or product header with a few top-level sections, some opening a panel of links.

**When not to use**

- App navigation with many sections → use Sidebar
- Commands (File, Edit…) → use Menubar
- Switching views within a page → use Tabs

**Anatomy**

- List: top-level items: links, or triggers with a chevron.
- Content: the flyout panel of links, under the bar.
- Link: `NavigationMenuLink`; mark the current with `active`.

**NavigationMenu props**

- `viewportClassName?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: NavigationMenuProps, HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, NavigationMenuContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, NavigationMenuLinkProps, SVGAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Four top-level sections fit in one row.

  ```tsx
  <NavigationMenu aria-label="Site sections">
    <NavigationMenuList>{['Products', 'Pricing', 'Docs', 'Blog'].map(link)}</NavigationMenuList>
  </NavigationMenu>
  ```

- Don’t: Ten app sections in a header bar: they wrap and get lost — use a Sidebar.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80 overflow-hidden">
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="All sections">
      <NavigationMenuList className="flex-wrap">
        {['Dashboard', 'Sites', 'Domains', 'Databases', 'Email', 'Backups', 'Logs', 'Team', 'Billing', 'Settings'].map(link)}
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A `nav`; give each one on a page its own `aria-label`.
- Triggers are buttons with aria-expanded; Tab moves through links, Escape closes a panel.
- The current section’s link has `aria-current="page"` (`active`).

## NumberField

`import { NumberField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/number-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-numberfield--docs

**When to use**

- A count or amount people adjust in small steps: quantity, seats, retention days, CPU cores.
- With `min`/`max` when the range is known.

**When not to use**

- Numbers that aren’t amounts: card, phone, postcode → use TextField / MaskedInput / PhoneField
- A range of two values → use RangeField
- Rough values where precision doesn’t matter → use Slider

**Anatomy**

- Label: outside, via Label.
- Input: typed value commits on blur/Enter, then clamps.
- − / + buttons: step by `step`; Shift+arrows ×10.

**NumberField props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `decrementLabel?`: `string`, default `Decrease (localized: numberField.decrement)`
- `defaultValue?`: `number`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md` — Matches TextField's heightSize: md 40px (default), sm 32px with 12px text and the 4px radius — for dense rows (cart quantities, table cells).
- `id?`: `string`
- `incrementLabel?`: `string`, default `Increase (localized: numberField.increment)`
- `max?`: `number`
- `min?`: `number`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: number) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `step?`: `number`, default `1`
- `value?`: `number`
- `widthSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "full"`, default `sm` — sm 128px (default — a stepper holds a short number), md 224, lg 348,

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Default width (sm, 128px) and limits — the width says “a small number”. full only inside a fixed-width cell or column.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-nf-seats">Seats</Label>
    <NumberField id="gl-nf-seats" defaultValue={5} min={1} max={50} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A plain text field for a count: no stepping, no limits, any text accepted.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Seats" defaultValue="5" description="Enter a number from 1 to 50" widthSize="full" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a spinbutton: `aria-valuenow/min/max` are set, arrows change the value.
- Name the − / + buttons if “Decrease/Increase” isn’t clear enough (decrementLabel / incrementLabel).
- Say the unit in the label (“Retention, days”).

## OptionCard

`import { OptionCard, OptionCardGroup } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/option-card';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-optioncard--docs

**When to use**

- A one-of choice where each option needs a title, a line of explanation and often a price: plans, verification methods, delivery.
- 2–5 options that are the main decision on the screen.

**When not to use**

- Short options a label explains → use RadioGroup
- Several options at once → use CheckboxGroup
- Cards that navigate somewhere → use Card with a link

**Anatomy**

- Group: `OptionCardGroup` — a radio group laid out as a grid (2 columns from sm).
- Icon (optional): helps tell options apart at a glance.
- Title and description: the title is the accessible name, the description is read after it.
- Aside (optional): right-aligned detail, usually the price.

**OptionCard props**

- `title`: `string`
- `aside?`: `ReactNode` — Right-aligned detail before the radio dot — typically the option's
- `description?`: `string`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, RadioGroupProps, RadioProps$1.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Each choice needs a sentence — cards give it room.

  ```tsx
  <OptionCardGroup defaultValue="http" aria-label="Verification method" className="w-full">
    <OptionCard value="http" title="HTTP-01" description="Serve a token file from the site." />
    <OptionCard value="dns" title="DNS-01" description="Add a TXT record. Works for wildcards." />
  </OptionCardGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: Cards for a plain yes/no — a radio pair or switch says it in a line.

  ```tsx
  <OptionCardGroup defaultValue="yes" aria-label="Send invoice" className="w-full">
    <OptionCard value="yes" title="Yes" />
    <OptionCard value="no" title="No" />
  </OptionCardGroup>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Works like a radio group: one tab stop, arrows move and select.
- Name the group with `aria-label` or a visible heading via `aria-labelledby`.
- Don’t put buttons or links inside a card — the whole card is one radio.

## OrbitCarousel

`import { OrbitCarousel } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/orbit-carousel';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-orbitcarousel--docs

**When to use**

- A showcase on a landing page: case studies, product shots, a few campaign cards.

**When not to use**

- Content people browse or compare in the product → use Carousel
- More than ~10 cards, or cards with forms and long text → use Card grid

**Anatomy**

- Drum: `shape="drum"`: cards round a cylinder that turns on its vertical axis.
- Wheel: `shape="wheel"`: cards on the rim of a large wheel to the start side, rolling past vertically; up to three on each side, fading out.
- Controls: Previous / Next; Pause when `autoplay` is set.

**OrbitCarousel props**

- `autoplay?`: `number` — Turn on its own every `autoplay` ms. Off by default.
- `itemWidth?`: `number`, default `240` — Card width in px (drum) or the card box width (wheel). Default 240.
- `onIndexChange?`: `((index: number) => void)` — Called with the index of the card that comes to the front.
- `shape?`: `"drum" | "wheel"`, default `drum`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Enough cards to read as a circle; each one makes sense on its own.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>5–8 image-led cards</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: Too few to form a circle — use a plain Carousel.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>2 cards on a drum</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- One tab stop; ← / → (↑ / ↓ for the wheel) turn it; drag or swipe does the same.
- Only the front card is in the accessibility tree; the others are aria-hidden and inert.
- autoplay pauses on hover and focus and has a Pause button (WCAG 2.2.2).
- prefers-reduced-motion: no turning animation and no autoplay.

## PageHeader

`import { PageHeader } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/page-header';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs

**When to use**

- The top of a page or major section: title, a line of description, and the page’s main action on the right.

**When not to use**

- Global app actions (account, notifications) → use Topbar
- Sub-sections inside a page → use a heading, or PageHeader with as="h2"

**Anatomy**

- Title: h1 by default (`as` h2/h3 for sections); optional `icon` and `tags`.
- Description (optional): one or two lines.
- Actions (optional): right-aligned on the top row: one primary, maybe one secondary.
- Breadcrumb / meta (optional): `breadcrumb`, `children` for meta rows.

**PageHeader props**

- `title`: `ReactNode`
- `actions?`: `ReactNode` — Right-aligned action row. Sits beside the breadcrumb when given, otherwise beside the title, vertically centered on that row.
- `as?`: `"h2" | "h3" | "h1"`, default `h1`
- `breadcrumb?`: `ReactNode` — Content above the title — typically a Breadcrumb.
- `contentActions?`: `ReactNode` — A second action row tied to the description/content — always below it, outside the actions-centering row.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Supporting line below the title. Capped at 540px so a long line wraps for readability.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Leading icon beside the title. Plain — no chip/circle background, sized to the title's own scale.
- `tags?`: `ReactNode` — Row of tags/chips below the title, above the description.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One primary action that matches the page.

  ```tsx
  <div className={FRAME}>
    <PageHeader as="h2" title="Sites" description="Websites hosted in this workspace." actions={<Button leftIcon={<Plus />} size="md">New site</Button>} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Three primary buttons: nothing stands out — keep one primary, move the rest to a menu.

  ```tsx
  <div className={FRAME}>
    <PageHeader
      as="h2"
      title="Sites"
      actions={
        <div className="flex gap-2">
          <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">New site</Button>
          <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Import</Button>
          <Button appearance="filled" tone="primary" size="md">Export</Button>
        </div>
      }
    />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- One h1 per page; use as="h2" for section headers so the outline stays correct.

## Pagination

`import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationPrevious, PaginationNext, PaginationEllipsis } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/pagination';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-pagination--docs

**When to use**

- Long lists and tables split into pages people jump between: search results, logs, invoices.
- When the position in the set matters (“page 3 of 10”).

**When not to use**

- Feeds people scroll through → use a “Load more” button or infinite scroll
- Fewer than about 25 items → use show them all

**Anatomy**

- Previous / Next: disabled at the ends (`disabled` keeps them announced).
- Pages: first, last, and the current with neighbours; `isActive` marks the current.
- Ellipsis: for skipped ranges.

**PaginationLink props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Not navigable (e.g. Previous on page 1). Drops the href so the link is
- `isActive?`: `boolean`
- `wide?`: `boolean`, default `false`

**PaginationPrevious props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`
- `disabled?`: `boolean` — Not navigable (e.g. Previous on page 1). Drops the href so the link is
- `isActive?`: `boolean`

**PaginationNext props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`
- `disabled?`: `boolean` — Not navigable (e.g. Previous on page 1). Drops the href so the link is
- `isActive?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: First, last, and the pages around the current one.

  ```tsx
  <Pagination aria-label="Results pages">
    <PaginationContent>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationPrevious href="#gl-pg" /></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="#gl-pg">1</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationEllipsis /></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="#gl-pg">4</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="#gl-pg" isActive>5</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="#gl-pg">6</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationEllipsis /></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="#gl-pg">12</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
      <PaginationItem><PaginationNext href="#gl-pg" /></PaginationItem>
    </PaginationContent>
  </Pagination>
  ```

- Don’t: Every page number, no Previous/Next: it wraps and keeps growing with the data.

  ```tsx
  <Pagination aria-label="Results pages, all numbers">
  ```
