  ```tsx
    <PaginationContent className="flex-wrap">
      {Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => (
        <PaginationItem key={i}>
          <PaginationLink href="#gl-pg" isActive={i === 4}>{i + 1}</PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
      ))}
    </PaginationContent>
  </Pagination>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A `nav` named “Pagination”; give each one on a page its own name.
- The current page has `aria-current="page"`; Previous/Next have text names, not just arrows.
- After changing page, move focus to the top of the results.

## Password

`import { Password } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/password';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-password--docs

**When to use**

- Signing in, setting or changing a password — with show/hide.

**When not to use**

- API keys and tokens shown to the person → use SecretField
- One-time codes → use InputOTP

**Anatomy**

- Field: a TextField with the show/hide toggle in its right slot.
- Description (optional): the rule, shown before typing (“At least 8 characters.”).
- Strength (optional): PasswordStrengthMeter under it, for new passwords.

**Password props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Helper text below the field. Hidden when `error` or `success` is set.
- `error?`: `ReactNode` — Error message shown below the field with a warning icon, and
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `labelPosition?`: `"top" | "left"` — 'top' (default) stacks label above the field. 'left' puts a fixed 216px label column beside it, matching Figma's horizontal Formfield layout.
- `optional?`: `boolean` — Shows "(optional)" after the label. Ignored when `required`.
- `required?`: `boolean` — Shows a small red asterisk after the label.
- `success?`: `ReactNode` — Success message shown below the field with a check icon, and
- `widthSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "full"`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The rule is visible before the first attempt.

  ```tsx
  <Password label="New password" description="At least 8 characters." widthSize="lg" />
  ```

- Don’t: The rule only appears as an error, after failing.

  ```tsx
  <Password label="New password" error="Password is too weak." widthSize="lg" />
  ```

- Do: One field; show/hide lets people check what they typed.

  ```tsx
  <Password label="New password" widthSize="lg" />
  ```

- Don’t: A “repeat” field doubles the typing and still doesn’t catch a typo made twice.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <Password label="New password" widthSize="lg" />
    <Password label="Repeat password" widthSize="lg" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- `autoComplete="current-password"` to sign in, `"new-password"` to set one — password managers depend on it.
- The toggle is a button with a name that says what it will do (“Show password”).

## PasswordStrengthMeter

`import { PasswordStrengthMeter } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/password-strength-meter';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-passwordstrengthmeter--docs

**When to use**

- Under a new-password field, to show how close the password is to the rules as it’s typed.

**When not to use**

- Signing in with an existing password
- When the only rule is a length — say it in the field’s description instead

**Anatomy**

- Bar: filled by score; danger / warning / success.
- Label: Weak / Good / Strong.
- Checklist: each rule met or not; `rules` to override.

**PasswordStrengthMeter props**

- `value`: `string` — The current password value to evaluate.
- `className?`: `string`
- `rules?`: `PasswordStrengthRule[]` — Override the default 5 rules (length/upper/lower/number/symbol).

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The checklist says what’s missing, not just “weak”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-[348px] max-w-full"><PasswordStrengthMeter value="abcDEF12" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A verdict without the rules leaves people guessing what to add.

  ```tsx
  <span className="font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-danger)]">Weak</span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The bar is a progressbar with a text value (Weak/Good/Strong).
- Each rule is text with a met/not-met state, not color only.

## PhoneField

`import { PhoneField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/phone-field';`

Status: beta · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-phonefield--docs

**When to use**

- Any phone number: account, 2FA by SMS, contact details.

**When not to use**

- Other fixed formats → use MaskedInput

**Anatomy**

- Country picker: flag + code; `preferredCountries` on top.
- Number: formatted as typed; the country’s example as placeholder.
- Message: too short / too long for the country, on blur.

**PhoneField props**

- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultCountry?`: `"AC" | "AD" | "AE" | "AF" | "AG" | "AI" | "AL" | "AM" | "AO" | "AR" | "AS" | "AT" | "AU" | "AW" | "AX" | "AZ" | "BA" | "BB" | "BD" | "BE" | "BF" | "BG" | "BH" | "BI" | "BJ" | "BL" | "BM" | "BN" | "BO" | "BQ" | "BR" | "BS" | "BT" | "BW" | "BY" | "BZ" | "CA" | "CC" | "CD" | "CF" | "CG" | "CH" | "CI" | "CK" | "CL" | "CM" | "CN" | "CO" | "CR" | "CU" | "CV" | "CW" | "CX" | "CY" | "CZ" | "DE" | "DJ" | "DK" | "DM" | "DO" | "DZ" | "EC" | "EE" | "EG" | "EH" | "ER" | "ES" | "ET" | "FI" | "FJ" | "FK" | "FM" | "FO" | "FR" | "GA" | "GB" | "GD" | "GE" | "GF" | "GG" | "GH" | "GI" | "GL" | "GM" | "GN" | "GP" | "GQ" | "GR" | "GT" | "GU" | "GW" | "GY" | "HK" | "HN" | "HR" | "HT" | "HU" | "ID" | "IE" | "IL" | "IM" | "IN" | "IO" | "IQ" | "IR" | "IS" | "IT" | "JE" | "JM" | "JO" | "JP" | "KE" | "KG" | "KH" | "KI" | "KM" | "KN" | "KP" | "KR" | "KW" | "KY" | "KZ" | "LA" | "LB" | "LC" | "LI" | "LK" | "LR" | "LS" | "LT" | "LU" | "LV" | "LY" | "MA" | "MC" | "MD" | "ME" | "MF" | "MG" | "MH" | "MK" | "ML" | "MM" | "MN" | "MO" | "MP" | "MQ" | "MR" | "MS" | "MT" | "MU" | "MV" | "MW" | "MX" | "MY" | "MZ" | "NA" | "NC" | "NE" | "NF" | "NG" | "NI" | "NL" | "NO" | "NP" | "NR" | "NU" | "NZ" | "OM" | "PA" | "PE" | "PF" | "PG" | "PH" | "PK" | "PL" | "PM" | "PR" | "PS" | "PT" | "PW" | "PY" | "QA" | "RE" | "RO" | "RS" | "RU" | "RW" | "SA" | "SB" | "SC" | "SD" | "SE" | "SG" | "SH" | "SI" | "SJ" | "SK" | "SL" | "SM" | "SN" | "SO" | "SR" | "SS" | "ST" | "SV" | "SX" | "SY" | "SZ" | "TA" | "TC" | "TD" | "TG" | "TH" | "TJ" | "TK" | "TL" | "TM" | "TN" | "TO" | "TR" | "TT" | "TV" | "TW" | "TZ" | "UA" | "UG" | "US" | "UY" | "UZ" | "VA" | "VC" | "VE" | "VG" | "VI" | "VN" | "VU" | "WF" | "WS" | "XK" | "YE" | "YT" | "ZA" | "ZM" | "ZW"` — Starting country when there's no value. Defaults to the browser's region, then US.
- `defaultValue?`: `string` — Uncontrolled starting value in E.164.
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `error?`: `string` — External error; replaces the built-in length check message.
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `id?`: `string`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `locale?`: `string` — Language for country names in the picker.
- `name?`: `string` — Name for the hidden input that carries the E.164 value in a native form post.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string, details: PhoneFieldChange) => void)`
- `optional?`: `boolean`
- `preferredCountries?`: `CountryCode[]`, default `[]` — Pinned to the top of the country list, e.g. where most of your customers are.
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `value?`: `string` — Controlled value in E.164, e.g. "+359888123456". Empty string when cleared.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: People type the way they know their number; the value comes out as E.164.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72"><PhoneField label="Phone" defaultCountry="BG" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Making people enter your storage format.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Phone" placeholder="+359XXXXXXXXX, no spaces" widthSize="md" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Pasting “+44…” switches the country by itself — autofill works.
- The picker has a search; the selected country is announced with the number field.
- Flags are emoji: on Windows they show as two letters.

## Popover

`import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverAnchor, PopoverClose, PopoverContent } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/popover';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-popover--docs

**When to use**

- A small panel tied to a control: a quick setting, a filter, a picker, extra details on tap.
- Content people can dismiss without losing work.

**When not to use**

- A short label for an icon → use Tooltip
- A list of actions → use DropdownMenu
- Forms with required fields, or a decision → use Dialog

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: a button; aria-expanded is set.
- Content: anchored panel; `side`, `align`; closes on Escape or a click outside.

**Popover props**

- `sheet?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Below 640px, open as a bottom sheet (Drawer) instead of a floating

**PopoverContent props**

- `sheetClassName?`: `string` — Sheet mode: classes for the scrolling body that holds the content (default padding px-6 pt-2 pb-5).
- `sheetTitle?`: `ReactNode` — Sheet mode: visible title at the top of the sheet. Falls back to `aria-label` (screen readers only).

Also accepts the props of: PopoverProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, PopperAnchorProps, PopoverContentProps, PopperContentProps, DismissableLayerProps, PopoverContentImplProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One quick setting right next to what it affects.

  ```tsx
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger asChild><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Limits</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent align="start" className="w-64">
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <Label htmlFor="gl-po-cpu">CPU cores</Label>
        <NumberField id="gl-po-cpu" defaultValue={2} min={1} max={8} />
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  ```

- Don’t: A required form in a popover: one click outside and it’s gone.

  ```tsx
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger asChild><Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Billing details</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent align="start" className="w-72">
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <TextField label="Company" required widthSize="full" />
        <TextField label="VAT number" required widthSize="full" />
        <TextField label="Address" required widthSize="full" />
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Focus moves into the panel on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape closes.
- Not modal: the page stays interactive — keep the content light.

## Price

`import { Price } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/price';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-price--docs

**When to use**

- Any amount of money in the UI: plan cards, checkout, invoices, add-ons.
- A discount (`compareAt`), a “from” price, a billing period.

**When not to use**

- A column of amounts in a table → use formatPrice in a right-aligned cell
- Charts and totals over time → use a chart with formatted axis

**Anatomy**

- From (optional): “From” before the amount (`from`).
- Amount: Intl-formatted for `currency` and `locale`; whole amounts drop .00; zero shows “Free”.
- Period (optional): “/mo” (`period`).
- Previous price + discount (optional): struck-through `compareAt` and a −N% badge.

**Price props**

- `amount`: `number`
- `compareAt?`: `number` — Previous price, shown struck through before the current one.
- `currency?`: `string`, default `USD` — ISO 4217 code. Default USD.
- `freeLabel?`: `string | null`, default `Free (localized: price.free)` — Text for a zero amount. Pass null to show "$0" instead.
- `from?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Prefix "From" — for a starting price.
- `locale?`: `string`
- `period?`: `string` — Short billing period shown after the amount: "mo", "year", "user"… Read out as "per month" etc.
- `showDiscount?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Show "−20%" next to a discounted price.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl"`, default `md`
- `superscript?`: `boolean`, default `false` — lg/xl only: raise the currency symbol and cents (retail price-tag style) instead of keeping them on the baseline.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Formatted for the locale, with period and the old price.

  ```tsx
  <Price amount={19.99} compareAt={24.99} currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" period="mo" size="lg" />
  ```

- Don’t: Hand-typed: wrong for German readers, and read aloud as fragments.

  ```tsx
  <span className="text-heading-m">19.99EUR/month (was 24.99)</span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Screen readers hear one sentence: “From €19.99 per month, was €24.99”; the visual pieces are hidden.
- The old price is never the only discount signal — the badge and the sentence say it too.
- Pass the real `locale`; the symbol position and separators follow it.

## ProductTour

`import { ProductTour } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/product-tour';`

Status: beta · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-producttour--docs

**When to use**

- Introducing what changed on a redesigned screen, once, in 2–5 steps.
- Teaching one action by doing it (an `interactive` step).

**When not to use**

- Explaining a whole product → use docs, or an empty state with guidance
- A single hint → use Tooltip or a callout
- Anything people need later → use Help content they can come back to

**Anatomy**

- Spotlight: the target cut out of a dim; a step without `target` is a centered card.
- Card: title, text, optional media, Back / Next, “2 of 4”, Skip.

**ProductTour props**

- `onOpenChange`: `(open: boolean) => void`
- `open`: `boolean`
- `steps`: `TourStep[]`
- `defaultStep?`: `number`, default `0`
- `hideSkip?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Hides the Skip button (the close button stays).
- `labels?`: `Partial<ProductTourLabels>`
- `onComplete?`: `(() => void)` — Finished with Done on the last step.
- `onSkip?`: `((step: number) => void)` — Closed early (Skip, close button, Esc). Receives the step it was on.
- `onStepChange?`: `((step: number) => void)`
- `step?`: `number` — Controlled step index.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Three steps about what’s new: easy to finish, easy to skip.

  ```tsx
  <Tour label="Start 3-step tour" steps={SHORT} />
  ```

- Don’t: Twelve steps pointing at everything: people skip on step 2 and learn nothing.

  ```tsx
  <Tour label="Start 12-step tour" steps={LONG} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Focus moves into the card on every step; ←/→ move between steps, Escape skips.
- The page under the dim is inert unless a step is interactive.
- Store “seen” in `onComplete`/`onSkip` — don’t show it again on every visit.

## Progress

`import { Progress } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/progress';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-progress--docs

**When to use**

- A task with a known percent done: upload, restore, export, install.
- A running task of unknown length (a deploy, a scan): `indeterminate`.
- A known number of stages (“stage 3 of 5”): `segments`.

**When not to use**

- How full something is (disk, quota) → use Meter
- Content loading for the first time → use Skeleton
- A background task people shouldn’t wait on → use Toaster (toast.progress)
- Named steps of a flow → use Stepper

**Anatomy**

- Label: what is running — next to the bar and linked with `aria-labelledby`.
- Track and indicator: `value` 0–100, clamped; or a sweeping bar with `indeterminate`; or `segments` equal steps that fill one after another.
- Value / status text (optional): percent, or “3 of 12 sites”, or time left.

**Progress props**

- `indeterminate?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Unknown length: no value, a sweeping bar.
- `segments?`: `number` — Split the bar into this many steps (2 or more).
- `value?`: `number`, default `0`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ProgressProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: What’s running and how much is done.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-1.5">
    <div className="flex justify-between text-body-s"><span id="gl-pr-label">Restoring backup</span><span className="tabular-nums">66%</span></div>
    <Progress value={66} aria-labelledby="gl-pr-label" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A bare bar: progress of what?

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72"><Progress value={66} aria-label="Progress" /></div>
  ```

- Do: Content loading for the first time → a skeleton of it. (A task of unknown length that people watch, like a deploy, is Progress indeterminate.)

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col gap-2">
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-56" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A fake percent for a page load lies about the wait.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72"><Progress value={30} aria-label="Loading" /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Always named: `aria-labelledby` to the visible label, or `aria-label`.
- Announce start and finish in a live region (or a toast); don’t announce every percent.
- Indeterminate has no value: the label says what is running. Movement respects reduced motion — the sweep becomes a slow fade.

## ProgressRing

`import { ProgressRing } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/progress-ring';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-progressring--docs

**When to use**

- A single completion figure on a card or a landing bento: setup 75% done, 3 of 4 steps.

**When not to use**

- A value that updates live (upload, CPU) → use Progress / Meter
- Several values to compare → use DonutChart / UsageBar

**Anatomy**

- Track: bg-neutral-subtle circle.
- Fill: rounded stroke in the `tone`, fills clockwise (counter-clockwise in RTL) when it scrolls into view.
- Middle (optional): the percentage counting up, or your own content (`children`).

**ProgressRing props**

- `label`: `string` — Accessible name, e.g. "Components generated".
- `value`: `number` — 0–max.
- `children?`: `ReactNode | ((shown: number) => ReactNode)` — What sits in the middle; default the percentage. Pass null for an empty middle.
- `duration?`: `number`, default `1200` — Fill time in ms (default 1200).
- `max?`: `number`, default `100`
- `size?`: `number`, default `120` — Diameter in px (default 120).
- `thickness?`: `number`, default `10` — Stroke width in px (default 10).
- `tone?`: `"info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One figure with a clear meaning.

  ```tsx
  <ProgressRing value={75} label="Setup" size={72} thickness={7} />
  ```

- Don’t: A live system value: the count-up shows numbers that were never true.

  ```tsx
  <ProgressRing value={33} label="CPU" size={72} thickness={7} tone="danger" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- role="progressbar" with `label`; the value is the final one from the start, the counting digits are hidden.
- Tone is never the only signal — the number is always there (or put it in children).
- prefers-reduced-motion: drawn full at once.

## PromptArea

`import { PromptArea } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/prompt-area';`

Status: beta · Category: AI & Chat
Docs: ./?path=/docs/ai-chat-promptarea--docs

**When to use**

- The composer of a chat or AI assistant: multi-line input that grows, send and stop, attachments, @mentions and /commands.

**When not to use**

- A one-line search → use SearchBox or TextField
- Long-form text in a form → use TextArea

**Anatomy**

- Textarea: grows to `maxRows`; Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks a line; ↑ in an empty field edits the last message.
- Send / Stop: one button: Send, or Stop while `busy` (streaming); `submitLabel`/`stopLabel`.
- Limit (optional): `maxLength` counter with a danger state near the limit.
- Slots (optional): `leading`/`trailing` tools, `attachments`, `mentions`, `commands`.

**PromptArea props**

- `accept?`: `string`
- `attachments?`: `ReactNode`
- `busy?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `commands?`: `PromptMenuItem[]` — Items shown when the user types "/" then a query, e.g. quick actions or saved prompts.
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `leading?`: `ReactNode`
- `maxFileSize?`: `number`
- `maxLength?`: `number`
- `maxRows?`: `number`, default `8`
- `mentions?`: `PromptMenuItem[]` — Items shown when the user types "@" then a query. Inserted as plain text on selection — see the component's own doc comment on why there's no inline pill.
- `onCommandSelect?`: `((item: PromptMenuItem) => void)` — Called when a command is picked from the "/" menu.
- `onEditLast?`: `(() => void)`
- `onFileRejected?`: `((file: File, reason: "type" | "size") => void)`
- `onFilesAdded?`: `((files: File[]) => void)`
- `onMentionSelect?`: `((item: PromptMenuItem) => void)` — Called when a mention is picked from the "@" menu.
- `onStop?`: `(() => void)`
- `onSubmit?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Send a message… (localized: promptArea.placeholder)`
- `stopLabel?`: `string`, default `Stop generating (localized: promptArea.stop)`
- `submitLabel?`: `string`, default `Send (localized: promptArea.send)`
- `trailing?`: `ReactNode`
- `value?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Grows with the message; Enter sends, Stop appears while answering.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-full"><PromptArea aria-label="Message the assistant" placeholder="Ask about your sites…" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A one-line field for prompts: long questions scroll out of sight, no stop, no attachments.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Message" placeholder="Ask about your sites…" widthSize="full" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name it with `aria-label` (default “Message”); status changes (sending, stopped, limit) go to a live region.
- Send and Stop are one named button that switches label while busy, so focus never jumps.

## PromptSuggestions

`import { PromptSuggestions } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/prompt-suggestions';`

Status: beta · Category: AI & Chat
Docs: ./?path=/docs/ai-chat-promptsuggestions--docs

**When to use**

- Starting points above an empty composer — what the assistant is good at, as tap-to-ask prompts.

**When not to use**

- Mid-conversation follow-ups → use short reply chips under the last answer
- Navigation → use links or buttons

**Anatomy**

- Cards: a short, concrete prompt each, optional icon; 2–4 of them.

**PromptSuggestions props**

- `items`: `PromptSuggestion[]`
- `onSelect`: `(item: PromptSuggestion) => void`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Concrete questions about the user’s own data — they show what’s possible.

  ```tsx
  <PromptSuggestions
    aria-label="Suggestions"
    onSelect={() => {}}
    items={[
      { id: '1', label: 'Why is shop.seashell.dev slow today?' },
      { id: '2', label: 'Which certificates expire this month?' },
      { id: '3', label: 'Summarize last night’s backup' },
    ]}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: “Help”, “Ask a question”: nothing to learn, nothing to tap for.

  ```tsx
  <PromptSuggestions
    aria-label="Vague suggestions"
    onSelect={() => {}}
    items={[{ id: '1', label: 'Help' }, { id: '2', label: 'Ask a question' }, { id: '3', label: 'Learn more' }]}
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Each suggestion is a button. In onSelect, fill or send the prompt and move focus to the composer — the component doesn’t do it for you.

## PropertyGrid

`import { PropertyGrid } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/property-grid';`

Status: stable · Category: Form Structure
Docs: ./?path=/docs/form-structure-propertygrid--docs

**When to use**

- Viewing and editing an object’s properties in a compact two-column list: an inspector panel, a resource’s settings, a selected item’s details.
- `readOnly` items for values people see but can’t change.

**When not to use**

- A form people fill once (sign-up, checkout) → use a stacked form (TextField, Form)
- Read-only facts with no editing → use DescriptionList
- Many records with the same fields → use DataTable

**Anatomy**

- Label column: sized to the longest label, capped by `maxLabelWidth`; long labels wrap.
- Value column: control per `type`: text, number, select, switch, textarea, custom.
- Rows: separated by a Separator; description under the control.

**PropertyGrid props**

- `items`: `PropertyGridItem[]`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValues?`: `Record<string, PropertyValue>` — Initial values keyed by item name (uncontrolled).
- `id?`: `string`
- `maxLabelWidth?`: `string`, default `30ch` — Cap on the label column (any CSS length). The column is still sized to the longest label; this only moves the ceiling past which labels ellipsise.
- `onValueChange?`: `((name: string, value: PropertyValue) => void)`
- `onValuesChange?`: `((values: Record<string, PropertyValue>) => void)`
- `values?`: `Record<string, PropertyValue>` — Controlled values keyed by item name (pair with onValueChange/onValuesChange).

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: An object’s properties, scanned and tweaked in place.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96 max-w-full">
    <PropertyGrid
      id="gl-pg"
      items={[
        { name: 'name', label: 'Display name', type: 'text' },
        { name: 'replicas', label: 'Replicas', type: 'number' },
        { name: 'public', label: 'Public URL', type: 'switch' },
        { name: 'id', label: 'Resource ID', type: 'text', readOnly: true },
      ]}
      defaultValues={{ name: 'shop-api', replicas: 3, public: true, id: 'res_8f2k1' }}
    />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A sign-up form as a grid: labels squeezed left, no room for help or errors — stack it instead.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96 max-w-full">
    <PropertyGrid
      id="gl-pg-signup"
      items={[
        { name: 'email', label: 'Email', type: 'text' },
        { name: 'company', label: 'Company name', type: 'text' },
        { name: 'about', label: 'Tell us about your project', type: 'textarea' },
      ]}
    />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Each label is a real label for its control; the grid is not a table to screen readers.
- Read-only values render as plain text (a read-only switch as a disabled switch), so they read and copy like any text.

## Prose

`import { Prose } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/prose';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-prose--docs

**When to use**

- Long-form content Theya doesn’t lay out itself: help articles, changelogs, legal pages, rendered Markdown or CMS HTML.

**When not to use**

- App UI — forms, cards, tables you build → use components with their own typography
- A single paragraph → use plain text classes

**Anatomy**

- Wrapper: `size` sm/md/lg; plain h1–h4, p, lists, code, tables, blockquote get the type scale and rhythm.

**Prose props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Render onto the child element instead of a <div> — e.g. `<Prose asChild><article>…</article></Prose>`.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — Base text step: `sm` body-s (side panels, in-product help), `md` body-m (default, docs/articles), `lg` body-l (editorial). Headings scale with it.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A help article: plain HTML, readable without a single class.

  ```tsx
  <Prose size="sm" className="w-full">
    <h3>Restore a backup</h3>
    <p>Backups run every night and are kept for <strong>14 days</strong>.</p>
    <ol>
      <li>Open <em>Backups</em>.</li>
      <li>Pick a date and choose <kbd>Restore</kbd>.</li>
    </ol>
  </Prose>
  ```

- Don’t: App UI inside Prose: article margins and text styles leak into the component.

  ```tsx
  <Prose size="sm" className="w-full">
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-lg)] border border-solid border-[var(--color-border-border)] p-3">
      <p>shop.seashell.dev</p>
      <p>Running</p>
    </div>
  </Prose>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Keep the source semantic (real headings in order, lists, table headers) — Prose styles structure, it doesn’t create it.

## PushSheet

`import { PushSheet, PushSheetHeader, PushSheetBody, PushSheetFooter, PushSheetTitle, PushSheetDescription, PushSheetClose } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/push-sheet';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-pushsheet--docs

**When to use**

- Details of a selected item beside the list, while the list stays usable: inspect, compare, pick the next one.

**When not to use**

- Tasks that must be finished or cancelled → use Dialog
- Confirmations → use AlertDialog

**Anatomy**

- Panel: in the page flow, pushes content aside; `side`, `width`. Below md it turns into a modal.
- Header: `PushSheetTitle` and `PushSheetClose`.
- Body / footer: scrolls on its own.

**PushSheet props**

- `open`: `boolean`
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `side?`: `"right" | "left"`, default `right`
- `width?`: `string`, default `22.5rem`

**PushSheetClose props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Click a site: details open beside the list, which stays clickable.

  ```tsx
  <Example title="shop.seashell.dev" body={<p className="font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">Running · eu-west-1. Click another site to switch.</p>} />
  ```

- Don’t: A destructive confirmation in a non-modal panel: easy to ignore, easy to hit by accident.

  ```tsx
  <Example title="Delete site?" body={<Button appearance="filled" tone="danger" size="sm">Delete</Button>} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Not modal: no focus trap, the page stays interactive.
- Opening should move focus into the panel; Close returns it to what opened it.

## QrCode

`import { QrCode } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/qr-code';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-qrcode--docs

**When to use**

- Moving something from screen to phone: 2FA setup, a Wi-Fi or app link, a payment or ticket.

**When not to use**

- The user is already on the phone → use a link or button
- Long data (a whole config) → use a download or a short link in the code

**Anatomy**

- Plate: white with a 4-module quiet zone — in both themes.
- Modules: one SVG path; error correction by `level` (H when there’s a center `icon`).
- Center icon (optional): a small brand mark.

**QrCode props**

- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Optional mark in the center (a logo or icon, ~20% of the code). Raises `level` to H.
- `label?`: `string`, default `QR code (localized: qrCode.label)` — Accessible name. Describe what scanning does, not what it is: "Scan to add Seashell to your authenticator app".
- `level?`: `"L" | "M" | "Q" | "H"`, default `M` — Error correction: how much of the code can be damaged or covered and
- `loading?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Shows a placeholder of the same size while the value is being fetched.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md` — Rendered edge length including the quiet zone: sm 128px, md 160px (default), lg 200px.
- `value?`: `string` — The text or URL to encode (e.g. an `otpauth://` URI for 2FA setup).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The same value as text, for people who can’t scan.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 flex-col items-center gap-3">
    <QrCode value={OTPAUTH} size="sm" label="Scan to add Seashell to your authenticator app" />
    <SecretField label="Or enter this key" value={SECRET} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A code alone locks out screen-reader users and anyone without a phone at hand.

  ```tsx
  <QrCode value={OTPAUTH} size="sm" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s an image named by `label` — describe what scanning does, not “QR code”.
- Always pair it with the value as text or a link.
- Don’t invert it for dark theme — many scanners can’t read light-on-dark.

## QueryBuilder

`import { QueryBuilder } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/query-builder';`

Status: stable · Category: Search & Filter
Docs: ./?path=/docs/search-filter-querybuilder--docs

**When to use**

- Saved segments, alert rules, automation triggers — conditions people compose and come back to.
- Operators beyond “is”: greater than, between, contains, is empty.

**When not to use**

- Filtering a list on the spot → use Filter or FilterField
- One or two fixed conditions → use a form with plain fields

**Anatomy**

- Match: all (AND) or any (OR) of the conditions.
- Condition row: field → operator (by field type) → value editor of the right kind.
- Add / remove: `addLabel`, `maxConditions`; an empty state when there are none.

**QueryBuilder props**

- `fields`: `QueryField[]`
- `addLabel?`: `string`, default `Add condition (localized: queryBuilder.add)`
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`, default `Filter conditions (localized: queryBuilder.label)`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `QueryValue`
- `emptyMessage?`: `ReactNode`, default `No conditions yet. Add one to start filtering. (localized: queryBuilder.empty)`
- `maxConditions?`: `number`
- `onChange?`: `((value: QueryValue) => void)`
- `value?`: `QueryValue`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A rule people build once and keep: “active and fewer than 2 replicas”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-[34rem] max-w-full">
    <QueryBuilder
      fields={FIELDS}
      ariaLabel="Alert rule"
      defaultValue={{
        match: 'all',
        conditions: [
          { id: 'c1', field: 'status', operator: 'is', value: 'active' },
          { id: 'c2', field: 'replicas', operator: 'lt', value: 2 },
        ],
      }}
    />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A whole builder to show active servers — a Filter does it in one click.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-[34rem] max-w-full">
    <QueryBuilder
      fields={FIELDS}
      ariaLabel="Filter servers"
      defaultValue={{ match: 'all', conditions: [{ id: 'd1', field: 'status', operator: 'is', value: 'active' }] }}
    />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a named group (`ariaLabel`); each row’s controls are named after its field (“Status condition”, “Remove Status condition”).
- Adding or removing a row keeps focus in the builder — on the new row’s field, a neighbouring remove button, or Add.
- Say the result in words near it when you can (“Matches 4 servers”).

## Radio

`import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/radio';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-radio--docs

**When to use**

- Exactly one of 2–5 options, all visible so people can compare them.
- A choice where the difference needs a line of explanation (description under each option).

**When not to use**

- More than 5 options → use Select (6–15) or Combobox (over 15)
- Several options at once → use CheckboxGroup
- Options that need a picture, price or several lines → use OptionCard
- A single on/off → use Switch or Checkbox

**Anatomy**

- Group: vertical with a 12px gap; `orientation="horizontal"` for 2–3 short options.
- Radio: dot plus `label`.
- Description (optional): a line under the label.

**Radio props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, RadioGroupProps, RadioProps$1.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A sensible default is selected, and “Off” is an option rather than an empty group.

  ```tsx
  <RadioGroup defaultValue="daily" aria-label="Backup frequency">
    <Radio value="daily" label="Daily" description="Kept for 7 days" />
    <Radio value="weekly" label="Weekly" description="Kept for 4 weeks" />
    <Radio value="off" label="Off" />
  </RadioGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: Checkboxes for a one-of choice let people pick both or none.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Daily" />
    <Checkbox label="Weekly" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name the group: `aria-label`, or put it in a `FormSection`/fieldset with a legend.
- Tab enters the group once; arrows move and select. Don’t make each radio a separate tab stop.
- Pre-select a default when one is safe — a group with nothing selected can’t be reset by keyboard.

## RangeField

`import { RangeField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/range-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-rangefield--docs

**When to use**

- A numeric range people set roughly and sometimes exactly: price filter, size, response time.
- Filters that fetch — `onValueCommit` fires once per finished change.

**When not to use**

- A single value → use Slider or NumberField
- A date span → use DateRangePicker

**Anatomy**

- Label: `label`, with the unit.
- Histogram (optional): `histogram` — how many items fall in each bucket.
- Two-thumb slider: for a quick rough pick.
- From / To fields: NumberFields for exact bounds; they can’t cross.

**RangeField props**

- `label`: `ReactNode`
- `max`: `number`
- `min`: `number`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `RangeValue`
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `formatValue?`: `((value: number) => string)`, default `(v) => String(v)` — Formats values for the summary and for screen readers, e.g. `(v) => \`€${v}\``.
- `fromLabel?`: `string`, default `From (localized: rangeField.from)` — Visible labels over the two inputs.
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `histogram?`: `number[]` — Counts per equal-width bucket from min to max, drawn above the track.
- `minDistance?`: `number`, default `0` — Smallest allowed gap between the two bounds, in value units.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: RangeValue) => void)` — Live, on every drag tick and committed input.
- `onValueCommit?`: `((value: RangeValue) => void)` — Once per finished change — thumb released or a bound committed.
- `step?`: `number`, default `1`
- `toLabel?`: `string`, default `To (localized: rangeField.to)`
- `value?`: `RangeValue`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Drag for a rough span, type for an exact one; the histogram shows where items are.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72">
    <RangeField label="Price, $" min={0} max={500} step={10} defaultValue={[50, 300]} histogram={[2, 5, 9, 14, 11, 7, 4, 3, 2, 1]} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A bare two-thumb slider: no values shown, no way to type $120.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72">
    <Slider aria-label="Price" min={0} max={500} defaultValue={[50, 300]} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Thumbs are named “From” and “To” with the label; the fields repeat them for typing.
- Change `fromLabel`/`toLabel` together with the slider names if the bounds have other words (“Min”, “Max”).
- Results updated by the filter should be announced in a live region by the page, not by the field.

## Rating

`import { Rating, RatingStar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/rating';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-rating--docs

**When to use**

- Leaving a 1–5 score (review form).
- `readOnly`: showing an average next to a review count, with fractional stars.

**When not to use**

- Satisfaction on a labelled scale (“Very poor … Excellent”) → use RadioGroup
- A single like/favourite → use Toggle or RatingStar

**Anatomy**

- Stars: one radio each in input mode; `size` sm 16px / md 24px.
- Value text (optional): the number and review count next to read-only stars.

**Rating props**

- `clearable?`: `boolean`, default `false` — A click on the currently selected star resets the rating to 0.
- `defaultValue?`: `number`, default `0`
- `formatLabel?`: `((value: number, max: number) => string)`, default `localized: rating.value` — Accessible text for a value ("3 of 5"). Localize here.
- `max?`: `number`, default `5` — Number of stars. Default 5.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: number) => void)`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Display only: one image named by the value, fractional values allowed.
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `value?`: `number` — Controlled value, 0 = no rating. Fractions are drawn only in readOnly.

**RatingStar props**

- `fill`: `number`
- `size?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: RadioGroupProps, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Stars plus the number and count — stars alone don’t say 4.6 vs 4.4.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Rating readOnly value={4.6} size="sm" />
    <span className="font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">4.6 · 128 reviews</span>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Stars with no number or count: imprecise and unweighted.

  ```tsx
  <Rating readOnly value={4.6} size="md" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Input mode is a radio group: arrows change the score, each star is named “3 of 5”.
- Read-only is one image named with the exact value (“4.6 of 5”); `formatLabel` changes the wording.
- Filled vs empty differs in shape (solid vs outline), not only color.

## Resizable

`import { ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/resizable';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-resizable--docs

**When to use**

- Work views where people balance two or three panes themselves: file tree + editor, list + details, editor + preview.

**When not to use**

- Page layout that should just adapt → use responsive CSS
- A details panel that opens and closes → use PushSheet

**Anatomy**

- Group: `orientation` horizontal/vertical.
- Panels: `defaultSize`, `minSize` so no pane collapses to nothing.
- Handle: `withHandle` grip; named per pane (“Resize file tree”).

**ResizableHandle props**

- `withHandle?`: `boolean`, default `false`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Sensible minimums and a named, visible grip.

  ```tsx
  <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className={BOX}>
    <ResizablePanel defaultSize="35%" minSize="25%"><div className={PANE}>Files</div></ResizablePanel>
    <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize file list" />
    <ResizablePanel defaultSize="65%" minSize="40%"><div className={PANE}>Editor</div></ResizablePanel>
  </ResizablePanelGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: No minimums and a hairline handle: panes can vanish, and the handle is hard to find.

  ```tsx
  <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className={BOX}>
    <ResizablePanel defaultSize="35%" minSize="0%"><div className={PANE}>Files</div></ResizablePanel>
    <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize panel" />
    <ResizablePanel defaultSize="65%" minSize="0%"><div className={PANE}>Editor</div></ResizablePanel>
  </ResizablePanelGroup>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The handle is role="separator": arrow keys resize, Home/End jump, double-click resets.
- Give each handle an `aria-label` that names what it resizes.

## Reveal

`import { Reveal, RevealGroup } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/reveal';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-reveal--docs

**When to use**

- Landing and marketing pages: feature blocks, cards, a pricing row easing in as the reader scrolls down.
- A group of similar items (`RevealGroup`) — they arrive one after another, 90ms apart.

**When not to use**

- Product UI — dashboards, forms, tables, settings → use no motion: content should just be there
- The only copy of something essential above the fold (it stays hidden until the page script runs)
- Something appearing because of a user action → use Collapsible, Dialog or the component’s own transition

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: the element entering the viewport (`threshold`, `once`).
- Effect: `rise` (default), `fade`, `scale`, `blur` — `duration-slower` on `ease-glide`.
- Stagger (optional): `RevealGroup` delays each direct child by `stagger` ms.

**Reveal props**

- `asChild?`: `boolean` — Animate the child element itself instead of a wrapping div.
- `delay?`: `number`, default `0` — Wait this long (ms) after the element comes into view.
- `effect?`: `"scale" | "blur" | "rise" | "fade"`, default `rise` — How the content enters.
- `once?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Play once (default) or every time it scrolls back into view.
- `threshold?`: `number`, default `0.2` — Share of the element that must be visible before it starts, 0–1.

**RevealGroup props**

- `delay?`: `number`, default `0` — Wait this long (ms) after the element comes into view.
- `effect?`: `"scale" | "blur" | "rise" | "fade"`, default `rise` — How the content enters.
- `once?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Play once (default) or every time it scrolls back into view.
- `stagger?`: `number`, default `90` — Time between one child and the next, ms.
- `threshold?`: `number`, default `0.2` — Share of the element that must be visible before it starts, 0–1.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One quiet entrance per block, the first time it’s seen.

  ```tsx
  <Reveal className="rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-2xl)] border border-solid border-[var(--color-border-border-subtle)] p-4 text-body-m">Feature block rises in once.</Reveal>
  ```

- Don’t: Replaying on every scroll, mixing effects on one page: motion turns into noise.

  ```tsx
  <Reveal once={false} effect="blur" className="rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-2xl)] border border-solid border-[var(--color-border-border-subtle)] p-4 text-body-m">Blurs in every time it scrolls past.</Reveal>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- prefers-reduced-motion: content shows at once, with no transition and no waiting for the scroll position.
- Only opacity and transform change, so the layout never moves and nothing is announced twice.
- Hidden content is still in the accessibility tree; don’t hide anything from screen readers with it.

## RichTextEditor

`import { RichTextEditor } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/rich-text-editor';`

Status: beta · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-richtexteditor--docs

**When to use**

- Text that is published or sent with formatting: announcements, product descriptions, email templates, ticket replies.
- Short replies and comments with a reduced toolbar (`RICH_TEXT_TOOLS_BASIC`).

**When not to use**

- Plain multi-line text → use TextArea
- One line (a title, a name) → use TextField
- Code, config, Markdown source → use CodeEditor
- Long documents with layout → use a dedicated editor or a doc tool

**Anatomy**

- Label / description: as in TextField.
- Toolbar (optional): controls from `tools`, in order; `[]` hides it.
- Editing area: styled like `Prose`; grows between `minHeight` and `maxHeight`, then scrolls.
- Counter (optional): with `maxLength`; typing past it is blocked.
- Error (optional): message under the field.

**RichTextEditor props**

- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`, default ``
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `error?`: `ReactNode` — `true` for error styling only, or a message.
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `maxHeight?`: `string | number`
- `maxLength?`: `number` — Character limit with a counter under the field (typing past it is blocked).
- `minHeight?`: `string | number`, default `160` — Editing area height.
- `name?`: `string` — Hidden input with the HTML, for plain form posts.
- `onEditorReady?`: `((editor: Editor) => void)` — Gives access to the Tiptap editor (e.g. to read JSON or text).
- `onValueChange?`: `((html: string) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `tools?`: `RichTextTool[]`, default `['textStyle', 'bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'strike', 'code', 'link', 'bulletList', 'orderedList', 'blockquote', 'codeBlock', 'history']` — Which toolbar controls to show, in order. `[]` hides the toolbar.
- `value?`: `string` — HTML.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A reply needs bold, links and lists — nothing more.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96"><RichTextEditor label="Reply" tools={RICH_TEXT_TOOLS_BASIC} placeholder="Write a reply…" minHeight={72} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Headings, code blocks and quotes for a two-line reply: a wall of buttons.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96"><RichTextEditor label="Reply" placeholder="Write a reply…" minHeight={72} /></div>
  ```

- Do: A title is one line — a text field.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Announcement title" defaultValue="Scheduled maintenance" widthSize="lg" />
  ```

- Don’t: Formatting a title invites bold-italic headlines that break the page style.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-96"><RichTextEditor label="Announcement title" defaultValue="<p>Scheduled maintenance</p>" tools={['bold', 'italic']} minHeight={40} /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Always a label (`label` or `aria-label`); the area is a multi-line textbox with its description, error and required state.
- The toolbar is one tab stop with arrow keys inside; buttons show pressed state and their shortcuts (⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘K…).
- Tab leaves the editor (inside a list it nests the item) — focus isn’t trapped.
- Headings in the text style menu start at H2, so content never adds a second H1 to the page.

## Scheduler

`import { Scheduler } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/scheduler';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-scheduler--docs

**When to use**

- Events placed in time: maintenance windows, bookings, shifts, release plans.
- Rescheduling by drag (`onEventChange`) and creating from an empty slot (`onSlotClick`).

**When not to use**

- Picking a date or a range → use DatePicker or DateRangePicker
- Past events as a log → use Timeline
- Work by stage, not by time → use Kanban
- A few upcoming items → use a list with dates

**Anatomy**

- Header: Today, previous / next, the visible range, view switch.
- Grid: day / week time grid with an all-day row and a “now” line; month grid with “+N more”. On phones the week is a list of days.
- Event: title and time; `tone` for its kind; `locked` can’t be moved.

**Scheduler props**

- `events`: `SchedulerEvent[]`
- `date?`: `Date` — The date the visible range is built around.
- `defaultDate?`: `Date`
- `defaultView?`: `"month" | "week" | "day"` — Starting view when `view` isn't controlled. Unset: `day` on phones (below 640px), `week` elsewhere.
- `hourHeight?`: `number`, default `48` — Pixel height of one hour in week/day view.
- `locale?`: `string`
- `maxEventsPerDay?`: `number`, default `3` — Month view: chips per day before "+N more".
- `now?`: `Date` — Fixed "now" for stories/tests; defaults to the real clock.
- `onDateChange?`: `((date: Date) => void)`
- `onEventChange?`: `((event: SchedulerEvent, next: { start: Date; end: Date; }) => void)` — Drag/resize finished. Omit to make events read-only.
- `onEventClick?`: `((event: SchedulerEvent) => void)`
- `onSlotClick?`: `((range: { start: Date; end: Date; allDay: boolean; }) => void)` — Empty slot clicked: a 1-hour range in week/day view, a whole day in month view.
- `onViewChange?`: `((view: SchedulerView) => void)`
- `scrollToHour?`: `number`, default `8` — Hour the time grid scrolls to on open.
- `view?`: `"month" | "week" | "day"`
- `views?`: `SchedulerView[]`, default `['day', 'week', 'month']`
- `weekStartsOn?`: `"0" | "1" | "2" | "3" | "4" | "5" | "6"`, default `1`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Tone marks the kind of event: risky work warning, a release success.

  ```tsx
  <Scheduler {...mini} events={GOOD} />
  ```

- Don’t: Danger for a planning meeting: color stops meaning anything.

  ```tsx
  <Scheduler {...mini} events={BAD} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Events are buttons named with title and time; the visible range is announced when it changes.
- Drag isn’t the only way: clicking an event should open an editor with date and time fields.
- On phones the week is a list: seven time columns would make each event a few pixels wide, under the 24px target size (WCAG 2.5.8).
- Set `locale` and `weekStartsOn` for the user, not the server.
- Tone is never the only signal — say the kind in the title or details.

## ScrollArea

`import { ScrollArea } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/scroll-area';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-scrollarea--docs

**When to use**

- A region that must scroll inside a fixed space: a list in a popover or panel, a log, a long menu.
- The overlay thumb takes no width, so content doesn’t shift when it appears.

**When not to use**

- The page itself → use normal document scrolling
- Nested scroll inside scroll on mobile → use let the content grow

**Anatomy**

- Root: needs a height: `h-72` or a cap like `max-h-60`.
- Viewport: a tab stop when content overflows (`focusable`); name it with `aria-label`.
- Scrollbar: thin translucent thumb, no track; shows on hover/scroll.

**ScrollArea props**

- `focusable?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `viewportClassName?`: `string`
- `viewportRef?`: `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`

Also accepts the props of: ScrollAreaProps, HTMLAttributes, ScrollAreaScrollbarProps, ScrollAreaScrollbarVisibleProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A capped list that scrolls in place; the rest of the panel stays put.

  ```tsx
  <ScrollArea className={`${BOX} h-48`} aria-label="Backups">
    {ITEMS.map((t) => <div key={t} className={ROW}>{t}</div>)}
  </ScrollArea>
  ```

- Don’t: A one-row window: people scroll more than they read — show more or paginate.

  ```tsx
  <ScrollArea className={`${BOX} h-12`} aria-label="Backups, tiny">
    {ITEMS.map((t) => <div key={t} className={ROW}>{t}</div>)}
  </ScrollArea>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The viewport is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it with arrows; give it a name.
- Native wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling are kept.

## SecretField

`import { SecretField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/secret-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-secretfield--docs

**When to use**

- Showing a secret the person needs to copy: API key, token, webhook secret, recovery code.

**When not to use**

- Typing a password → use Password
- Values that aren’t secret → use text + CopyButton

**Anatomy**

- Value: masked by default, monospaced.
- Reveal (optional): `revealable` — show/hide.
- Copy: copies without revealing; confirms with a toast.

**SecretField props**

- `value`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `copyToastTitle?`: `string`, default `Copied (localized: secretField.copied)` — Title of the copy-success toast. Default "Copied".
- `defaultRevealed?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `label?`: `string`, default `Value (localized: secretField.label)`
- `revealable?`: `boolean`, default `true`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Masked until asked; copy works without showing it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><SecretField label="API key" value="sk_live_9f2c41aa7b3e" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A secret in plain text ends up in screenshots and screen shares.

  ```tsx
  <code className="font-mono text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text)]">sk_live_9f2c41aa7b3e</code>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Reveal and Copy are named buttons (“Show API key”, “Copy API key”).
- Copy success is announced; the value itself isn’t read out while masked.

## Select

`import { Select, SelectGroup, SelectValue, SelectTrigger, SelectContent, SelectLabel, SelectItem, SelectSeparator, SelectScrollUpButton, SelectScrollDownButton } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/select';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-select--docs

**When to use**

- One choice from 6–15 known options (up to 5 → RadioGroup, over 15 → Combobox).
- Values people recognise rather than type: a region, a plan, a sort order.

**When not to use**

- Up to 5 options — show them all → use RadioGroup or ToggleGroup
- Long lists people search in → use Combobox
- Several values at once → use CheckboxGroup or TagInput
- Actions, not values → use DropdownMenu

**Anatomy**

- Label: above the trigger.
- Trigger: shows the value or a placeholder; `widthSize` / `heightSize` match TextField.
- Content: the list; can be grouped with labels and separators.
- Item: one option; the selected one is checked.

**Select props**

- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`

**SelectTrigger props**

- `error?`: `boolean` — Turns the trigger danger-styled (border + bg together, matching TextField's own error variant). Stays danger while the popup is open too — see the InvalidOpen story for why that needs its own rule.
- `widthSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "full"`, default `md`

**SelectItem props**

- `badge?`: `{ label: ReactNode; tone?: StatusTone; }` — Pill shown after the text, before the checkmark space.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Second line under the text, smaller and subtler — for extra context, not truncated interaction.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon shown before the text — 16px by default, decorative. Pass `iconSize="lg"` for the 32px media variant (bold label, matches the Figma media-icon item). Mutually exclusive with `tone` — same slot.
- `iconSize?`: `"lg" | "sm"`, default `sm`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"` — Tone of a colored status dot before the text instead of `icon` — same slot, so passing both just shows the dot.

Also accepts the props of: SelectSharedProps, HTMLAttributes, SelectValueProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, SelectContentProps, SelectContentImplProps, PopperContentProps, SelectItemProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Up to 5 options: show them all as radios — compared at a glance, picked in one click.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <span id="gl-sel-billing-radio" className="font-body text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
      Billing
    </span>
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="monthly" aria-labelledby="gl-sel-billing-radio">
      <Radio value="monthly" label="Monthly" />
      <Radio value="quarterly" label="Quarterly" />
      <Radio value="yearly" label="Yearly" />
    </RadioGroup>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Three options hidden in a select — an extra click to see what the choices even are.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-sel-billing">Billing</Label>
    <Select defaultValue="monthly">
      <SelectTrigger id="gl-sel-billing" widthSize="md">
        <SelectValue />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="monthly">Monthly</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="quarterly">Quarterly</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="yearly">Yearly</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </div>
  ```

- Do: 8 regions — in the 6–15 range a Select fits. No answer yet, so the placeholder says what to pick.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-sel-region">Data region</Label>
    <Select>
      <SelectTrigger id="gl-sel-region" widthSize="md">
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a region" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {regionItems}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A preselected answer to a question that matters gets accepted without being read.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-sel-region2">Data region</Label>
    <Select defaultValue="eu-central">
      <SelectTrigger id="gl-sel-region2" widthSize="md">
        <SelectValue />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {regionItems}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Label it: a `Label` with `htmlFor` on the trigger’s id, or `aria-label` on the trigger.
- Arrow keys move, typing jumps to a matching option, Escape closes without changing the value.
- Never navigate or submit on change — choosing an option should only choose it.

## Separator

`import { Separator } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/separator';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-separator--docs

**When to use**

- A quiet line between groups that spacing alone doesn’t separate: menu groups, list rows, toolbar sections.

**When not to use**

- Between every element → use spacing
- Inline facts in a line → use DotSeparator

**Anatomy**

- Line: horizontal or vertical; `emphasis` subtle (default) or strong.

**Separator props**

- `emphasis?`: `"strong" | "subtle"`, default `subtle` — Line weight. `subtle` (default) stays below interactive borders; `strong` matches a form-field border.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, SeparatorProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One line where the group changes.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-3">
    <span className={ROW}>Profile</span>
    <span className={ROW}>Billing</span>
    <Separator />
    <span className={ROW}>Sign out</span>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A strong line under every row: everything is separated, so nothing is grouped.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-3">
    <span className={ROW}>Profile</span>
    <Separator emphasis="strong" />
    <span className={ROW}>Billing</span>
    <Separator emphasis="strong" />
    <span className={ROW}>Sign out</span>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decorative by default (hidden from screen readers). Pass `decorative={false}` only when the line marks a real boundary that should be announced.

## Sidebar

`import { Sidebar, SidebarProvider, SidebarHeader, SidebarBrand, SidebarNav, SidebarSection, SidebarItem, SidebarFooter, SidebarCollapse } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/sidebar';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-sidebar--docs

**When to use**

- App navigation with several sections people switch between all day.
- Grouped destinations, counts and per-item actions; collapses to an icon rail.

**When not to use**

- Two to four sections → use Tabs or NavigationMenu
- Content filters → use Filter or FacetedList

**Anatomy**

- Header: `SidebarBrand` and `SidebarCollapse`.
- Sections: `SidebarSection label` groups related items.
- Item: icon, label, `badge`, hover `actions`; `active` marks the current page.
- Footer (optional): account, help.

**Sidebar props**

- `inverse?`: `boolean` — Dark, inverse-color rail regardless of the page's own theme — sets

**SidebarProvider props**

- `defaultCollapsed?`: `boolean`, default `false`

**SidebarSection props**

- `action?`: `ReactNode`
- `label?`: `string`

**SidebarItem props**

- `actions?`: `ReactNode` — DropdownMenuItem(s) for a hover-revealed "more actions" trigger. Omit for no trigger. Hidden when the rail is collapsed.
- `active?`: `boolean`
- `badge?`: `ReactNode`
- `badgeTone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `neutral` — Tone for the badge pill (e.g. a notification count). Default 'neutral'.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Grouped, with the current page marked.

  ```tsx
  <SidebarProvider>
    <div className={BOX}>
      <SidebarNav aria-label="Grouped navigation example">
        <SidebarSection label="Manage">
          <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<HomeSimple />}>Dashboard</SidebarItem>
          <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Globe />} active badge="128">Sites</SidebarItem>
          <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Database />}>Databases</SidebarItem>
        </SidebarSection>
        <SidebarSection label="Account">
          <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<User />}>Team</SidebarItem>
          <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Settings />}>Settings</SidebarItem>
        </SidebarSection>
      </SidebarNav>
    </div>
  </SidebarProvider>
  ```

- Don’t: Nine items in one flat list, nothing marked as current: hard to scan, no “you are here”.

  ```tsx
  <SidebarProvider>
    <div className={BOX}>
      <SidebarNav aria-label="Flat navigation example">
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<HomeSimple />}>Dashboard</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Globe />}>Sites</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Database />}>Databases</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Mail />}>Email</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<ShieldCheck />}>Certificates</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Key />}>Credentials</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Archive />}>Backups</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<User />}>Team</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="#gl-sb" icon={<Settings />}>Settings</SidebarItem>
      </SidebarNav>
    </div>
  </SidebarProvider>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Items are a `nav` (“Main” by default); the active one has `aria-current="page"`.
- Items without href render as buttons, so they’re still keyboard-reachable.
- Collapsed: labels are visually hidden but stay as accessible names (no tooltips yet, and badges are hidden); focus follows the collapse toggle.
- Below md it’s a slide-over drawer with focus trap and Escape.

## Skeleton

`import { Skeleton } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/skeleton';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-skeleton--docs

**When to use**

- First load of content whose shape is known: a card, a list, a profile header.
- Short waits, roughly under a few seconds.

**When not to use**

- Table rows → use TableSkeleton
- A task with known percent done → use Progress
- Reloading data that is already shown → use keep the old data and show a subtle busy state
- Nothing to show → use EmptyState

**Anatomy**

- Block: a pulsing shape; size it with `className` to the content it stands in for.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Same layout as the real item — nothing jumps when it loads.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-72 items-center gap-3">
    <Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" />
    <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />
      <Skeleton className="h-3 w-48" />
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: One big block: the layout shifts when content arrives.

  ```tsx
  <Skeleton className="h-24 w-72 rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-lg)]" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Skeletons are hidden from screen readers; mark the loading region aria-busy="true" and remove it when done.
- Fully rounded by default; give blocks (images, cards) a block radius. The sweep stops with reduced motion.
- Don’t put focusable elements inside a loading region.

## Slider

`import { Slider } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/slider';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-slider--docs

**When to use**

- A value where roughly right is good enough and seeing the position helps: volume, concurrency, a budget.
- Two thumbs for a range, when the exact numbers matter less than the span.

**When not to use**

- An exact number → use NumberField
- A range people also want to type → use RangeField
- A handful of named steps → use RadioGroup or ToggleGroup

**Anatomy**

- Track and range: the filled part shows the value.
- Thumb: one per value; `defaultValue` is an array.
- Value text: show the number next to it; `formatValue` is also what screen readers hear.

**Slider props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string` — Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
- `aria-label?`: `string` — Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `defaultValue?`: `number[]`
- `formatValue?`: `((value: number, index: number) => string)` — Map a thumb's numeric value to a human-readable string for aria-valuetext.
- `invalid?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Marks the slider as invalid — track fill + thumb switch to danger colors.
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: number[]) => void)`
- `value?`: `number[]`

Also accepts the props of: SliderProps, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A rough value with the number shown.

  ```tsx
  <ConcurrencyExample />
  ```

- Don’t: An exact number on a 65 535-step track, no value shown — nobody hits 8080 by dragging.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-64 flex-col gap-3">
    <span className="font-body text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">Port</span>
    <Slider aria-label="Port" min={1} max={65535} defaultValue={[8080]} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Each thumb is a `slider`: arrows step, Page Up/Down take bigger steps, Home/End jump to the ends.
- Every thumb needs a name — `aria-label`, and for a range say which end (“Minimum budget”).
- Pass `formatValue` when the number has a unit, so it’s read as “$40”, not “40”.

## Toaster

`import { Toaster } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/sonner';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-toaster--docs

**When to use**

- Short feedback on an action just taken: saved, sent, copied, failed.
- A background task’s progress (`toast.progress`) or result (`toast.promise`).

**When not to use**

- An error people must fix on this page (form, field) → use Alert or the field’s error
- Something that needs a decision → use AlertDialog
- Undo after a destructive action → use UndoToast
- Site-wide news → use AnnouncementBar

**Anatomy**

- Icon (optional): by type: success, info, warning, error.
- Title: what happened, in past tense.
- Description (optional): the object or detail.
- Action (optional): one: Retry, View, Open.
- Close: on every toast by default.

**Toaster props**

- `dark?`: `boolean`, default `false`

Also accepts the props of: ToasterProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: What happened, to what.

  ```tsx
  <Fire label="Show good toast" run={() => toast.success('Certificate issued', { description: 'shop.seashell.dev · valid 90 days' })} />
  ```

- Don’t: “Success!” — of what?

  ```tsx
  <Fire label="Show vague toast" run={() => toast.success('Success!')} />
  ```

- Do: Errors stay until closed and offer a retry.

  ```tsx
  <Fire label="Show error toast" run={() => toast.error('Couldn’t reissue certificate', { description: 'DNS check failed for shop.seashell.dev', action: { label: 'Retry', onClick: () => {} } })} />
  ```

- Don’t: A field error in a toast: it’s far from the field and the user has to find it.

  ```tsx
  <Fire label="Show field error as toast" run={() => toast.error('Email is invalid')} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Toasts are announced politely; errors don’t auto-close, so there is time to read and act.
- Never put the only path to something in a toast — it may be gone before people get to it.
- Mount `<Toaster />` once at the app root and use `toast` from this module.

## Sparkline

`import { Sparkline } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/sparkline';`

Status: stable · Category: Charts
Docs: ./?path=/docs/charts-sparkline--docs

**When to use**

- The shape of a trend next to its number: a stat card, a table cell, a list row.

**When not to use**

- When people need values, axes or comparisons → use AreaChart or LineChart
- Without a number beside it → use show the number, or a full chart

**Anatomy**

- Line: `tone` (brand, success, warning, danger, info, muted); optional `area`.
- Last point (optional): `showLast` dot on the latest value.

**Sparkline props**

- `data`: `number[]`
- `area?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Soft gradient area fill under the line.
- `ariaLabel?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `height?`: `number`, default `32`
- `showLast?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Dot on the latest point.
- `tone?`: `"info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "muted" | "brand"`, default `brand`
- `width?`: `number` — Fixed width in px; omit for fluid (fills the container).

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The number says how much, the line says which way.

  ```tsx
  <div className={TILE}>
    <div className="flex flex-col">
      <span className="font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtler)]">Requests</span>
      <span className="font-body text-heading-xs font-semibold tabular-nums text-[var(--color-text-text)]">4.2M</span>
    </div>
    <Sparkline data={[3, 5, 4, 6, 5, 7, 9]} width={96} ariaLabel="Requests trending up over 7 days." />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A line with no number: up — from what, to what?

  ```tsx
  <div className={TILE}>
    <span className="font-body text-body-s text-[var(--color-text-text-subtler)]">Requests</span>
    <Sparkline data={[3, 5, 4, 6, 5, 7, 9]} width={96} ariaLabel="Requests." />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- One `role="img"`: its `ariaLabel` must say the trend (“trending up over 7 days”).
- The value lives in text beside it — the sparkline has no tooltip.

## Spinner

`import { Spinner } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/spinner';`

Status: beta · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-spinner--docs

**When to use**

- A short wait inside a control or a small area: a button that is saving, a list that is loading, a file being read.

**When not to use**

- A whole page or a layout that is loading → use Skeleton
- Work with a known amount done → use Progress
- A button’s own loading state → use Button loading (it already uses Spinner)

**Anatomy**

- Track: a faint ring.
- Arc: grows and shrinks while the ring turns.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Next to text that says what is loading.

  ```tsx
  <p className="flex items-center gap-2 font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">
    <Spinner className="size-4 text-[var(--color-icon-icon-primary)]" />
    Loading domains…
  </p>
  ```

- Don’t: Several spinners at once — show one for the area that is waiting.

  ```tsx
  <p className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Spinner className="size-4" />
    <Spinner className="size-4" />
    <Spinner className="size-4" />
  </p>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decorative (aria-hidden). Mark the waiting region aria-busy, or add a role="status" text such as “Loading domains”.
- With reduced motion the arc stops and the spinner slowly fades in and out.

## SplitButton

`import { SplitButton } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/split-button';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-splitbutton--docs

**When to use**

- One main action with a few variations of it: “Deploy” / Deploy to staging / Deploy without cache.
- The main action is what people want most of the time; the rest are occasional.

**When not to use**

- Unrelated actions → use separate Buttons or a DropdownMenu
- When none of the options is clearly the default → use DropdownMenu button
- Destructive variants hidden in the menu

**Anatomy**

- Main segment: a Button running `onMainClick`; `leftIcon` if any.
- Caret segment: opens the menu; named by `menuLabel`.
- Menu: `menuContent`: DropdownMenuItems — variants of the main action.

**SplitButton props**

- `children`: `ReactNode` — Label + icon(s) for the primary (left) action.
- `menuContent`: `ReactNode` — Content rendered inside the DropdownMenu opened by the caret — typically DropdownMenuItem elements.
- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `filled`
- `badge?`: `ReactNode | ButtonBadge` — Count or status pinned to the top-right corner (a BadgeIndicator, sm,
- `badgeLabel?`: `string` — What the badge means, read after the button's name ("5 unread",
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered before the label (or the sole icon when iconOnly is set).
- `loading?`: `boolean` — Shows a spinner in place of leftIcon and disables the button. Not supported with asChild.
- `menuLabel?`: `string`, default `More actions (localized: splitButton.menu)` — Accessible name of the caret that opens the menu. Default "More actions" — make it specific when several split buttons share a screen, e.g. "More send options".
- `onMainClick?`: `(() => void)` — Called when the primary action is clicked.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon rendered after the label.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`, default `lg`
- `softDisabled?`: `boolean` — Soft-disable: looks disabled and ignores clicks/Enter/Space, but stays
- `success?`: `boolean` — The action just succeeded: a tick draws itself in place of leftIcon (Kinetics'
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The menu holds variants of the same action.

  ```tsx
  <SplitButton
    size="md"
    menuLabel="More deploy options"
    menuContent={
      <>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Deploy to staging</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Deploy without cache</DropdownMenuItem>
      </>
    }
  >
    Deploy
  </SplitButton>
  ```

- Don’t: Three buttons for one action crowd the bar; the rare variants belong in the menu.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button size="md">Deploy</Button>
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Deploy to staging</Button>
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Without cache</Button>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Give the caret a specific `menuLabel` when there are several on a screen: “More send options”.
- Two tab stops: the main action and the caret.

## Stat

`import { Stat } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/stat';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-stat--docs

**When to use**

- Headline numbers on a dashboard or overview: active sites, uptime, revenue — 2 to 4 in a row.
- A number with its trend against a previous period.

**When not to use**

- Counts repeated as rows in a card → use Metric
- A trend people need to read → use Sparkline or LineChart
- A fill level → use Meter

**Anatomy**

- Label: what is counted.
- Value: big, tabular numbers.
- Status (optional): dot or `toneIcon` with a word for screen readers (`tone`, `toneLabel`).
- Icon (optional): top-right, decorative.
- Delta (optional): change with direction (`delta`).

**Stat props**

- `label`: `string`
- `value`: `ReactNode` — A string/number is the common case (tabular-nums); a ReactNode is allowed for a composite value.
- `delta?`: `StatDelta`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Optional icon, rendered muted in the top-right corner.
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`
- `toneIcon?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Render a ToneIcon instead of a bare StatusDot for the tone signal.
- `toneLabel?`: `string` — Word conveying the status meaning for assistive tech. Defaults to a per-tone word.
- `variant?`: `"card" | "plain"`, default `card`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A number, and how it changed against what.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-56"><Stat label="Active sites" value={128} icon={<Globe />} delta={{ value: '+12% vs last month', direction: 'up' }} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A sentence in the value slot: nothing to read at a glance.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-56"><Stat label="Sites" value="128 active, 4 suspended, 2 with errors" /></div>
  ```

- Do: Tone when the value itself is good or bad.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-56"><Stat label="Uptime, 30 days" value="99.98%" tone="success" /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Danger on a neutral count makes people look for a problem.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-56"><Stat label="Team members" value={14} tone="danger" /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A named group; the tone is announced as a word (“healthy”, “critical”), not color.
- Delta direction is in the text too (“+12%”); the arrow is decorative.
- Inside a Card use `variant="plain"` — one border, not two.

## StatusDot

`import { StatusDot } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/status-dot';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-statusdot--docs

**When to use**

- Live state next to its text label: Running, Stopped, Degraded, Online.
- Dense lists and tables where a Badge would be too heavy.

**When not to use**

- A status that should stand out → use Badge
- A count or “new” mark on an icon → use BadgeIndicator

**Anatomy**

- Dot: 7px, `tone`; `inverse` on a forced-dark surface.
- Label: a sibling text — always.

**StatusDot props**

- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The word says the state; the dot helps scanning.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-body-s">
  ```
