  ```tsx
    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" />Running</span>
    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" />Stopped</span>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Color alone: not everyone can tell these two apart.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-body-s">
    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" />web-01</span>
    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" />web-02</span>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The dot is presentational — the text label carries the status.
- On a forced-dark surface (Terminal header, dark toast) use `inverse` so the dot keeps its contrast.

## Stepper

`import { Stepper } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/stepper';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-stepper--docs

**When to use**

- A process done in order over several screens: onboarding, checkout, a setup wizard.
- 3–5 steps with short labels.

**When not to use**

- Sections people visit in any order → use Tabs
- Progress of a background task → use Progress
- A location in a hierarchy → use Breadcrumb

**Anatomy**

- Indicator: number, or a check when complete; color is never the only signal.
- Label and description: short; `labelAlign` start or center.
- Orientation: horizontal, or vertical for long labels and narrow space.
- Back to a step (optional): `onStepClick` makes completed steps clickable.

**Stepper props**

- `current`: `number` — 0-based index of the in-progress step.
- `steps`: `StepperStep[]`
- `labelAlign?`: `"center" | "start"`, default `start` — Horizontal only: "start" matches the indicator's left edge; "center" pins under it (short labels only).
- `onStepClick?`: `((index: number) => void)` — Makes completed steps clickable (their label becomes a button), so
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `horizontal`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, OlHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Four short steps; where you are and what’s left is clear at a glance.

  ```tsx
  <Stepper
    className="w-[30rem] max-w-full"
    current={1}
    steps={[{ label: 'Account' }, { label: 'Plan' }, { label: 'Payment' }, { label: 'Review' }]}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: Nine steps: labels get crushed and the process feels endless — merge steps or go vertical.

  ```tsx
  <Stepper
    className="w-[30rem] max-w-full"
    current={3}
    steps={['Account', 'Email', 'Password', 'Company', 'Team', 'Plan', 'Billing', 'Payment', 'Review'].map((label) => ({ label }))}
  />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- An ordered list; each step says its status in words (“completed”, “current step”), and the current one has `aria-current="step"`.
- Clickable completed steps are buttons; upcoming steps aren’t interactive.
- Move focus to the new step’s heading when the step changes.

## StickyActionBar

`import { StickyActionBar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/sticky-action-bar';`

Status: beta · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-stickyactionbar--docs

**When to use**

- Save / Discard at the end of a long form, kept in view while scrolling.
- Bulk actions for a selection (`variant="floating"`) — appears when something is selected.
- The primary button of a mobile screen.

**When not to use**

- Short forms where the buttons are already in view
- Navigation → use Tabs or a bottom nav
- A message without actions → use Alert or Toaster

**Anatomy**

- Bar: `bar` (full-width strip) or `floating` (centered card); `sticky` or `fixed`.
- Message (optional): “3 selected”, “Unsaved changes” — announced when it changes.
- Actions: primary last; md buttons.
- Close (optional): `onClose` — “Clear selection”.

**StickyActionBar props**

- `aria-label?`: `string` — Landmark name. Default "Actions".
- `closeLabel?`: `string`, default `Close (localized: common.close)`
- `message?`: `ReactNode` — Status on the start side; announced politely when it changes.
- `onClose?`: `(() => void)`
- `open?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `position?`: `"fixed" | "sticky"`, default `sticky` — `sticky` (default) pins to the bottom of the nearest scroll container; `fixed` to the viewport.
- `variant?`: `"bar" | "floating"`, default `bar`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Says what the actions apply to.

  ```tsx
  <BarMock message="3 selected">
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Export</Button>
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="danger" size="md">Delete</Button>
  </BarMock>
  ```

- Don’t: Without the count, “Delete” could mean anything.

  ```tsx
  <BarMock message="">
    <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" size="md">Export</Button>
    <Button appearance="filled" tone="danger" size="md">Delete</Button>
  </BarMock>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a labelled landmark (“Actions” by default); the message is a polite live region.
- Closed means not rendered — no hidden tab stops.
- Keep the end of the page reachable: the bar covers the content under it.

## SuccessCheck

`import { SuccessCheck } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/success-check';`

Status: beta · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-successcheck--docs

**When to use**

- The moment something succeeds: a success Alert or Toast, a finished step, a "Saved" confirmation.
- Next to text that says what succeeded.

**When not to use**

- A success state that is already on screen when the page opens (a list of passed checks) → use a static CheckCircle icon
- Many items at once (every row of a table) → use a static icon — one drawing at a time

**Anatomy**

- Ring: drawn first, clockwise from 12 o’clock.
- Tick: drawn after the ring.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Shown when the success happens, with text that names it.

  ```tsx
  <p className={ROW}>
    <SuccessCheck />
    Backup restored
  </p>
  ```

- Don’t: Several drawings at once, or next to a static check — the motion stops meaning “just now”.

  ```tsx
  <p className={ROW}>
    <CheckCircle />
    <SuccessCheck />
    <SuccessCheck />
  </p>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decorative (aria-hidden): announce the success in text, e.g. a Toast or an Alert with live="polite".
- Plays once, under a second; with reduced motion the icon is simply shown.

## SurfaceEffect

`import { SurfaceEffect } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/surface-effect';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-surfaceeffect--docs

**When to use**

- Feature and pricing cards on a landing page: a glow under the pointer (`spotlight`), a light running round the border of the plan you recommend (`beam`), a gentle `tilt`, `shine` or `lift` on hover.
- `Aurora`: a slow color field behind a hero.

**When not to use**

- Cards in product UI (lists, dashboards, settings) → use Card with its own hover
- A way to say “this one is selected” or “this is clickable” → use Card selectable / action — the effect is decoration only
- Several different effects on one page

**Anatomy**

- Surface: wraps the card; give it the card’s radius (`rounded-*`) so the effect is clipped to it.
- Effect layer: a pseudo-element or CSS variables; no extra DOM in the card’s own content.
- Aurora (optional): separate, as the first child of a `relative isolate` section.

**SurfaceEffect props**

- `effect`: `"tilt" | "spotlight" | "lift" | "beam" | "shine"`

**Aurora props**

- `intensity?`: `"subtle" | "vivid"`, default `subtle`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One accent on the one card that matters.

  ```tsx
  <SurfaceEffect effect="beam" className="w-56 rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-2xl)]"><div className="p-4 text-body-m">Pro — recommended</div></SurfaceEffect>
  ```

- Don’t: A different effect on every card: nothing stands out any more.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex gap-2"><SurfaceEffect effect="tilt" className={CARD}>Tilt</SurfaceEffect><SurfaceEffect effect="shine" className={CARD}>Shine</SurfaceEffect><SurfaceEffect effect="lift" className={CARD}>Lift</SurfaceEffect></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decoration only: no role, no focus stop, nothing announced; Aurora is aria-hidden.
- Pointer effects (spotlight, tilt) do nothing on touch screens, so nothing depends on them.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no movement; the beam becomes a plain border.
- Keep text over Aurora at full contrast: a solid surface under the copy, or the subtle intensity.

## SwatchPicker

`import { SwatchPicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/swatch-picker';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-swatchpicker--docs

**When to use**

- Choosing by look: product color or material, a label color, a color facet in a filter.
- `type="multiple"` for filters (“Blue or Green”).

**When not to use**

- Any color, including custom ones → use ColorPicker / ColorField
- Options that aren’t visual → use RadioGroup or Select

**Anatomy**

- Legend (optional): shows the selected name — “Color: Midnight”.
- Swatch: color, two-tone `colors` or an `image`; circle or square; sm/md/lg.
- Unavailable (optional): struck through but still selectable — the variant exists, it’s out of stock.

**SwatchPicker props**

- `options`: `SwatchOption[]`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string | string[]`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `hideValueLabel?`: `boolean` — Hides the selected name after the legend.
- `legend?`: `ReactNode` — Group label, e.g. "Color". Shown as "Color: <selected name>".
- `max?`: `number` — Display only the first N swatches, then a "+K" counter (product cards).
- `name?`: `string`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void) | ((value: string[]) => void)`
- `required?`: `boolean`
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square" | null`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`
- `tooltips?`: `boolean` — Shows the swatch name in a tooltip on hover/focus.
- `type?`: `"single" | "multiple"`
- `unavailableLabel?`: `string`, default `out of stock (localized: swatchPicker.unavailable)` — Text appended to the accessible name of unavailable swatches.
- `value?`: `string | string[]`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The legend names the selected shade; out-of-stock is struck through, not hidden.

  ```tsx
  <SwatchPicker options={COLORS} legend="Color" defaultValue="midnight" />
  ```

- Don’t: No name: is that navy, midnight or black?

  ```tsx
  <SwatchPicker options={COLORS} defaultValue="midnight" aria-label="Color" hideValueLabel />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Single: a radio group, arrows move. Multiple: toggle buttons, each its own tab stop.
- Every option has a `label` — it’s the swatch’s name and tooltip.
- “Unavailable” is announced, not only drawn (`unavailableLabel`).
- Without a `legend` pass `aria-label`.

## SwipeDeck

`import { SwipeDeck } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/swipe-deck';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-swipedeck--docs

**When to use**

- A quick keep-or-skip pass over a short set: templates to try, suggested domains, onboarding interests.

**When not to use**

- Choosing several items the user needs to compare side by side → use CheckboxGroup / OptionCard
- Browsing content without a decision → use Carousel
- Destructive decisions (delete, cancel) → use ConfirmDialog

**Anatomy**

- Stack: the top card plus `depth` cards behind it, each lower and 5% smaller.
- Top card: follows the pointer and tilts; past a third of its width (or a quick flick) it flies out.
- Skip / Keep: buttons that do the same as a swipe left / right; labels from the locale or `skipLabel` / `keepLabel`.
- Empty (optional): what shows when every card is gone (`empty`).

**SwipeDeck props**

- `getKey`: `(item: T) => string`
- `items`: `T[]`
- `renderCard`: `(item: T) => ReactNode`
- `depth?`: `number`, default `2` — Cards visible in the stack behind the top one (default 2).
- `empty?`: `ReactNode` — Shown when every card has been swiped.
- `hideButtons?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Hide the Skip / Keep buttons (keep the arrow keys). Only when the page offers another non-drag way to decide.
- `keepLabel?`: `string`
- `onSwipe?`: `((item: T, direction: SwipeDirection) => void)` — Called when a card leaves: `left` = skip, `right` = keep.
- `skipLabel?`: `string` — Button labels; default from the locale (Skip / Keep).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Swipe plus buttons and arrow keys: anyone can decide.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>Skip · Keep buttons under the deck</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: A drag as the only way out fails WCAG 2.5.7 and keyboard users.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>Swipe only, no buttons</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The deck is one tab stop: ← skips, → keeps (mirrored in RTL).
- Only the top card is in the accessibility tree; the cards behind are aria-hidden and inert.
- After each decision a status message says what happened and how many cards are left.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no fly-out or spring; the next card simply appears.

## Switch

`import { Switch } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/switch';`

Status: stable · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-switch--docs

**When to use**

- A setting that takes effect the moment it’s flipped — no Save button.
- Turning a feature, service or notification on and off.

**When not to use**

- A choice that applies when a form is submitted → use Checkbox
- Two named options that aren’t on/off (Monthly / Yearly) → use RadioGroup or ToggleGroup
- A button that starts an action → use Button

**Anatomy**

- Track and thumb: on/off; `tone` warning or danger for risky settings.
- Label: names the setting, not the action (“Auto-renew”, not “Turn on auto-renew”).
- Description (optional): what changes when it’s on.
- Check icon (optional): `checkIcon` marks “on” with a shape, not only color.

**Switch props**

- `checkIcon?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Shows a checkmark inside the thumb when on. Default true — set false to hide it.
- `description?`: `ReactNode`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `tone?`: `"warning" | "danger" | "primary" | null`, default `primary`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, SwitchProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Applies at once and says what “on” does.

  ```tsx
  <Switch defaultChecked label="Auto-renew" description="Renews 14 days before expiry." />
  ```

- Don’t: A switch inside a form that still needs Save — use a checkbox for both.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
    <Switch label="Auto-renew" />
    <Checkbox label="Accept the terms" />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a `role="switch"`: announced as “on/off”, toggled with Space.
- Without a visible label pass `aria-label` — in a table row, name the row (“Auto-renew for seashell.shop”).
- If flipping it fails, set it back and say why next to it — don’t leave a switch showing a state the server didn’t accept.

## Table

`import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/table';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-table--docs

**When to use**

- Static tabular data with a few rows and no sorting, paging or selection: a price breakdown, DNS records, a spec sheet.
- Building something custom where DataTable doesn’t fit.

**When not to use**

- Sorting, paging, selection, row menus → use DataTable
- Label / value pairs about one object → use DescriptionList
- Laying out a form or a page → use CSS grid / flex
- Rows with one main item and an action → use ListItem

**Anatomy**

- Container: scrolls horizontally on a wide screen; with `containerLabel` it becomes a named region.
- Phone layout: below 640px rows stack into items (`mobileLayout="stack"`, default; labels from the headers, `label` / `stackAction` on a cell). A comparison pages its columns (`paged`); `scroll` keeps the table, `stickyFirstColumn` freezes the first column.
- Caption (optional): what the table shows; can be sr-only.
- Header: column names on a subtle surface.
- Rows and cells: numbers right-aligned with `text-right tabular-nums` on head and cell.

**Table props**

- `columnsPerPage?`: `number`, default `2` — `mobileLayout="paged"`: how many columns besides the first show at a time.
- `containerLabel?`: `string` — Optional accessible name for the scroll container. When set, the
- `mobileLayout?`: `"stack" | "paged" | "scroll"`, default `stack` — How the table fits a phone (below 640px): `stack` rows into label/value items (default), show the columns in `paged` groups, or `scroll` sideways.
- `stickyFirstColumn?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Keep the first column in place while the table scrolls sideways.

**TableCell props**

- `label?`: `string | false` — Label beside the value when the Table stacks on a phone. Defaults to the column header's text; `false` makes the cell run full width (another title line).
- `stackAction?`: `boolean` — In a stacked Table, pin this cell (a row menu, a remove button) to the item's top end.

Also accepts the props of: TableHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, HTMLAttributes, ThHTMLAttributes, TdHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Numbers right-aligned, the table has a caption.

  ```tsx
  <Table className="w-72">
    <TableCaption className="sr-only">Disk usage by site</TableCaption>
    <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Site</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">Disk</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
    <TableBody>{ROWS.map(([s, d]) => <TableRow key={s}><TableCell>{s}</TableCell><TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">{d}</TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```

- Don’t: Left-aligned numbers are hard to compare by magnitude.

  ```tsx
  <Table className="w-72">
    <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Site</TableHead><TableHead>Disk</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
    <TableBody>{ROWS.map(([s, d]) => <TableRow key={s}><TableCell>{s}</TableCell><TableCell>{d}</TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Real table markup: header cells are announced with every cell.
- Name the table — a `TableCaption` (visible or sr-only) or `containerLabel`.
- A scrolling table must be reachable by keyboard; the named container is a region screen-reader users can jump to.
- Don’t make a row clickable by itself — use DataTable’s row link, which is a real link.

## TableSkeleton

`import { TableSkeletonRows } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/table-skeleton';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-tableskeleton--docs

**When to use**

- First load of a hand-built Table: real headers, skeleton rows.
- Avoiding a flash on fast loads with `useFirstLoad`.

**When not to use**

- DataTable → use its own loading state
- Cards or lists → use Skeleton
- Refreshing rows already on screen → use keep them and show a busy state

**Anatomy**

- Header: the real column headers stay visible.
- Rows: `rows` placeholder rows; `columns` sets alignment, width and control-sized cells.

**TableSkeletonRows props**

- `columns`: `number | SkeletonCol[]`
- `rows?`: `number`, default `6`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Headers are real, rows match the columns.

  ```tsx
  <Table className="w-80">
    <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Domain</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">Replicas</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
    <TableBody aria-busy="true"><TableSkeletonRows rows={3} columns={[{}, { align: 'right', width: '2rem' }]} /></TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```

- Don’t: One block instead of a table: no idea what is loading.

  ```tsx
  <Skeleton className="h-32 w-80 rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-lg)]" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Rows are hidden from screen readers; set aria-busy="true" on the tbody while loading.
- `useFirstLoad` resolves at once under reduced motion.

## Tabs

`import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/tabs';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-tabs--docs

**When to use**

- Switching between views of the same object: Overview, Settings, Logs.
- Two to about six sections people move between freely, in any order.

**When not to use**

- Steps people go through in order → use Stepper
- A tab state that should survive reload or be shared → use UrlTabs
- Filtering one list (All / Unread) → use ToggleGroup
- Navigating between pages → use links, Sidebar or NavigationMenu

**Anatomy**

- List: underline (default) or `variant="chips"` — segmented, for a compact switch of views in a card or toolbar; scrolls when it doesn’t fit. The marker glides to the active tab.
- Trigger: label, optional `icon`, badge; `onClose` for closable tabs.
- Panel: `TabsContent` for each value.

**TabsList props**

- `variant?`: `"underline" | "chips"`, default `underline` — `underline` (default): tabs over a hairline, the active one underlined.

**TabsTrigger props**

- `closeLabel?`: `string` — Tooltip for the pointer "×" (e.g. "Close Draft 1"). Screen readers get the Delete shortcut instead.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon shown before the label.
- `onClose?`: `((event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement> | MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void)` — Makes the tab closable, following the WAI-ARIA APG "deletable tabs"

Also accepts the props of: TabsTriggerProps, TabsProps, HTMLAttributes, TabsListProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, TabsContentProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Parallel views of one site, visited in any order.

  ```tsx
  <Tabs defaultValue="overview">
    <TabsList aria-label="Site sections">
      <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="domains">Domains</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="backups">Backups</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="logs">Logs</TabsTrigger>
    </TabsList>
    {['overview', 'domains', 'backups', 'logs'].map((v) => (
      <TabsContent key={v} value={v} className={panel}>The site’s {v}.</TabsContent>
    ))}
  </Tabs>
  ```

- Don’t: Numbered steps as tabs: people can skip to Payment with nothing filled in — use Stepper.

  ```tsx
  <Tabs defaultValue="1">
    <TabsList aria-label="Checkout">
      <TabsTrigger value="1">1. Account</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="2">2. Plan</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="3">3. Payment</TabsTrigger>
    </TabsList>
    {['1', '2', '3'].map((v) => (
      <TabsContent key={v} value={v} className={panel}>Step {v} form.</TabsContent>
    ))}
  </Tabs>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name the list (`aria-label`) when no heading does. Tab enters the list once; arrows switch tabs.
- Each panel is labelled by its tab; keep focusable content inside panels reachable with Tab.
- Closable tabs: Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab; the × is for the pointer, with `closeLabel` as its tooltip.

## TagInput

`import { TagInput } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/tag-input';`

Status: beta · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-taginput--docs

**When to use**

- Several free-form values of one kind: email recipients, domains, IP ranges, tags.

**When not to use**

- Picking several from a known list → use Combobox multiple or CheckboxGroup
- One value → use TextField

**Anatomy**

- Field: chips and the input in one border.
- Chip: one value, removable; invalid ones turn danger and stay (`validate`).
- Description / errors: what to type, then which values are wrong.

**TagInput props**

- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string[]`, default `[]` — Uncontrolled starting list.
- `delimiters?`: `string[]`, default `['Enter', ',', ';']` — Keys that commit the typed text. Default Enter, comma, semicolon. Add ' ' for space-separated tags.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Helper text under the field (replaced by the error while there is one).
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `error?`: `string` — External error (e.g. "Add at least one recipient"). Shown under the field, above per-value errors.
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm"`, default `md`
- `id?`: `string`
- `max?`: `number` — Maximum number of values; the input hides once it's reached.
- `name?`: `string`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string[]) => void)`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Type and press Enter (localized: tagInput.placeholder)`
- `readOnly?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `transform?`: `((tag: string) => string)` — Normalize each value before it's added, e.g. `(v) => v.toLowerCase()` for emails and domains. Trimmed first.
- `validate?`: `((tag: string) => string)` — Return a message for a bad value (it's still added, as a danger chip), undefined when it's fine.
- `value?`: `string[]` — Controlled list of values.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Each value is a chip — easy to check and remove.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><TagInput aria-label="Recipients" defaultValue={['dana@seashell.shop', 'ops@seashell.shop']} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A comma list in one field hides which value is wrong.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Recipients" defaultValue="dana@seashell.shop, ops@seashell.shop" description="Separate with commas" widthSize="lg" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Additions and removals are announced.
- Backspace in the empty input removes the last chip; each chip’s remove button is named.
- Invalid values stay visible with their reason — never dropped silently.

## Terminal

`import { Terminal, TerminalHeader, TerminalBody, TerminalLine } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/terminal';`

Status: beta · Category: Code
Docs: ./?path=/docs/code-terminal--docs

**When to use**

- Live or past console output: a web SSH session, a deploy or build log, a tail of access logs.
- Output where the order and severity of lines matter.

**When not to use**

- A command for the user to copy → use CodeBlock
- A list of events people browse or filter → use Timeline or DataTable
- Editable code → use CodeEditor

**Anatomy**

- Header (optional): connection dot + label, `user@host`, status text and a `tools` slot.
- Body: scrollback log; follows new lines only while the reader is at the bottom.
- Line: one line of output; `level` sets the color (cmd, success, warning, error, muted).

**Terminal props**

- `ariaLabel?`: `string`, default `Terminal output (localized: terminal.output)`
- `bodyClassName?`: `string`
- `connection?`: `"connected" | "connecting" | "down"`, default `connected`
- `hideHeader?`: `boolean`
- `host?`: `string`
- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `true` — Forces the whole terminal (header + body) onto the fixed dark
- `lines?`: `TerminalLineData[]` — Data-driven lines. Omit to compose the body yourself via children.
- `live?`: `"off" | "polite"`, default `polite` — Live-region politeness. Set "off" for chatty/high-frequency streams.
- `status?`: `string` — Free-text status shown next to user@host.
- `tools?`: `ReactNode` — Right-aligned header content.
- `user?`: `string`

**TerminalHeader props**

- `connection?`: `"connected" | "connecting" | "down"`, default `connected`
- `host?`: `string`
- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `status?`: `string`
- `user?`: `string`

**TerminalBody props**

- `ariaLabel?`: `string`, default `Terminal output (localized: terminal.output)`
- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `lines?`: `TerminalLineData[]`
- `live?`: `"off" | "polite"`, default `polite`

**TerminalLine props**

- `inverse?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Match the parent Terminal's `inverse` when composing lines
- `level?`: `"info" | "success" | "warning" | "muted" | "error" | "cmd" | "ok" | "warn" | "err" | "dim"`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Levels color the lines, and the text itself says “warning” / “error”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <Terminal hideHeader lines={[
      { id: '1', text: '$ npm run build', level: 'cmd' },
      { id: '2', text: 'warning: 2 unused exports', level: 'warning' },
      { id: '3', text: 'error: build failed (exit 1)', level: 'error' },
    ]} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: A static code block for a log: no severity, no following new output.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><CodeBlock language="bash" code={'$ npm run build\nwarning: 2 unused exports\nerror: build failed (exit 1)'} /></div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The body is `role="log"` and a tab stop; new lines are announced politely. For chatty streams set `live="off"` and announce only the result.
- Connection state is a dot plus a text label, never color alone.
- Give each terminal on a page its own `ariaLabel` (“Deploy log”, “SSH: web-04”).
- Line colors come from tokens that pass contrast on the dark surface — don’t override them with raw ANSI colors.

## TextEffect

`import { TextEffect } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/text-effect';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-texteffect--docs

**When to use**

- A hero headline or one key word on a landing page: letters rising in (`split`), a code-like reveal (`scramble`), a soft highlight (`shimmer`), rotating phrases (`typewriter`).

**When not to use**

- Body copy, labels, buttons, anything in product UI → use plain text
- More than one animated headline in view at a time
- Text people must read quickly (prices, warnings) → use plain text

**Anatomy**

- Text: the string itself (`children`), or `phrases` for the typewriter.
- Trigger: split and scramble start in view (default), on hover or on mount (`trigger`).
- Caret (optional): typewriter only, in the primary icon color.

**TextEffect props**

- `effect`: `"split" | "scramble" | "shimmer" | "typewriter"`
- `as?`: `ElementType`, default `span` — The element to render: a heading level, `p`, `span` (default).
- `children?`: `string`, default `` — The text (split, scramble, shimmer).
- `phrases?`: `string[]` — Typewriter: the phrases it types in turn.
- `trigger?`: `"view" | "hover" | "mount"`, default `view` — When split / scramble start: in view (default), on hover, or on mount.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One short headline, animated once.

  ```tsx
  <TextEffect effect="split" as="p" className="text-heading-s">Ship faster</TextEffect>
  ```

- Don’t: An effect on running text: harder to read, and it doesn’t stop.

  ```tsx
  <TextEffect effect="shimmer" as="p" className="text-body-s">Your password must be at least 12 characters long.</TextEffect>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Screen readers get the plain text (every phrase, for the typewriter); the animated letters are aria-hidden.
- prefers-reduced-motion: the text simply shows; the typewriter shows its first phrase.
- Shimmer falls back to plain text in Windows high contrast.

## TextField

`import { TextField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/text-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-textfield--docs

**When to use**

- Short free text on one line: a name, an email, a domain, a URL, a code.
- With a visible label above it, every time.

**When not to use**

- More than a line of text → use TextArea
- Picking from known values → use Select or Combobox
- A number people step up and down → use NumberField
- A password → use Password
- A phone number → use PhoneField
- Free text with suggestions → use Autocomplete

**Anatomy**

- Label: always visible; required fields get *, optional ones “(optional)” via `optional`.
- Input: with optional `leftIcon` / `rightIcon`; a clear button appears when filled.
- Description (optional): help shown before typing: format, limits.
- Message (optional): `error` or `success` text; replaces the description while shown.

**TextField props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Helper text below the field. Hidden when `error` or `success` is set.
- `error?`: `ReactNode` — Error message shown below the field with a warning icon, and
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`, default `md`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `labelPosition?`: `"top" | "left"`, default `top` — 'top' (default) stacks label above the field. 'left' puts a fixed 216px label column beside it, matching Figma's horizontal Formfield layout.
- `leftIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon shown at the start of the field (16px, decorative).
- `optional?`: `boolean` — Shows "(optional)" after the label. Ignored when `required`.
- `required?`: `boolean` — Shows a small red asterisk after the label.
- `rightIcon?`: `ReactNode` — Icon shown at the end of the field. Overrides the built-in clear button, error, and success icons when set.
- `success?`: `ReactNode` — Success message shown below the field with a check icon, and
- `widthSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "full"`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Label above; the placeholder only shows an example.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Domain" placeholder="example.com" widthSize="md" />
  ```

- Don’t: Placeholder as the label disappears as soon as people type.

  ```tsx
  <TextField aria-label="Domain" placeholder="Domain" widthSize="md" />
  ```

- Do: The error says what’s wrong and how to fix it.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Email" defaultValue="dana@seashell" error="Add the domain ending, like .com." widthSize="md" />
  ```

- Don’t: “Invalid input” makes people guess.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Email" defaultValue="dana@seashell" error="Invalid input." widthSize="md" />
  ```

- Do: Width hints at the expected length (`widthSize`).

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Verification code" widthSize="sm" />
  ```

- Don’t: A 6-digit code in a full-width field reads like “type a paragraph here”.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Verification code" widthSize="full" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Pass `label` (or a `Label` with `htmlFor`); `aria-label` only where a visible label truly can’t exist.
- Description and error are linked with `aria-describedby`; an error also sets `aria-invalid`.
- Set `type`, `inputMode` and `autoComplete` — the right keyboard on phones and autofill everywhere.
- Validate on leaving the field, re-check live once an error shows; never while someone types into an empty field.

## TextArea

`import { TextArea } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/textarea';`

Status: stable · Category: Text Input
Docs: ./?path=/docs/text-input-textarea--docs

**When to use**

- Text that can run to several lines: a description, a message, notes, a list one per line.

**When not to use**

- One short line → use TextField
- Code or config → use CodeEditor
- A chat-style prompt with send → use PromptArea

**Anatomy**

- Label: with required * / `optional`.
- Field: resizable vertically; height shows the expected length.
- Description / error: limits and format; error replaces the description.

**TextArea props**

- `description?`: `ReactNode` — Helper text below the field. Hidden when `error` is set.
- `error?`: `ReactNode` — Error message shown below the field with a warning icon, and
- `heightSize?`: `"md" | "sm" | null`, default `md`
- `label?`: `ReactNode`
- `labelPosition?`: `"top" | "left"`, default `top` — 'top' (default) stacks label above the field. 'left' puts a fixed 216px label column beside it, matching TextField's horizontal Formfield layout.
- `optional?`: `boolean` — Shows "(optional)" after the label. Ignored when `required`.
- `required?`: `boolean` — Shows a small red asterisk after the label.
- `widthSize?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "full" | null`, default `full`

Also accepts the props of: InputHTMLAttributes, TextareaHTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Room that matches the expected text, and the limit up front.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72"><TextArea label="Message" description="Up to 500 characters." /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: A one-line field for a paragraph scrolls the text out of sight.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Message" widthSize="lg" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Label, description and error are linked like TextField’s.
- If there’s a limit, show the count as text, not only by stopping input.

## ThemeToggle

`import { ThemeToggle } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/theme-toggle';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-themetoggle--docs

**When to use**

- A quick light/dark switch in the top bar.

**When not to use**

- When “same as system” must be a choice too → use a radio group in the account menu or settings

**Anatomy**

- Icon button: sun / moon; flips `data-theme` on the document.

Also accepts the props of: ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One place, in the top bar, next to the other global controls.

  ```tsx
  <ThemeToggle />
  ```

- Don’t: Repeating a global setting on every page makes it look page-specific.

  ```tsx
  <span className="font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text-subtle)]">A theme switch in every page header</span>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Its name says the action — “Switch to dark theme” / “Switch to light theme” — so it also tells which theme is on now.
- Keyboard: a regular button, Enter or Space.

## TickerList

`import { TickerList } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/ticker-list';`

Status: beta · Category: Motion
Docs: ./?path=/docs/motion-tickerlist--docs

**When to use**

- A few rows of recent activity inside a showcase card: transactions, signups, deploys.

**When not to use**

- A real activity feed people scroll and act on → use List / DataTable
- Notifications → use Toast

**Anatomy**

- Window: `visible` rows at a time.
- Turn: every `interval` ms the top row leaves and the next one slides in at the bottom.
- Pause: a small Pause / Play button under the list.

**TickerList props**

- `hidePause?`: `boolean`, default `false` — Hide the Pause button — only when the page has another way to stop it.
- `interval?`: `number`, default `2500` — Time between moves, ms (default 2500).
- `visible?`: `number`, default `3` — Rows on screen at once (default 3).

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Short rows, enough of them to make the motion meaningful.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>3 visible of 6–10 short rows</Tile>
  ```

- Don’t: A row that moves away while someone aims at it.

  ```tsx
  <Tile>Rows with buttons</Tile>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A plain list of the rows on screen; nothing is announced as it moves.
- Pauses on hover and focus and has a Pause button (WCAG 2.2.2).
- prefers-reduced-motion: it doesn’t move.

## TimeField

`import { TimeField } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/time-field';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-timefield--docs

**When to use**

- A time of day: a daily backup time, a meeting start, a reminder.
- Times on a grid (`step`) with limits (`min`/`max`) — any typed time is still accepted.

**When not to use**

- Start and end → use TimeRangePicker
- A date and a time → use DateTimePicker
- A duration (“90 minutes”) → use NumberField with a unit

**Anatomy**

- Input: type to filter or enter any time (“9:47”).
- List: times from `min` to `max` every `step` minutes, shown per `hourCycle`.
- Value: 24-hour “HH:MM” string, whatever the display.

**TimeField props**

- `aria-describedby?`: `string`
- `aria-invalid?`: `boolean | "true" | "false"`
- `aria-label?`: `string`
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string`
- `className?`: `string`
- `contentClassName?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `string` — Uncontrolled initial value as a 24-hour "HH:MM" string.
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `hourCycle?`: `"12" | "24"`, default `12` — 12-hour (AM/PM) or 24-hour labels. Defaults to 12.
- `id?`: `string`
- `max?`: `string`, default `23:59` — Latest time offered, "HH:MM". Defaults to "23:59".
- `min?`: `string`, default `00:00` — Earliest time offered, "HH:MM". Defaults to "00:00".
- `onChange?`: `((value: string) => void)` — Called with the selected "HH:MM" value (or "" when cleared).
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Select time (localized: timeField.placeholder)`
- `step?`: `number`, default `30` — Minutes between options. Defaults to 30.
- `value?`: `string` — Controlled value as a 24-hour "HH:MM" string.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A list on a 30-minute grid, with typing for anything in between.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-48 flex-col gap-2">
    <Label htmlFor="gl-tf-backup">Daily backup at</Label>
    <TimeField id="gl-tf-backup" step={30} placeholder="Choose a time" />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Free text: “9.30”, “930” and “9:30pm” all need guessing.

  ```tsx
  <TextField label="Daily backup at" placeholder="e.g. 9:30" widthSize="md" />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s a combobox: arrows move through times, Enter picks, typing filters.
- Label it (`Label` + `id` or `aria-label`); put the time zone in the label or description if it matters.

## TimeRangePicker

`import { TimeRangePicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/time-range-picker';`

Status: stable · Category: Date & Time
Docs: ./?path=/docs/date-time-timerangepicker--docs

**When to use**

- A start and end time within one day: opening hours, a maintenance window, quiet hours.

**When not to use**

- Spans across days → use DateRangePicker or two DateTimePickers
- A single time → use TimeField

**Anatomy**

- Start and End: two TimeFields with “to” between; `startLabel`/`endLabel` name them.
- Linked limits: the end list starts after the chosen start.

**TimeRangePicker props**

- `aria-label?`: `string` — Names the pair as a group (role="group"), e.g. "Maintenance window".
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` — Id of a visible label that names the pair as a group.
- `className?`: `string`
- `defaultValue?`: `TimeRange`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`
- `endLabel?`: `string`, default `End time (localized: timeRangePicker.end)`
- `hourCycle?`: `"12" | "24"`, default `12`
- `max?`: `string`, default `23:59`
- `min?`: `string`, default `00:00`
- `onChange?`: `((value: TimeRange) => void)`
- `startLabel?`: `string`, default `Start time (localized: timeRangePicker.start)`
- `step?`: `number`, default `30`
- `value?`: `TimeRange`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: One control: the end can’t be set before the start.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
    <span id="gl-trp-quiet" className="font-body text-body-m font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
      Quiet hours
    </span>
    <TimeRangePicker aria-labelledby="gl-trp-quiet" step={30} defaultValue={{ start: '22:00', end: '23:30' }} />
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Two unlinked fields: “to 09:00” — the next morning, or a mistake?

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-end gap-2">
    <div className="flex w-36 flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="gl-trp-from">From</Label>
      <TimeField id="gl-trp-from" step={30} defaultValue="22:00" />
    </div>
    <div className="flex w-36 flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="gl-trp-to">To</Label>
      <TimeField id="gl-trp-to" step={30} defaultValue="09:00" />
    </div>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name the pair (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`); each field is named Start/End within it.
- If an overnight range is allowed, say so in the description.

## Timeline

`import { Timeline, TimelineItem, TimelineTitle, TimelineDescription, TimelineTime } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/timeline';`

Status: stable · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-timeline--docs

**When to use**

- A sequence of events in time: activity on a site, an incident’s history, an order’s progress.

**When not to use**

- A searchable, filterable log → use DataTable (audit log)
- Steps people go through → use Stepper
- Raw console output → use Terminal

**Anatomy**

- Rail: a dot, or a chip with `icon`, colored by `tone`; a line to the next event.
- Time: `time` — absolute, or relative with the exact time on hover.
- Title: what happened.
- Description (optional): the object or detail.

**TimelineItem props**

- `icon?`: `ReactNode`
- `time?`: `ReactNode`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`, default `neutral`
- `toneLabel?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: OlHTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Newest first, each event with a time; color only where it matters.

  ```tsx
  <Timeline className="w-80">
    <TimelineItem tone="success" time="14:02" icon={<CheckCircle />}>
      <TimelineTitle>Certificate issued</TimelineTitle>
      <TimelineDescription>shop.seashell.dev · valid 90 days</TimelineDescription>
    </TimelineItem>
    <TimelineItem tone="warning" time="13:40" icon={<WarningTriangle />}>
      <TimelineTitle>DNS check retried</TimelineTitle>
    </TimelineItem>
    <TimelineItem time="13:38"><TimelineTitle>Renewal started</TimelineTitle></TimelineItem>
  </Timeline>
  ```

- Don’t: No times, every event green — order and meaning are lost.

  ```tsx
  <Timeline className="w-80">
    <TimelineItem tone="success" icon={<CheckCircle />}><TimelineTitle>Certificate issued</TimelineTitle></TimelineItem>
    <TimelineItem tone="success" icon={<CheckCircle />}><TimelineTitle>DNS check retried</TimelineTitle></TimelineItem>
    <TimelineItem tone="success" icon={<CheckCircle />}><TimelineTitle>Renewal started</TimelineTitle></TimelineItem>
  </Timeline>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- An ordered list; each non-neutral tone adds an sr-only word (“success”, “error”), so status isn’t color alone.
- Override that word with `toneLabel` when the default doesn’t fit.
- Use a <time> element or full date in the description where the time is ambiguous.

## Toggle

`import { Toggle } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/toggle';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-toggle--docs

**When to use**

- A button that stays pressed: bold in an editor, “Show archived”, pin.
- In toolbars, where a switch would look out of place.

**When not to use**

- A setting with a label and an immediate effect → use Switch
- One of several options → use ToggleGroup type="single"
- An action that runs once → use Button

**Anatomy**

- Button: `appearance` ghost / tonal / outlined, `size`; pressed state from `pressed`.
- Icon or label: icon-only needs aria-label.

**Toggle props**

- `appearance?`: `"tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Square, icon-only control (no side padding). Detected automatically when the only child is an icon; pass it to override. Needs an `aria-label`.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`

Also accepts the props of: ToggleProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A toolbar control that stays on.

  ```tsx
  <Toggle aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed><Bold /></Toggle>
  ```

- Don’t: A setting dressed as a button — it reads like an action, not a state.

  ```tsx
  <Toggle>Email alerts</Toggle>
  ```

- Do: Settings use Switch with a label.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Switch id="gl-tg-sw" />
    <Label htmlFor="gl-tg-sw">Email alerts</Label>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: “On” on a button: on what? and does pressing it turn it off?

  ```tsx
  <Toggle appearance="outlined">On</Toggle>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Announced with `aria-pressed`; the name stays the same in both states.
- Icon-only toggles need aria-label.

## ToggleGroup

`import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/toggle-group';`

Status: stable · Category: Actions
Docs: ./?path=/docs/actions-togglegroup--docs

**When to use**

- Switching a view or a filter among 2–5 options, all visible: Grid / List, All / Unread, Monthly / Yearly.
- `type="multiple"` for independent format toggles (bold, italic).

**When not to use**

- Switching between panels of content → use Tabs
- A choice in a form that’s saved later → use RadioGroup
- More than 5 options → use Select

**Anatomy**

- Group: `type` single/multiple, `appearance` (`outlined` for a visible segmented control, `ghost` for toolbars).
- Items: sized to their content, not stretched to equal widths.

**ToggleGroup props**

- `appearance?`: `"tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `ghost`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`

**ToggleGroupItem props**

- `appearance?`: `"tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean` — Square, icon-only item. Detected automatically when the only child is an icon; pass it to override.
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | null`

Also accepts the props of: ToggleGroupSingleProps, ToggleGroupMultipleProps, ToggleGroupImplSingleProps, ToggleGroupImplMultipleProps, ToggleGroupImplProps, HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Same thing shown differently — a view switch.

  ```tsx
  <ToggleGroup type="single" appearance="outlined" defaultValue="grid" aria-label="Layout">
    <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" aria-label="Grid"><ViewGrid /></ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem value="list" aria-label="List"><List /></ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```

- Don’t: Different sections of content are Tabs, not a toggle.

  ```tsx
  <ToggleGroup type="single" appearance="outlined" defaultValue="general" aria-label="Settings">
    <ToggleGroupItem value="general">General</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem value="billing">Billing</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem value="security">Security</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Give the group an `aria-label`. Arrow keys move between items.
- Icon-only items need aria-label each.
- Single: one is always on — don’t let it be unselected unless “none” is a real option.

## ToneIcon

`import { ToneIcon } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/tone-icon';`

Status: stable · Category: Labels
Docs: ./?path=/docs/labels-toneicon--docs

**When to use**

- Leading a row or card whose meaning is a tone: a warning in a list, a success step, an info note.
- When the tone must still read in grayscale (fill + icon shape + color).

**When not to use**

- A live state on a small item → use StatusDot
- A labelled status → use Badge
- A full message → use Alert

**Anatomy**

- Container: tinted fill; `shape` circle/square, `size` sm/md/lg.
- Glyph: a distinct shape per tone (info i, success check, warning triangle, danger circle).

**ToneIcon props**

- `tone`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary"`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Overrides the tone's default icon.
- `shape?`: `"circle" | "square"`, default `circle`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm"`, default `md`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Shape and text carry the meaning; color adds to it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <div className={ROW}><ToneIcon tone="warning" />Certificate expires in 5 days</div>
    <div className={ROW}><ToneIcon tone="success" />Backup completed</div>
  </div>
  ```

- Don’t: Colored dots with nouns: what about the certificate? Color alone says it.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <div className={ROW}><StatusDot tone="warning" />Certificate</div>
    <div className={ROW}><StatusDot tone="success" />Backup</div>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Decorative by default (aria-hidden) — the text next to it must say the status.
- Standalone with no text: pass `aria-hidden={false}` and an `aria-label`.

## Toolbar

`import { Toolbar, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarSeparator, ToolbarLink, ToolbarButton } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/toolbar';`

Status: stable · Category: Layout
Docs: ./?path=/docs/layout-toolbar--docs

**When to use**

- A row of related commands sharing one tab stop: bulk actions on a selection, text formatting, editor tools.

**When not to use**

- Search and filter fields → use a search region with normal tab order
- Two or three unrelated buttons → use Buttons

**Anatomy**

- Toolbar: one tab stop, arrows move inside; named with `aria-label`.
- Items: `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup` (toggles), `ToolbarLink`.
- Separator: between groups; destructive actions last.

**ToolbarGroup props**

- `type?`: `"single" | "multiple"` — Selection mode, as on Radix ToggleGroup: one pressed item at a time, or any number. Default `multiple`.

**ToolbarButton props**

- `appearance?`: `"filled" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "ghost" | null`, default `ghost`
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean | null`
- `iconOnly?`: `boolean | null`
- `size?`: `"md" | "lg" | "sm" | "xl" | "2xl" | null`, default `lg`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "primary" | "secondary" | null`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ToolbarProps, ToggleGroupImplSingleProps, ToggleGroupImplMultipleProps, ToggleGroupImplProps, SeparatorProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Related actions on a selection; Tab in once, arrows across, Delete set apart.

  ```tsx
  <Toolbar aria-label="Bulk actions" className={CARD}>
    <ToolbarButton><Copy /> Duplicate</ToolbarButton>
    <ToolbarButton><Download /> Export</ToolbarButton>
    <ToolbarSeparator />
    <ToolbarButton appearance="ghost" tone="danger"><Trash /> Delete</ToolbarButton>
  </Toolbar>
  ```

- Don’t: Loose buttons styled as a toolbar: three tab stops, no grouping, Delete right next to Export.

  ```tsx
  <div className={`${CARD} flex gap-1`}>
    <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md"><Copy /> Duplicate</Button>
    <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md"><Download /> Export</Button>
    <Button appearance="ghost" tone="danger" size="md"><Trash /> Delete</Button>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Role toolbar with roving tabindex: Tab enters once, ←/→ move, Home/End jump.
- Name it (`aria-label`: “Bulk actions”).

## Tooltip

`import { Tooltip, TooltipProvider, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/tooltip';`

Status: stable · Category: Overlays
Docs: ./?path=/docs/overlays-tooltip--docs

**When to use**

- Naming an icon-only control (“Copy API key”) or adding a short hint to something focusable.
- A shortcut next to the name: “Search  /”.

**When not to use**

- Information people need to complete a task → use text on the page or a field description
- Links, buttons or anything interactive → use Popover
- Previews of linked content → use HoverCard

**Anatomy**

- Trigger: a focusable element — a Button, not a bare icon.
- Content: a few words; `tone` success/danger for feedback (“Copied”).

**TooltipContent props**

- `showArrow?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `tone?`: `"neutral" | "success" | "danger"`, default `neutral`

Also accepts the props of: TooltipProps, TooltipProviderProps, TooltipContentProps, TooltipContentImplProps, HTMLAttributes, PopperContentProps, ButtonHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Hover or focus: two words that name the icon.

  ```tsx
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger asChild>
      <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="md" iconOnly leftIcon={<Copy />} aria-label="Copy API key" />
    </TooltipTrigger>
    <TooltipContent>Copy API key</TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
  ```

- Don’t: Rules people need while typing, hidden in a tooltip — put them under the field.

  ```tsx
  <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 font-body text-body-m text-[var(--color-text-text)]">
    Password
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger asChild>
        <Button appearance="ghost" tone="secondary" size="sm" iconOnly leftIcon={<InfoCircle />} aria-label="Password rules" />
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>At least 12 characters, one number, one symbol, no spaces, different from your last 5 passwords.</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Shows on hover and keyboard focus, hides on Escape; it describes the trigger and doesn’t replace its name.
- Not reachable on touch — never the only place for important information.

## Topbar

`import { Topbar, TopbarSearch, TopbarAction, TopbarMenu } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/topbar';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-topbar--docs

**When to use**

- The app header above the content: breadcrumb or page context on the left, a few global actions on the right.
- `orientation="vertical"` for a slim icon rail.

**When not to use**

- Section navigation → use Sidebar
- A marketing site header → use NavigationMenu
- Page-level actions (Save, Create) → use PageHeader

**Anatomy**

- Menu button (optional): `TopbarMenu` opens the Sidebar on small screens.
- Context: Breadcrumb, or a page title.
- Search (optional): `TopbarSearch`.
- Spacer and actions: `TopbarSpacer`, then 2–4 `TopbarAction`s (icon buttons with names).

**Topbar props**

- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `horizontal`

**TopbarSearch props**

- `children?`: `ReactNode` — The results dropdown's content, anchored under the field. Omit (or pass nothing selectable) and the popover simply won't open.
- `defaultOpen?`: `boolean`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `open?`: `boolean`
- `placeholder?`: `string`, default `Search sites, servers, users… (localized: topbar.searchPlaceholder)`
- `value?`: `string`

**TopbarAction props**

- `badge?`: `boolean`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, SVGAttributes, ImgHTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Where you are on the left, two global actions on the right.

  ```tsx
  <Frame label="Topbar example">
    <Topbar className="!static">
      <Breadcrumb aria-label="Topbar breadcrumb">
        <BreadcrumbList>
          <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#gl-tb">Sites</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbSeparator />
          <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Backups</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
        </BreadcrumbList>
      </Breadcrumb>
      <TopbarSpacer />
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Notifications" badge><Bell /></TopbarAction>
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Account"><User /></TopbarAction>
    </Topbar>
  </Frame>
  ```

- Don’t: A row of unlabeled icons and no context: people guess which is which and where they are.

  ```tsx
  <Frame label="Overloaded topbar example">
    <Topbar className="!static">
      <TopbarSpacer />
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Help"><HelpCircle /></TopbarAction>
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Messages"><Mail /></TopbarAction>
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Notifications" badge><Bell /></TopbarAction>
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Settings"><Settings /></TopbarAction>
      <TopbarAction aria-label="Account"><User /></TopbarAction>
    </Topbar>
  </Frame>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- It’s the page `header` (banner); keep one per page.
- Every `TopbarAction` needs `aria-label`; the badge dot is announced only through the label (“Notifications, 3 new”).
- Keep the same order on every page so people find actions by position.

## Tree

`import { Tree } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/tree';`

Status: beta · Category: Data
Docs: ./?path=/docs/data-tree--docs

**When to use**

- Real hierarchy people expand and pick from: files and folders, DNS zones, nested categories.

**When not to use**

- A flat list → use ListItem or a menu
- Site navigation → use Sidebar
- Rows with several columns → use DataTable
- Showing / hiding sections of content → use Accordion

**Anatomy**

- Item: chevron for parents, optional icon, label.
- Group: children, indented one level.

**Tree props**

- `items`: `TreeNode[]`
- `defaultExpandedIds?`: `string[]`
- `defaultSelectedId?`: `string`
- `expandedIds?`: `string[]`
- `onExpandedChange?`: `((ids: string[]) => void)`
- `onSelect?`: `((id: string, node: TreeNode) => void)`
- `selectedId?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: Folders that really nest.

  ```tsx
  <Tree
    aria-label="Site files"
    className="w-64"
    defaultExpandedIds={['public']}
    items={[
      { id: 'public', label: 'public', children: [{ id: 'index', label: 'index.html' }, { id: 'robots', label: 'robots.txt' }] },
      { id: 'logs', label: 'logs', children: [{ id: 'access', label: 'access.log' }] },
    ]}
  />
  ```

- Don’t: One level is just a list — a tree adds keyboard rules for nothing.

  ```tsx
  <Tree aria-label="Plans" className="w-64" items={[{ id: 's', label: 'Starter' }, { id: 'p', label: 'Pro' }, { id: 'x', label: 'Scale' }]} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (it warns in dev otherwise).
- One tab stop; ↑/↓ move, → expands or steps in, ← collapses or steps out, Home/End, Enter/Space select, typing jumps.
- Expanded and selected state are announced, so is the position (“2 of 5”).

## UndoToast

`import { undoToast } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/undo-toast';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-undotoast--docs

**When to use**

- A destructive action that can be held back for a few seconds: delete a file, archive a site, remove a member.
- Replacing a confirm dialog for frequent, low-risk removals.

**When not to use**

- The action can’t be rolled back (data wiped, email sent, payment) → use ConfirmDialog
- Plain success feedback → use Toaster (toast.success)

**Anatomy**

- Title: what was done: “Site archived”.
- Description (optional): the object, if the title doesn’t name it.
- Undo: rolls back via `onUndo`; otherwise `onCommit` runs when the toast closes.

**undoToast(options)**

- `title`: `string`
- `description?`: `string`
- `duration?`: `number` — Grace period before the action commits (ms).
- `undoLabel?`: `string`
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` — Defaults to a trash glyph; pass null to omit.
- `onUndo?`: `() => void`
- `onCommit?`: `() => void`

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: The file is still recoverable — Undo is real.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" onClick={() => undoToast({ title: 'Moved to trash', description: 'invoice-0923.pdf' })}>Delete file</Button>
  ```

- Don’t: Undo on something already gone for good is a broken promise — confirm first.

  ```tsx
  <Button appearance="outlined" tone="secondary" onClick={() => undoToast({ title: 'Database deleted', description: 'shop_prod' })}>Delete database</Button>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The window is 10 s by default (`duration`) — long enough to reach Undo with a keyboard or screen reader. Don’t shorten it.
- Commit happens on close, so people who navigate away still get the action done.
- After Undo, the item returns to its place; restore focus there if it was focused.

## UrlTabs

`import { UrlTabs } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/url-tabs';`

Status: stable · Category: Navigation
Docs: ./?path=/docs/navigation-urltabs--docs

**When to use**

- Page-level tabs people link to, share, or return to after reload: a resource’s Settings or Billing tab.
- Pass `values` so a stale `?tab=` falls back to the default.

**When not to use**

- Tabs inside a dialog, popover or card → use Tabs
- Several tab groups on one page sharing a param → use separate param names, or Tabs

**Anatomy**

- Tabs: the same Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent.
- URL param: `param` (default “tab”), written with replaceState — no history entry per arrow key.
- Router adapter (optional): `navigate` for your router.

**UrlTabs props**

- `navigate?`: `UrlTabsNavigate`
- `param?`: `string`, default `tab`
- `values?`: `readonly string[]` — Valid tab values. An unknown `?tab=` then falls back to defaultValue.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes, TabsProps.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A settings page: “Billing” can be bookmarked, shared, and survives reload.

  ```tsx
  <UrlTabs param="gl-section" defaultValue="general" values={['general', 'billing', 'members']}>
    <TabsList aria-label="Settings sections">
      <TabsTrigger value="general">General</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="billing">Billing</TabsTrigger>
      <TabsTrigger value="members">Members</TabsTrigger>
    </TabsList>
    {['general', 'billing', 'members'].map((v) => (
      <TabsContent key={v} value={v} className={panel}>{v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1)} settings.</TabsContent>
    ))}
  </UrlTabs>
  ```

- Don’t: Tabs in a small preview card rewriting the page URL — plain Tabs are enough.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-72 rounded-[var(--size-border-radius-border-radius-lg)] border border-solid border-[var(--color-border-border)] p-3">
    <p className="mb-2 font-body text-body-s font-medium text-[var(--color-text-text)]">Quick preview</p>
    <UrlTabs param="gl-preview" defaultValue="code" values={['code', 'result']}>
      <TabsList aria-label="Preview">
        <TabsTrigger value="code">Code</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="result">Result</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="code" className={panel}>{'<Button>Save</Button>'}</TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="result" className={panel}>A Save button.</TabsContent>
    </UrlTabs>
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- Same keyboard model as Tabs.
- Opening a shared URL lands on the right tab; focus stays at the top of the page, not on the tab.

## UsageBar

`import { UsageBar } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/usage-bar';`

Status: stable · Category: Status & Feedback
Docs: ./?path=/docs/status-feedback-usagebar--docs

**When to use**

- A total split into up to four parts: storage by type, bandwidth by site, seats by role.
- Showing parts against a limit (total) — used vs. free.

**When not to use**

- One value in a range → use Meter
- Task progress → use Progress
- Many parts or comparing over time → use DonutChart or BarChart

**Anatomy**

- Bar: segments sized by `value`; the remainder up to `total` stays empty.
- Legend: color, label and formatted value for each segment (`formatValue`).

**UsageBar props**

- `segments`: `UsageSegment[]`
- `formatValue?`: `((n: number) => string)`, default `(n) => String(n)`
- `showLegend?`: `boolean`, default `true`
- `total?`: `number` — Denominator for the percentages; defaults to the sum of the values.

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: A few parts with a legend — easy to compare.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80"><UsageBar total={50} formatValue={gb} segments={[{ label: 'Files', value: 18 }, { label: 'Databases', value: 9 }, { label: 'Email', value: 4 }]} /></div>
  ```

- Don’t: Eight parts on a four-color palette: colors repeat and the legend can’t be matched. Keep to four, group the rest into “Other”.

  ```tsx
  <div className="w-80">
    <UsageBar total={50} formatValue={gb} segments={['Files', 'DB', 'Email', 'Logs', 'Backups', 'Cache', 'Tmp', 'Other'].map((label, i) => ({ label, value: 6 - (i % 3) }))} />
  </div>
  ```


**Accessibility**

- The bar is one image with a text summary of all segments; the legend repeats every value as text.
- Segment colors are told apart by the legend text, not color alone.

## WheelPicker

`import { WheelPicker } from '@theya/shadcn/ui/wheel-picker';`

Status: beta · Category: Selection
Docs: ./?path=/docs/selection-wheelpicker--docs

**When to use**

- Picking one value from a short ordered scale — an interval, a duration, a size — where nudging up or down is the natural gesture.

**When not to use**

- Up to five options that should all be visible → use RadioGroup
- A long or unordered list → use Select
- Any number → use NumberField

**Anatomy**

- Wheel: the options, rolled so the chosen one sits in the middle.
- Band: the raised row that marks the chosen option.

**WheelPicker props**

- `options`: `WheelPickerOption[]`
- `defaultValue?`: `string`
- `disabled?`: `boolean`, default `false`
- `onValueChange?`: `((value: string) => void)`
- `rows?`: `"3" | "5"`, default `3` — Rows visible at once: 3 (default) or 5.
- `value?`: `string`

Also accepts the props of: HTMLAttributes.

**Do / Don’t**

- Do: An ordered scale, labelled.

  ```tsx
  <WheelPicker aria-label="Backup interval" options={INTERVALS} defaultValue="1 hour" />
  ```

- Don’t: An unordered list — there is no “next” to roll to; use Select.

  ```tsx
  <WheelPicker aria-label="Country" options={['Bulgaria', 'Germany', 'Spain'].map((label) => ({ value: label, label }))} />
  ```


**Accessibility**

- A listbox: ↑ ↓ move one option, Page Up / Page Down a screen, Home / End to the ends.
- Always give it a name (aria-label or aria-labelledby).
- With reduced motion the wheel jumps to the option instead of rolling.
